# @automagik/bots-dsh

Omni for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (dsh): a team of long-lived Bots that talk to you, to each other and in group chats, with Omni as the Main Bot. With the Omni channels plugin, Omni also operates your Omni channels, chats and automations inside dsh; with the Omni canvas plugin, it shows what it found as live views in the chat (see [Three plugins](#three-plugins)). It is built on [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot) (Apache-2.0, see `VENDORED.md`).

> Labs release. Features, tools and the saved data format can still change.

Tested with dsh `0.2.1-rc.4` (Web) on Linux.

**Your own dsh stays yours.** Installed into an existing dsh, the team keeps its files in `$AUTOMAGIK_HOME/bots` (`~/.automagik/bots`), keeps the key of the Omni it is linked to in its own file there, uses its own route (`/api/omni-ui`), plugin id (`omni-ui`) and browser-storage prefix (`omni-ui:`), overrides no other plugin's configuration, and checks for no updates. It can run beside upstream DS Bot.

## Three plugins

Omni for dsh is three packages. This one is the team; the other two sit on it and add Omni's own parts. Install all three to have everything; the team works alone.

| Package | Folder | Row id | What it adds |
|---|---|---|---|
| `@automagik/bots-dsh` (this one) | `apps/bots-dsh` | `omni-ui` | The Bot team and its surface: Bots, group chats, settings, themes, interface copy, memory, secrets, usage, scheduled tasks, the Bot browser, updates, diagnostics, the `POST /api/omni-ui` route, and the `web-search` plugin |
| `@automagik/omni-channels-dsh` | [`apps/omni-channels-dsh` in Omni](https://github.com/automagik-dev/omni/tree/dev/apps/omni-channels-dsh#readme) | `omni-channels` | The link to an Omni (pairing, `omni.json`), the Channels page and chats, Omni's tools for the platform (and the shell and file tools a Main Bot loses for them), the events Omni listens to, automations and their board, Omni's operator rules, and the onboarding step Connect Omni (`omni-connect`) |
| `@automagik/omni-canvas-dsh` | [`apps/omni-canvas-dsh` in Omni](https://github.com/automagik-dev/omni/tree/dev/apps/omni-canvas-dsh#readme) | `omni-canvas` | `show_canvas`, the canvas check, the canvas language in Omni's rules, and the renderer that draws canvases in the chat (OpenUI and zod live only here) |

How they fit:

- **Host**: this plugin provides its runtime as the `omniTeam` service. The channels plugin injects it, installs its modules on a runtime whose prototype is the team's, and provides that one as `omniChannels`; the canvas plugin injects both and sits on the channels runtime. Each plugin's tools, listeners and effects stay on its own fiber, and it adds to the team only through `rt.hooks` (`src/host/extend.js`): `endpoint(name, fn, { read })` for the `/api/omni-ui` route, `view(fn)` and `live(fn)` for the state answers, and `mainRules(fn, { order })` for a part of the Main Bot's rules, which stay inside the one `bot-identity` section. A plugin that runs a Bot kind on its own engine, not on a DSH model, owns that kind's model menu with `botModels(kind, { snapshot, pick, refresh })` (`src/host/host-models.js` has the shape): the team then never selects a DSH model for those Bots (their settings and `list_bots` name what the plugin says answers), their menu lists only the plugin's entries (each with where a message goes, the one picked and the one answering now) and levels, and only you pick; a Bot's `update_bot` with a model or level is refused. Without a registration the team answers as before. Each hook returns its disposer, so turning a plugin off takes what it added with it. Three more parts of the runtime are for other plugins:
  - `rt.resumable.register({ id, sessions, onResume })` hands the team's one restart pass (`src/host/resume.js`) the plain Sessions a plugin owns: `sessions()` names them when the pass runs, `onResume({ sessionId })` runs right before the team posts a resume to one of them (whoever found it), and the registration returns its disposer. Every resume post carries `source.resumed === true`.
  - `rt.resumesDone` is one promise per start that never rejects: `{ resumed, resent }` after the pass, `{ readOnly, resumed: [], resent: [] }` on a host that only reads the team, `{ failed, resumed, resent }` when it threw or stopped. `resumed` lists every Session the pass resumed, `resent` every Session it sent dropped messages again.
  - `rt.dshBots`: `list()` gives `[{ id, name, workDir, profile }]` (`null`: the team workspace, DSH's default preset), `createSession(botId, { title, firstMessage })` gives `{ sessionId }` in that DSH bot's folder with its preset, and `onChange(fn)` calls `fn(list)` when the list changes and returns its disposer.
- **Browser**: this plugin's `client.js` exports `omni`: the host call, the interface copy (`t`, `addStrings`), the Bot surface's registries (`toolCards`, `nav`, `badges`, `botChildren`, `headerButtons`, `sidebarTools`, `botSettings`, `onShell`, `setCanvasRenderer`, `registerComposerPack`), the running surface (`face`) and a few UI pieces (`ui`). The other plugins name `@automagik/bots-dsh/client` in `dsh.client.external`, so dsh loads this bundle first and hands them the same module instance: one dictionary, one roster, one set of registries.
- **Composer**: a Bot's composer changes with the model it runs on (`src/client/composer-packs.js`). Every Bot's chat shows the model that Bot runs on in its own model menu, which saves to that Bot alone: with thinking levels when the model has them, and on an agent over ACP (`acp-claude`, `acp-codex`) with the levels the agent offers for that model, or without any when it offers none. On a Bot whose plugin owns its model menu, it shows that menu. A group chat, where each member runs on its own model, and a Bot still waiting for its model show none. The plan cell and the activity and usage docks stay Omni's in every pack. Other plugins add a pack with `omni.registerComposerPack({ id, order, match(provider, target), available(env), cells: { permission, model }, hostFor })`.
- **Data**: all three keep the team's one `state.json` and its lock (automations ride it); `omni.json` is the channels plugin's, in the same folder.
- **Upgrading from one package**: a team linked to an Omni whose dsh has only this plugin shows a card in the sidebar footer that points to the plugin market for the channels plugin.

## Features

- **Long-lived Bots**: each Bot is a dsh Session in the "DS Bot" workspace, with its own name, role, instructions and model.
- **Working folders**: a Bot can work in a folder you choose instead of the team workspace, and a group chat can set one folder for all its members there. Pick it in the Bot's settings or details panel or in the group's settings, or ask a Bot (`update_bot`, `update_group`). After a change, the chat goes on in a fresh part that starts in the new folder. When a Bot sets a folder outside the team workspace, or adds a Bot to a group that works in one, it asks for your approval if those Bots can only write in their folder. Folders that hold dsh data (`$DSH_HOME`, the team's data) are refused. The team workspace itself moves in Settings > General > Locations; Bots and groups that work there go on in a fresh part in the new folder, and the old folder keeps its files.
- **Permission presets**: each Bot runs with its own dsh permission preset (Read only, Workspace or Full access), set in its details panel. A group chat can run all its members with one preset there, in place of their own: turn on **Same for every member** under Permissions in the group's settings. A new Bot starts with the team default, set under Permissions in Settings > Bots. While DSH's experimental Auto review plugin is on, **Auto review** is a preset too, marked Experimental and confirmed once when picked. Where Auto cannot hold (the plugin is off, or DSH refuses it), the Bot or group runs as Workspace and says so; a chat whose Session was left on Auto opens again once Auto review is back on. Only you set permissions; Bots cannot change them.
- **Bots work together**: `message_bot` sends a message to another Bot, `create_bot`, `update_bot` and `delete_bot` add, set up and remove Bots (including a profile photo from a local image file or a data URL), and `ask_user` asks you a question without blocking the other Bots. `show_view` draws a card in a Bot's own chat — text, metrics, tables, progress, choices, confirmations and short forms; an interactive card waits for your answer.
- **Group chats**: members speak one at a time, and each one reads the latest messages first. A message can `@Name` a member to pass the turn on; type `@` to pick one from a list. **+ → Reference a chat** adds another Bot's chat to a message as context, and in a group the members who answer get it. A member with nothing new to add stays quiet (`[PASS]`). Each member has its own hidden Session per group, so a group never reads a Bot's private chat.
- **Roles and permissions**:

  | Who | Can do |
  |---|---|
  | You | Everything |
  | Main Bot (there can be more than one) | Manage every group; change and delete Bots |
  | Group admin | Manage its own group only (name, notice, members, reply mode) |
  | Member | Speak in the group, `@` another member, and post into its groups from outside them |

- **Scheduled tasks and restricted Bots**: a Bot with a deny list cannot create or
  edit a scheduled task, because a `new` or `new_once` target opens a Session no deny
  layer binds; the tasks it already armed are paused and their record stays. A
  delivery no team lineage can bind is refused while such a task cannot be paused;
  when the pause lands, dsh is asked to drive again and the refused delivery goes
  through. A reminder due during the boot window, before the team has loaded, is
  refused the same way and lands once the team loads.
- **Long chats stay inside the model's window**: dsh's own compaction never runs on a Bot's Session. When a turn ends past the check line (a share of the model's context window), a small separate model call, the context steward, reads the latest messages of the chat and decides once. If the work is still under way, the chat is condensed in place into a checkpoint: a handoff summary plus your recent messages word for word. If the work has reached a stopping point, the Bot writes a handoff note and continues in a new part. Either way you still see one chat, with no marker. Earlier parts and condensed messages stay searchable in a full-text index (`node:sqlite` FTS5) through `read_own_chat`. These side calls (steward, note, checkpoint) never go to an agent over ACP (Claude Code, Codex): they run on the team's background model, and a Bot with no model that answers beside its agent skips them, says so once in the log, and past the hard line continues in a new part that carries its latest messages word for word, without a model call. Switching a Bot from an agent to an API model measures the chat against that model's own switch threshold (computed as DSH's compaction does) before DSH checks it: below it nothing happens; above it, the chat is condensed into a checkpoint only when you picked a background model in Settings and the chat fits that model (it is the one charged), and otherwise the Bot continues in a new part with the latest messages that fit, no note and no model call. The part it leaves is archived only once the new part's first answer comes from the chosen model; if that first call fails, the Bot goes back to the part it left. No message is deleted either way.
- **Memory**: each Bot keeps notes across all its conversations, each group chat keeps its own for its members, and the team shares one more. See [Memory](#memory).
- **Web search**: see [Web search](#web-search).
- **Bot browser**: each Bot drives a browser of its own: it opens pages, clicks, types, uploads and downloads. Posting, uploading, downloading and deleting ask you first, and payments always come back to you. See [Bot browser](#bot-browser).
- **Side chat**: ask a Bot about its work while it runs, in the side panel (`/side`, or `/btw` as before), without stopping its turn or adding to its chat. Nothing runs to answer.
- **Images**: for a model that cannot read images, a vision model first turns the image into text.
- **Secrets**: a Bot asks for an API key or token with a card in its own chat and never sees the value. See [Secrets](#secrets).
- **Usage**: Settings → Usage shows token usage by time (24 hours to 12 months, or days picked on a calendar), by Bot and by model, with a page for each Bot and each model. Calls that a Session logs are read from the logs, so older chats count too. Calls that leave no log (checkpoints, handoff notes, the steward, image readings, dsh titles and compaction) are counted while they stream, from the time the plugin runs. Legacy aggregates can omit provider fields; they do not claim a cross-provider cache percentage. Tokens only, no cost.
- **Official right sidebar**: every Bot chat can open Live as a tab in DSH's own pane, rather than a second fixed rail. DSH owns its collapse, focus, docking and narrow-screen behavior. Existing Browser, side-chat and plugin routes remain available.
- **Advanced Bot**: Bot Settings has a per-Bot switch, initially off and saved across parts and restarts. It reveals supported native session controls, Context and Stats without changing identity, permissions, model access or context policy. Models and permissions remain managed by the canonical Bot controls. Ordinary DSH keeps its native conversation surface.
- **Advanced Context**: shows current part/checkpoint boundaries, measured or estimated usage and effective usable/check/hard windows. Per-Bot check threshold and recent-message carry budget override host defaults (80% and 16,384 tokens); the 95% hard safety threshold is protected and effective carry is additionally capped by the check line. **Checkpoint now** requires an idle, loaded own-chat Session and condenses that same Session through Bot maintenance; stale, running, cancelled or read-only requests fail rather than bypass the native guard. **Start new part** is separate, confirmed and carries nothing from the old part. Native manual Bot compaction remains unavailable, with an explanation. Automatic memory review has separate own-chat controls/status and no guaranteed ordering with compaction; a host-wide off setting cannot be overridden.
- **Advanced Stats**: read-only last-request, last-turn, current-Session and Bot-total scopes show input/output/cache read/cache write, logical calls, recorded attempts and retries where reported. Session drilldown is limited to that Bot's own-chat parts; Bot totals partition group, task/child and tagged memory/steward/checkpoint/handoff overhead without adding overlapping scopes together. Unlinked overhead is not guessed into a request or turn. Missing is **Unknown**, not zero; legacy provenance cannot be reconstructed. Cache ratios are token-weighted within compatible, explicitly identified provider normalization, with their prompt-token denominator displayed; providers are never averaged together. Refresh may update the derived ledger but never runs a model or changes a Session. Partial history is labeled. No cost, timing, task-success or native-DSH effectiveness comparison is inferred.
- **DSH bots**: New… → New DSH bot creates a native DSH identity with a name, project folder and preset, and immediately adds team membership: the native DSH conversation UI and tooling stay available alongside roster, messages, groups and browser access. It has the same final shape as adopting an existing DSH bot, with one sidebar row and a retained original registration. Membership failure fails creation and cleans up the new registration and Session. If archival or required persistence is unavailable, a durable pending-creation registration retains ownership and tool restrictions, stays hidden from both rosters, and retries cleanup on the next load (including restart). The error reports pending cleanup; it never reports successful standalone creation. Cleanup waits for an operation-bound terminal receipt in `agent-creations/<UUID>.json`, published atomically by the allocation's producer only after native creation settles—even if that producer lost the team lock or was disposed. This receipt contains only operation and Session IDs plus outcome, grants no team-write or archival authority, and is removed after durable membership or cleanup. Missing/invalid receipts (including a hard kill before publication or receipt persistence failure) retain hidden pending ownership rather than guessing that an absent Session cannot appear later; back up `agent-creations/` with the team file while creation is pending. Cleanup is claimed durably before archival so an old producer cannot re-adopt an archived Session. DSH archival and the team file are not atomic: a failed post-archive save can temporarily retain a pending reference to an archived Session, which idempotent retry removes. For compatibility, legacy `add-agent` callers without `teamMember: true` and `rt.dshBots` keep the standalone DSH registration/session contract (no team tools); the UI explicitly opts into membership. A Bot's one-off work (`start_task`) runs under that Bot and reports back when its first turn ends.
- **Adopting a DSH bot**: **Adopt as Bot** adds team membership without replacing the DSH identity, native conversation surface, preset, avatar or capabilities. The newest Session becomes its team chat and earlier Sessions remain readable parts; nothing is renamed or recreated. `list_bots`, messages, groups, capabilities and tasks become available. Fresh parts, group member Sessions and tasks inherit its preset. The original DSH registration stays saved with an `adoptedBotId` reference, but is hidden from the standalone roster to avoid duplicate rows.
  - **Rollback**: the local `POST /api/omni-ui` endpoint `agent-bot-rollback`, payload `{ "agentId": "<original DSH id>" }`, removes only the added membership and restores the original registration and team-tool restrictions. It does not archive Sessions. Remove Main Bot/group roles first; rollback refuses new parts or tasks rather than discarding new team history. Ordinary Bot deletion refuses adopted registrations; roll back first. A failed adoption/rollback save restores the pre-operation records. This cannot reconstruct identities already removed by the older destructive implementation: those require the original registration from a backup and verified preset/avatar information; no identity is inferred from a Bot's name.
- **Make it yours**: name, role, instructions, model and look (20 characters and 12 colors, or a photo from the ones you added) for each Bot. An adopted DSH identity wears DSH's blue whale until it has a look of its own; ordinary Bots retain their identity-derived defaults and a Genie keeps its genie-clay pet; a theme, an accent color and an avatar animation level (quiet, normal or lively) for the team. A pinned Bot or group chat shows a small pushpin in the sidebar. Settings has these pages: General (look), Bots (Main Bots and each Bot's settings), Group chats (each group's settings), Connectors, Capabilities, Scheduled tasks, Usage, Secrets, Feedback and About DS Bot (versions, updates and links).

## Install

The [project page](../../README.md#install) has the full steps for dsh Desktop and dsh Web. In short:

- dsh Desktop: Settings → Plugins → add a `.tgz` of this package (`npm pack` in this folder).
- Command line: `dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/automagik-bots-dsh-<version>.tgz`.
- Or skip dsh setup entirely: the Automagik desktop app ([`apps/desktop`](../desktop/README.md), `omni desktop` from Omni's CLI) ships dsh with this plugin on a home of its own.

To work on the plugins from a checkout, add them to a dsh profile as linked dependencies and bundles (the channels and canvas plugins are optional):

```json
{
  "dependencies": {
    "@automagik/bots-dsh": "link:/path/to/apps/bots-dsh",
    "@automagik/omni-channels-dsh": "link:/path/to/omni/apps/omni-channels-dsh",
    "@automagik/omni-canvas-dsh": "link:/path/to/omni/apps/omni-canvas-dsh"
  },
  "dsh": { "profile": { "bundles": ["@deepseek-ai/dsh-base", "@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app", "@automagik/bots-dsh", "@automagik/omni-channels-dsh", "@automagik/omni-canvas-dsh"] } }
}
```

Run `pnpm install` in the profile folder, then start dsh from the deepseek-harness repository:

```sh
pnpm -s dsh --profile web --no-open
```

The first time the team opens, the plugin creates a Main Bot called Omni.

**Upgrading from the `ds-bot` builds of the Omni UI**: earlier builds were named `ds-bot` with the plugin id `bot` and kept the team in `~/.dsh/bot`. Replace `ds-bot` with `@automagik/bots-dsh` in the profile, and set `importHome: ~/.dsh/bot` once (see [Configuration](#configuration)) to copy that team into `~/.omni/ui`; the old folder is left as it was. Browser settings saved under `ds-bot:` are not carried over, because DS Bot uses the same names.

## Connect to an Omni

This needs the Omni channels plugin. On the Channels page, type the address of an Omni (for example `omni.example.com`) and choose **Get a code**. Omni answers with a short code and the WhatsApp number of its pairing channel; send the code to yourself from that WhatsApp ("Message yourself"; **Open WhatsApp** or the QR opens the chat with the code typed). The page goes live as soon as the code arrives. The Omni must have pairing turned on (`OMNI_PAIRING_ENABLED=true` and a pairing instance on the server).

The key Omni mints is saved in `~/.automagik/bots/omni.json` (readable by you only), with the scopes the server gives paired keys and an expiry; it never reaches the browser. Delete that file to disconnect; revoke the key in Omni to cut it off from the server side. A profile can still name an Omni the older way, with `omni.url` in this plugin's config (or the channels plugin's) and the `OMNI_API_KEY` credential in dsh's store; a saved link wins over both.

## Configuration

Options go in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`, under the `omni-ui` entry. All of them are optional.

```yaml
- id: omni-ui
  name: '@automagik/bots-dsh'
  config:
    workspace: /path/to/workspace   # where the Bots work; default <home>/workspace
    home: /path/to/team-data       # where the team is saved; default $AUTOMAGIK_BOTS_HOME, else $AUTOMAGIK_HOME/bots (~/.automagik/bots)
    importHome: ~/.dsh/bot          # copy a team saved there into home once, when home has none
    checkRatio: 0.8                 # share of the model's usable window where the steward decides
    browser: true                   # force the browser panel and read_browser on or off; default both in dsh Desktop, the panel alone in the Automagik app
    browserPlugin: refs             # the browser each Bot drives: refs (default), script or task; false turns it off
    browserExecutablePath: /usr/bin/google-chrome   # the browser it launches; default the first Chrome, Edge, Chromium or Brave found
    browserHeadless: false          # default: headless only on Linux without a display
    memory: true                    # false turns memory off: no memory tools, section or panel
    memoryReview: true              # false leaves memory to the Bots' own remember calls
    fallback: true                  # false lets a failed model end the turn instead of moving it to the fallback
    fallbackModel: deepseek-official/deepseek-flash   # where a failed turn moves; default the team's default model
    diagnosticsFile: false          # keep the error log in memory only; default <home>/logs/diagnostics.jsonl
    updateCheck: false              # the package's own patch sets false: nothing is checked or installed
    updateRegistry: https://registry.example/   # ask only this npm registry for updates
    github: false                   # hide the GitHub connector; default shown in Connectors
    appManifest:                    # the web app's name; default Automagik, false keeps DSH's own
      name: Automagik
      short_name: Automagik
      theme_color: '#1a1a2e'        # optional, a #hex color (also background_color)
      icon: /absolute/path/icon.svg # optional, an .svg or .png; default the Automagik app icon
```

**The web app's name**: DSH's page calls itself "DeepSeek Harness", in its manifest (what a browser shows when you install the page as an app) and in its `<title>`. With this plugin it is "Automagik": the plugin serves `/manifest.webmanifest` (`application/manifest+json`, DSH's own fields with these names) ahead of DSH's static file, the icon at `/omni-ui/app-icon.png` (or `.svg`), and puts `name` in the page's `<title>`. The icon is the Automagik app icon (`apps/desktop/assets/icon.png`) at 512 px. `appManifest` names the app otherwise; `appManifest: false` keeps DSH's name and icon. A value it can't use (no `name` or `short_name`, a color that isn't `#hex`, an icon that isn't an absolute `.svg` or `.png` path it can read) is refused with a line in the diagnostics, and the page stays "Automagik".

**Updates**: when a window opens, DS Bot asks where it was installed from for a newer release: the npm registry (the one the DSH plugin manager installs from, then its fallbacks), or the latest GitHub release for a `github:…#vX.Y.Z` install. A newer version shows a cloud button at the top right of the sidebar; **Update** reinstalls DS Bot through the DSH plugin manager, and the new version runs from the next DSH start. A linked or local checkout is never offered an update. Settings → About DS Bot shows the same state, with **Check for updates** to ask again at once.

The same card can carry DSH itself: a DS Bot release may name the DSH release it was verified against (`dsBot.verifiedDsh` in its `package.json`), and only that version is offered — running something newer is a downgrade offer too. A release that names no version offers no DSH update. A DSH installed from npm is swapped by `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>`. DSH Desktop installs the newest release its own updater finds, so the card shows DSH there only when that release is the verified one, and **Open updates** opens the app's update panel. A release may raise the floor with `dsBot.minBot`: until the bot itself is that new, the DSH row waits.

## Models

Model providers are set up with dsh's `llm-pi-ai` plugin in `cordis.patch.yml`. Every Bot runs on one model of its own, from the models DSH serves. A new team's first Main Bot has none, and holds its greeting until it has one. With `@automagik/welcome-dsh`, finishing Connect AI with an AI on gives it (and the Omni Bot) the team's default model, and the greeting goes out then. Otherwise its chat offers that model with one press to start and a "change" link to the model menu; with no model that can run, the card offers ways to set one up. The team's default model is DSH's default model when it is served and its provider has its key, else the first model that can run (a provider's `default` alias after the models it names). While a chat holds only the greeting, one line under it names the model and its provider, with "change". Of the Claude models pi-ai serves on `anthropic`, the menus offer each family's newest (Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, Fable); the older versions and dated snapshots stay served, so a Bot already on one keeps it and its menu still shows it. The Create Bot form starts on the DSH default model. The Bot's details panel and settings (or a Main Bot's `update_bot`) change it; a Bot whose model is no longer served shows the card again. A team saved by an older version keeps the model each Bot last ran on.

**Background model**: the jobs that run beside the chats use one model of the team's, never the Bot's agent: memory review and the memory panel, and, for a chat on an agent over ACP (`acp-claude`, `acp-codex`), the steward's call and the part's note and checkpoint. An agent answers only in its own chat, so it cannot take those. Other chats keep their own model for these, so the provider serves their prefix from cache. The model is the team's pick in Settings → Bots → Background jobs (`prefs.backgroundModel`, any model DSH serves that is not an agent), else DSH's default model (DeepSeek, unless the person chose another there) when it can run, else the first account connected here. A memory call that fails on it is tried once more on the Bot's own model, when that one is not an agent. DSH's own session titles and compaction summaries pick their model in DSH's config (`session-title-llm`'s `provider` and `model`, `compaction-basic`'s `summarizationProvider` and `summarizationModel`); those fields are not live settings, so this setting does not reach them.

**Claude on ACP**: Claude Code came back through `@automagik/acp-dsh`. Once per team, a Bot that ran
on the retired Claude Code plugin and is still on the pi-ai Claude model it was moved to takes
`acp-claude` on the same family (`opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`), keeping its Session and history. It
moves only when the ACP plugin's `dshTools` bridge is on (its absent default is on for Claude), a
live bridge probe on this machine passes (cached per adapter version, retried after ten minutes or
the next start), its adapter is installed, its CLI is signed in, and its route lists that model; a
Bot the person has changed since, or whose model the route does not list, stays where it is. The
sign-in is the CLI's own answer, asked again on every pass: an installed-but-signed-out Claude moves
nothing, and after signing in the Bots move on the next pass (a settings or adapter change) or the
next DSH start, with no separate action. The move records the model and thinking level the Bot had
and carries that level onto the agent's own effort setting where the agent offers it, by the same
id or a unique display name: Claude Code's levels are low, medium, high, xhigh and max, an

# Português (`@automagik/locale-pt-br-dsh`)

Brazilian Portuguese for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH). DSH 0.2.2 ships Portuguese itself, as **Português** (`pt`); this client plugin adds the part DSH does not carry — the Bot team's own `omni-ui` strings — under that same entry. It adds no language: Settings › General › Language keeps exactly **one** Portuguese row, DSH's.

Supported runtime: **DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 or later** (`engines.dsh` is `>=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0-0`). Earlier DSH releases have no `pt` to register under, and DSH refuses the install there.

## One Portuguese entry

The pack used to add its own **Português (Brasil)** entry with a corrected copy of four DSH namespaces (date order, thousands separator, the plan hint and several mistranslations). A pack cannot override a namespace DSH already registers for `pt` — the second registration throws (`locale namespace "<ns>" already has locale "pt"`) — so those corrections required a second language, and therefore a second Portuguese row in the picker.

That row is gone. The Language list shows DSH's **Português** alone, and DSH's `pt` copy serves the DSH screens. The pack's own strings are the Bot team's, and they belong to the Bot team's namespace: DSH does not have `omni-ui`.

## What it carries

| Namespace | Keys | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `omni-ui` | all 1,450 | The Bot team's namespace (`@automagik/bots-dsh`), which DSH does not have; registered under `pt` |

`omni-ui` holds all 1,450 Bot team keys. A few keep their English text on purpose: brand and product names (`Omni`, `DSH`, `Automagik`, `DeepSeek`, `Claude`, `Codex`, `ChatGPT`, `OpenAI`, `Anthropic`, `Google`, `GitHub`, `Namastex`, `Kimi`, `MCP`, `API`), code-like strings (`cookies.txt, JSON, storageState`, `MEMORY.md`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `~/.codex/pets`, `#rrggbb`, `@Name`, `/side`, `/feedback`), words Brazilian Portuguese uses unchanged (`Chat`, `Bots`, `Plugins`, `Admin`, `Site`, `Terminal`, `Endpoint`, `Feedback`, `Skill`, `status`, `tokens`, `Pets`), and strings that are only a value (`{count}`, `{n}h`, `1 item`). `test/coverage.test.js` requires every Bot key to have an entry and at least 95% of them to differ from the English text.

A plugin can add its own words to `omni-ui` through the Bot team's `addStrings` (Unfold session's model-menu messages, `apps/unfold-session-dsh/src/client/strings.js`); `scripts/copy-check.mjs` lists those modules in `OMNI_PLUGIN_STRINGS`, so their keys are checked and covered like the Bot team's. The Bot team words a host message with any language pack's entry for it.

The welcome (`@automagik/welcome-dsh`) keeps its own copy in its `welcome.team` namespace and registers it under DSH's `pt` as well, so the onboarding reads in Portuguese with this pack installed.

## Upgrading from the old pack, and removing it

A profile that installed the pack before 0.2.2 has an older copy that registered a **pt-BR** language and its dictionaries. DSH replaces a plugin in place: when it loads this version it unloads the old one first, whose language and dictionary effects are disposed with it. This client adds no language at all, so it cannot leave a second Portuguese row behind; while the old copy is still mounted, it does not register over the dictionary the old copy holds (it waits for that copy's disposer), so nothing throws on a duplicate locale registration.

A language choice saved as `pt-BR` under the old pack is an exact id to DSH's locale runtime, and DSH's entry is `pt`. On load the pack rewrites the stored choice through the runtime's only preference write (`setLocale`), before the choice is read, so a team that picked **Português (Brasil)** opens in Portuguese instead of falling back to English. A browser or home that never picked a language is left alone.

To stop shipping the Bot team's strings, remove the plugin: `dsh plugin --profile <profile> remove @automagik/locale-pt-br-dsh` (or Settings › Plugins, then the Plugins page, which manages what the list only shows). DSH's own **Português** entry and everything DSH translates stay; only `omni-ui` falls back to its English text, and a saved `pt` choice keeps resolving.

## Install

1. Add the Automagik market to DSH's plugin market ([marketplace/README.md](../../marketplace/README.md) has the URL).
2. Install **Português (Brasil)** — the market title of this pack. If DSH asks for a restart, restart it.
3. Pick **Português** in Settings › General › Language (DSH's entry), or open DSH in a browser set to Portuguese.

The client declares `inject: ['locale']` and loads in DSH's first boot phase (`immediately`). The host half does nothing. It needs no settings.

## Develop

```sh
bun run harness      # the pinned DSH release the tests and the linter run against
bun run build        # client.js from src/client; commit it with the sources
bun run test         # on Node: a fake locale service, then DSH's own LocaleRuntime
bun run lint
node scripts/copy-check.mjs     # every pt-BR text against its English text and the copy rules
```

`src/client/locales/pt-BR/omni-ui.json` is keyed by the Bot team's English text. The copy check rejects a key the Bot team no longer has and every `{placeholder}` that does not match its English text. Its rules: Brazilian Portuguese, gender-neutral for the person, no article before Unfold, "clique" for a click, and "ambiente isolado" for a sandbox.

# Automagik

Automagik's plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), and the Automagik desktop app that runs them.

| Folder | Package | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| [`apps/bots-dsh`](apps/bots-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/bots-dsh` | The Bot team: long-lived Bots, group chats, memory, settings, scheduled tasks, the Bot browser. Omni's and Genie's plugins build on it. |
| [`apps/welcome-dsh`](apps/welcome-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/welcome-dsh` | The welcome: the octopus, the team step, and Connect AI through DSH's own sign-ins. |
| [`apps/acp-dsh`](apps/acp-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/acp-dsh` | Agents other than DSH's own, over ACP (Agent Client Protocol), as DSH models: the agent's tool calls show as DSH tool cards and ask through DSH's approval dialog (RFC 0003). |
| [`apps/locale-pt-br-dsh`](apps/locale-pt-br-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/locale-pt-br-dsh` | Português: the Bot team's Brazilian Portuguese under DSH's own Portuguese entry. Adds no language of its own, so Settings › General › Language keeps one Portuguese row; a pt-BR choice saved by an older pack moves to DSH's pt. |
| [`apps/desktop`](apps/desktop/README.md) | (the app) | The Automagik desktop app: DSH of its own with the Bot team, the welcome and Omni's channels and canvases. `omni desktop` opens it with Omni preloaded, `genie desktop` with Genie. |

Omni's own plugins (its channels and canvases) live with Omni, in [automagik-dev/omni](https://github.com/automagik-dev/omni) (`apps/omni-channels-dsh`, `apps/omni-canvas-dsh`), and carry Omni's version.

## Install

- **The desktop app**: download it from [Releases](https://github.com/automagik-dev/automagik/releases/latest), or run `omni desktop`. See [apps/desktop](apps/desktop/README.md).
- **Into your own DSH**: add the Automagik market to DSH's plugin market and install from there:

  ```
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/automagik-dev/dsh-marketplace/main/index.json
  ```

  Every Omni also serves a market at `https://<your-omni>/api/market/index.json` with the release of these plugins it was tested with.

Nothing here is published to npm. The plugins install as git sources pinned to a release commit, or from the tarballs each release carries (`plugins.json` lists their integrity).

## History

`@automagik/bots-dsh` and `@automagik/welcome-dsh` were `@automagik/omni-dsh` and `@automagik/omni-ai-dsh` in automagik-dev/omni (`apps/omni-ui-dsh`, `apps/omni-ai-dsh`), and the desktop app was automagik-dev/omni-desktop. They moved here with their history. What did not change with the names: plugin ids (`omni-ui`, `omni-ai`), routes and browser-storage prefixes. From 3.12 the team's home is Automagik's own (`~/.automagik/bots`, or `~/.automagik/desktop/bots` in the app), and the app's identity is Automagik's (`ai.namastex.automagik`): an app from 3.11.x or before is installed afresh, not updated.

- The Bot team's client bundle also answers to its former name, so channels and canvas plugins built before the rename keep working on it.
- In your own DSH: install `@automagik/bots-dsh` from the market. With both installed, the newer one runs (they share the plugin id); remove `@automagik/omni-dsh` when you like. A settings row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` that names `@automagik/omni-dsh` needs its `name:` changed to `@automagik/bots-dsh` to keep applying.

## Versions and releases

One version for the whole repository, `3.N` (semver `3.N.0`, N one above the last release: `scripts/version.ts`), above the 2.x builds omni-desktop released. Every merge into dev is a release: `release.yml` tags `v<version>`, publishes the plugin tarballs and `plugins.json`, builds the desktop app into the same release (`desktop-build.yml`), lists the release in [`marketplace/automagik.json`](marketplace/automagik.json), and moves `main` to it. `follow-omni.yml` moves the desktop app to each newer Omni release and cuts a release with it.

| Branch | What |
|---|---|
| `dev` | Integration: pull requests land here; releases are cut from it |
| `main` | The latest release, moved by `release.yml` only |

## Develop

Bun for the repository's own tooling; the plugins run on Node, as DSH does (`node --test`, esbuild), with Bun installing them; the desktop app uses npm for Electron.

```sh
bun install && bun run check                    # versions, release tooling, market index
cd apps/bots-dsh && bun install && bun run harness && bun run test
cd apps/welcome-dsh && bun install && bun run harness && bun run test
cd apps/desktop && npm ci && npm test
node scripts/boot-check.mjs                     # boot the plugins with Omni's in headless Chromium
```

# Omni AI for DSH

`@automagik/welcome-dsh` is the first thing a DeepSeek Harness (DSH) shows with Omni
installed: the Omni octopus says hello, then helps you connect an AI. It adds no provider
code. Every sign-in it offers is one DSH 0.2.1-rc.4 already ships, and every route it
writes goes through DSH's own settings and credential store.

## What it does

Two steps on DSH's `settings.onboarding` slot, shown once each on a fresh start (a new
chat with nothing in it), ahead of DSH's own steps:

| Step | Order | What it shows |
|---|---|---|
| `omni-welcome` | −300 | The octopus, a typewriter speech bubble and a glitch, on a starfield. |
| `omni-connect-ai` | −200 | Connect AI: one switch per AI, Continue and Skip. |

The Omni channels plugin (`@automagik/omni-channels-dsh`) adds `omni-connect` (−250) between them when it
is installed. DSH's `welcome-notice` (−100) and `deepseek-official` (0) follow.

Each step draws its own modal and makes `#root` inert while it shows. When you finish or
skip a step, the plugin records it in its own settings entry, `omni-ai`, in three live
fields (`welcomeDone`, `connectAiDone`, `connectOmniSkipped`), so the step does not come
back after a restart. A step whose flag is already set completes without showing.

Connect AI is a list of switches, and several can be on. What this computer already has
comes first, under **Found on this computer**: a key in DSH's store
or in the environment, a sign-in DSH already holds, Claude Code or Codex signed in, a
CLIProxyAPI route, Ollama answering on `127.0.0.1:11434`. **Add another** shows four more, then the rest on demand. Continue
needs one AI really on; Skip finishes the step either way.

Flipping a switch on turns on what is set up, or opens its setup in the row: a key field,
the provider's own sign-in in DSH, or, for a provider that takes both (Grok), a choice of the
sign-in or a key. Claude and ChatGPT sign in only through their CLIs (Claude Code, Codex; see
below): their setup offers the CLI's **Sign in**, and for Claude an Anthropic API key. Off
stops using an AI and keeps its key, sign-in or account:

| Kind | On | Off |
|---|---|---|
| Key | writes the pi-ai route that names the key | removes the route; the key stays |
| Sign-in | the route is written once the sign-in succeeds; with no sign-in, a key the row also takes | removes the route; the sign-in and the key stay |
| Claude, ChatGPT | signed in to the CLI: turns on acp-dsh's `claude` or `codex` switch; else (Claude) the Anthropic key's route | turns that switch off, for every Bot on that agent, and removes the key's route; the CLI's sign-in and the key stay |
| CLIProxyAPI | the gateway form writes its route | removes the route; the key stays |
| Ollama | lists its models into a local OpenAI-compatible route | removes the route |
| dsh-subscriptions | shows the vendor's models again | hides them in that plugin's picker settings; the account stays |

DeepSeek is DSH's own route: its row turns on with a key or a DeepSeek account, and its key
is removed in Settings → Models. Every other provider DSH knows stays one link away, in
Settings → Models.

Continue gives the companion and the Omni Bot their model. Both are made without one, so
joining the team sends nothing anywhere; once Connect AI finishes with an AI on, each gets
the team's default model and its held greeting goes out, without a further click. With no
model that can run (Skip, or only a provider that still needs its key), they keep waiting
and their chats offer the ways to set one up.

### The team step and the preload

The team step (`omni-team`) asks who joins the companion's team: Omni and Genie, each a card
with what it starts with. Omni's card starts asleep; its power button installs what a plain
DSH lacks (below), then looks for an Omni to connect. Genie has no DSH plugin yet, and
says so; it can still be added to the team.

The Automagik desktop app passes the product it was opened for (`omni desktop` →
`--preload=omni`, `genie desktop` → `--preload=genie`) to DSH as `AUTOMAGIK_PRELOAD`, which
`state` reports as `preload` (`src/host/preload.js`; anything but `omni`, `genie` or
`unfold` is none). That card comes first and starts chosen: Omni's powers on by itself, through the
same box and steps as a press, and Remove still sends it back to sleep; Genie's starts on
the team. The other card stays to add, then or later. Without a preload Omni comes first
and nothing is chosen.

Unfold's card is shown only in Unfold's own Automagik instance. Anywhere else the team step has
no Unfold card and `unfold-plugin-install` is refused, so the welcome installs no `unfold-*`
plugin. Unfold's own Automagik instance starts DSH with `AUTOMAGIK_HOST=unfold` or
`AUTOMAGIK_PRELOAD=unfold` (either one names it: `src/host/host.js`, the same rule as the Bot
team's and the Unfold Bot's). There Unfold's card comes first and is on the team from the start,
because the Unfold Bot is the instance's Main Bot, so the companion step is done (Unfold leads)
and no other Bot is made. `state` reports it as `host`, and Omni and Genie come with the
instance: Omni's card offers no new Omni of its own, and Genie's names the command line the
instance brought instead of the line that installs one.

### The power shortcut in the Bot team's sidebar

Where the Bot team runs, the welcome puts a power button in its sidebar, between the update
cloud and Search (and in the collapsed rail), through the Bot team's `sidebarTools`
registry: `@automagik/bots-dsh/client` is in `dsh.client.external` and in the build's
`external`, and is looked up only when the plugin applies, so a DSH without the Bot team
gets no button and no error. Its card has a row per product, in the team step's order
(Unfold only in its own instance, read-only), each led by the Bot team's own mark for that
product (its `BotMark`) and offering the one thing to do next: power it on or off, install
it (with a line on what that does, then its step and place, "Installing Genie · 2 of 3 ·
Bot team", from the host's install job), try again with the reason, add the Omni Bot back,
open Plugins, or choose where Omni lives (the Bot itself sits in the sidebar, so a row does
not open it). Powering off is the
team step's own (`powerOff`): it stops a run and puts the box to sleep, and undoes nothing
on the host (a linked Omni stays linked, no Bot is removed); Genie, once on the team, stays,
as on its box. Powering on runs the team step's own steps in a shared store
(`src/client/power-store.js`), so it keeps going when the card or the step closes. That store
lives in the page, so the button reads the host's `omni-plugins` and `genie-plugin` when it
mounts and each time the card opens: an install the host is running (its `install.phase` is
`installing`) that this window does not follow, after a reload or from another window, is
picked up where it is, without asking for a second install, and polled every `POLL_MS`
(900 ms) as the team step polls it, to On or to the reason with Try again. Choosing where Omni
lives, or "Open team setup", opens the team step on purpose: there Continue only closes it and
saves nothing, so the Main Bot keeps its name. Both show only when the Bot team passes the
shell's onboarding opener (`actions.openHarnessOnboarding`).

The team step follows the DSH language. Its copy is the `welcome.team` namespace
(`src/client/i18n.js`): the keys are the English text, registered in English and in Brazilian
Portuguese (`pt-BR`), and the rows the host sends are read through it too. A language pack that
adds `pt-BR` to DSH turns the step Portuguese; it registers no `welcome.team` dictionary of its
own, since DSH takes one per namespace and language. The other steps are English only.

### What the power button installs

The Bot team (`@automagik/bots-dsh`) is this repository's, at this plugin's version: from
the source this plugin came from, pointed at `apps/bots-dsh` (the same commit, or a linked
checkout), else that release's tarball. A release tarball is installed only after every
one about to be installed matches the `lane.json` on the same release, signed with a key
the plugin carries (`src/host/lane-keys.json`, a copy of `plugin-lane/keys.json`): the lane
for this version, each tarball's size, sha256 and sha512. One that does not match, or a
release without a signed lane, stops the install before anything is installed; the checked
tarballs are kept, 0600, under `<AUTOMAGIK_HOME>/welcome/tarballs`, where the profile
installs them from. A DSH that has the team under its former name,
`@automagik/omni-dsh`, has the team: it is switched on, not installed over. Omni's channels
and canvases (`@automagik/omni-channels-dsh`, `@automagik/omni-canvas-dsh`) are Omni's, at
Omni's version: they install as a git source from Omni's repository at the release
`package.json` pins under `automagik.omni`, the same one the desktop app carries
(`apps/desktop/omni.json`; `follow-omni.yml` moves both).

### One way to each AI

| AI | Through | Not offered |
|---|---|---|
| Claude | Claude Code's own sign-in (acp-dsh's `acp-claude`), or an Anthropic API key on pi-ai's `anthropic` route (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) | DSH's Claude Pro/Max sign-in (`llm-pi-ai/anthropic`) |
| ChatGPT | Codex's own sign-in (acp-dsh's `acp-codex`) | DSH's ChatGPT sign-in (`openai-codex`) as a chat route |
| Kimi | DSH's sign-in (`kimi-coding`) | dsh-subscriptions' `kimi` |
| Copilot | DSH's sign-in (`github-copilot`) | dsh-subscriptions' `copilot` |
| Grok | DSH's sign-in (`xai`), or an `XAI_API_KEY` | dsh-subscriptions' `grok` |
| DeepSeek | DSH's key or account | pi-ai's `deepseek` route |
| Ollama | a local pi-ai route | dsh-subscriptions' `ollama` |

A pi-ai route still on DSH's own sign-in for Claude or ChatGPT (`openai-codex`, or `anthropic`
naming no key while DSH holds its Claude sign-in) is a duplicate of the CLI: the row says
*Also connected through DSH sign-in*, and once the CLI can answer, turning the row on (or
**Use only this**) removes that route, but only after the Bot team (bots-dsh's `omniTeam`,
`moveSubscriptionBots`) has moved the Bots on it to the CLI's route. While any Bot (its model,
or the model a pending switch goes back to) or the team's background jobs still run on it, or
the team cannot be read, the route stays and stays listed. Only the route: the sign-in record
stays, and so does any route that names a key. `signin-start` (and the other `signin-*`
endpoints) refuse `anthropic` and `openai-codex`: nothing here starts DSH's own Claude or
ChatGPT plan sign-in. Images and the companion's drawing on a ChatGPT plan go through Codex's
own sign-in (acp-dsh's `generateImage`); an `openai-codex` record an earlier version stored is
still read as a last resort, and an OpenAI API key draws as before. dsh-subscriptions no
longer ships `claude` or `codex` (0.7.21-omni.1), so nothing stands for them.

The route earlier versions added for DSH's Claude sign-in did not retry a 429 (`retryPolicy`
without `RATE_LIMIT`). A route on an API key keeps DSH's default retries, also one such a
sign-in made before the key: saving the key drops the sign-in's policy (a policy set by hand
stays).

dsh-subscriptions keeps the vendors nothing else reaches (Cursor, Kiro, GLM, Qwen,
Perplexity, JetBrains, Cody, Replit and the rest). When an AI is turned on, the other ways
it is connected stop showing: their models are hidden, and no account or stored sign-in is
deleted. A row says when its AI is also
connected another way.

### Claude Code and Codex

With [`@automagik/acp-dsh`](../acp-dsh) in the DSH, Connect AI's Claude and ChatGPT rows are
these CLIs, and DSH's Settings (and the Bot team's) have a **Claude Code and Codex** page with
a row for each agent. Connect AI has no section of its own for them. Without acp-dsh, Claude
takes only its API key, ChatGPT is not offered a sign-in, and the Settings page says the ACP
agents plugin is not running. Each Settings row says (and a Connect AI row shows the same lines
while its CLI is missing, installing or failed, or signed in but not answering yet):

- whether the agent's CLI (`claude`, `codex`) is on this computer, as acp-dsh's own store has
  it: installing or updating it by itself, failed with its error and **Retry**, or found with
  its version; with its install link and **Check again** when it is missing;
- whether the CLI is signed in, as the CLI itself says (`claude auth status`, `codex login
  status`; only yes or no is read). Signed out, the row has **Sign in**, and the command to run
  in a terminal as the other way (`claude auth login`, `codex login`); not checked yet, it says
  so, with **Check again**;
- the connector acp-dsh installs in the background: installing, failed with its last error and
  **Retry**, or ready with its version;
- once ready and signed in, *Ready: pick Claude Code in the model picker*. The model appears
  without a restart; a DSH that has not loaded acp-dsh's routes says to restart instead.

**Sign in** (in Connect AI, **Sign in to Claude Code** or **Sign in to Codex**) opens the sign-in row in a Bot's chat (the selected Bot, or else the Main Bot), through
the Bot team's bridge (`Symbol.for('automagik.cli-login')`, [`@automagik/bots-dsh`](../bots-dsh)).
The row in the chat runs the CLI's own sign-in: a link to open on any device, then Codex's code
to type there or Claude's code to paste back in that row. This page only opens the chat: it starts
no sign-in, picks no model and never sees a link, a code or a credential. In Connect AI the step
steps aside while the chat is in front (a small **Back to setup** brings it back) and is not
completed by it; Settings closes its panel. Without the Bot team or a Bot the row says to run the
command in a terminal instead. While a sign-in waits, the busy file (`src/host/busy.js`, `AUTOMAGIK_BUSY_FILE`) counts it, so an
automatic plugin update does not restart DSH in the middle of it.

The switch is acp-dsh's own `claude` or `codex` setting, written through DSH's settings service,
and Connect AI's Claude and ChatGPT switches are that same setting: off there is off for every
Bot on that agent. An agent that can answer (CLI found, switched on, connector ready, no restart
pending, signed in) is an AI on: its row is on, it counts for Continue and for `aiConnected`.
A signed-out or still-installing CLI does not. Their copy is in the `welcome.team` namespace, in
English and pt-BR.

### Subscription sign-ins and vendor terms

A sign-in with a consumer plan is **personal use under the vendor's terms**: check that
provider's terms before you use a personal plan for work.

## Install into a raw DSH

The plugin needs DSH `>=0.2.1-rc.2 <0.3.0`. Add the Automagik marketplace index to DSH's
plugin market ([marketplace/README.md](../../marketplace/README.md) has the URL and the
steps) and install `@automagik/welcome-dsh` from it. DSH asks before it installs, then
applies the bundle patch (`cordis.patch.yml`), which adds one row, `id: omni-ai`, and
changes nothing else.

Restart DSH and start a new chat to see the octopus.

## The CLIProxyAPI route

[CLIProxyAPI](https://github.com/router-for-me/CLIProxyAPI) serves an OpenAI-compatible
API for the providers you sign into on it. The form asks for its address (for example
`http://localhost:8317/v1`; an address without a path gets `/v1`) and its API key. On
Connect, the host:

1. Checks the address is `http://` or `https://`, with no user name, query or fragment.
2. Lists the gateway's models with `GET {baseURL}/models` and `Authorization: Bearer <key>`,
   without following redirects. An empty list refuses the save.
3. Stores the key with `ctx.credentials.set('OMNI_AI_CLIPROXY_API_KEY', key)`.
4. Writes the route into pi-ai's settings entry with
   `ctx.settings.update('llm-pi-ai', patch, revision)`, the revision read from
   `ctx.settings.describe()`:

   ```yaml
   providers:
     cliproxy:
       displayName: CLIProxyAPI
       api: openai-completions
       baseURL: http://localhost:8317/v1
       apiKeyEnv: OMNI_AI_CLIPROXY_API_KEY
       models:
         - { id: <model id>, name: <model id> }
   ```

The key never enters a settings file, a reply or a log: the route names it by the
env-shaped credential reference, which DSH resolves for each request. Saving again
replaces this route's model list and keeps every other route. Use `https://` for a
gateway that is not on your own machine, since the key travels with each request.

The shape was read from DSH 0.2.1-rc.2:

- `dsh-llm-pi-ai`: `Config = z.object({ providers: z.dict(profile).default({}).volatile() })`,
  where a profile has `apiKeyEnv` (a credential reference), `displayName`, `api`, `baseURL`
  and `models: [{ id, name, … }]`. Its README: a route pi-ai does not ship needs `api`,
  `baseURL` and a non-empty `models` list. The base bundle mounts it as entry `llm-pi-ai`.
- `dsh-settings`: `update(ns, patch, expectedRevision)` deep-merges plain objects and
  replaces arrays, so other routes stay and this route's `models` is replaced.
- `dsh-credentials`: a reference matches `/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$/`.

## Host endpoint

`POST /api/omni-ai` with `{ endpoint, payload }`, answered `{ ok: true, value }` or
`{ ok: false, error: { code, message } }`:

| Endpoint | Payload | Does |
|---|---|---|
| `state` | none | The flags; `deepseek` (a `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` or a DeepSeek account sign-in is stored); `piAiRoutes`; `aiConnected`; `preload` (`omni`, `genie`, `unfold` or null); `host` (`unfold`, only when set). |
| `done` | `{ stepId, connected? }` | Sets the flag for `omni-welcome`, `omni-connect-ai` or `omni-connect`. Connect AI's Continue sends `connected: true`: the companion and the Omni Bot, made without a model, then get the team's default model (DSH's default model when it is served and has its key, else the first model that can run), and their held greetings go out. Skip sets nothing. |
| `cliproxy` | `{ baseURL, apiKey }` | The route above; answers `{ route, baseURL, models }`. |
| `ais` | none | Every row: `{ id, name, via, kind, ready, on, found, signIn?, keyUrl?, needs?, duplicates? }`, and dsh-subscriptions' accounts and hidden vendors. Names and states only. |
| `ai-switch` | `{ id, on }` | Turns a row that is set up on or off (table above). |
| `ai-dedupe` | `{ id }` | Stops the other ways that row's AI is connected. |
| `ai-subscription` | `{ provider, on }` | Shows or hides a dsh-subscriptions vendor's models. |
| `provider-key`, `signin-*` | see `src/host/providers.js` | A key, or a sign-in run through DSH's authorization service. |
| `omni-plugins` | none | The Omni plugins (`@automagik/bots-dsh`, `@automagik/omni-channels-dsh`, `-canvas-dsh`): each one's version and whether it is installed, `ready` once they run here, and the install in progress. |
| `omni-plugins-install` | none | Installs the missing ones in order through DSH's plugin manager (`installBundle`: the Bot team from this plugin's own source pointed at its sibling, else this release's tarball; Omni's from Omni's repository at the pinned release), switching on any that are off. Pressing Omni's power button in the team step calls it. |
| `acp` | `{ refresh? }` | Claude Code and Codex, from acp-dsh's `acpAgents` service: `{ available, agents: [{ id, key, name, on, cli: { found, installUrl?, state?, version?, updating?, error?, diagnostic?, logPath? }, connector: { state, version?, error? }, signedIn?, listed, restartNeeded }] }`. `refresh` looks for the CLIs again and asks each whether it is signed in. `{ available: false }` without acp-dsh. |
| `acp-switch` | `{ id, on }` | Writes acp-dsh's `claude` or `codex` setting in the entry its service names (`settingsEntry`, else `acp-dsh`) at the revision `describe()` gave. |
| `acp-retry` | `{ id }` | Starts a failed connector install again. |
| `bot-type` | `{ type: 'omni' }` | What the Omni Bot starts with, as groups: model and thinking (DSH's default), plugins with versions, tool groups with their switches, skills, folder and permissions. |

The host declares `inject: ['settings', 'credentials', 'connection']`; `connection` serves
the route. It reads DSH's `llm`, `authorization`, `pluginManager`, `agentDefaultModel`, `tools`, `skills`
and `permissionPresets` services when they are there, and acp-dsh's `acpAgents`.

## Develop

```sh
bun install          # esbuild, for the client bundle
bun run harness      # the pinned DSH release the tests and the linter run against
bun run test         # on Node, as DSH runs
bun run lint
bun run build        # rewrites client.js; commit it
node scripts/build-client.mjs --check
```

`client.js` is generated from `src/client` and committed, so git and `link:` installs need
no build step.

# Automagik

Automagik's plugins for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH), and the Automagik desktop app that runs them.

| Folder | Package | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| [`apps/bots-dsh`](apps/bots-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/bots-dsh` | The Bot team: long-lived Bots, group chats, memory, settings, scheduled tasks, the Bot browser. Omni's and Genie's plugins build on it. |
| [`apps/welcome-dsh`](apps/welcome-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/welcome-dsh` | The welcome: the octopus, the team step, and Connect AI through DSH's own sign-ins. |
| [`apps/acp-dsh`](apps/acp-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/acp-dsh` | Agents other than DSH's own, over ACP (Agent Client Protocol), as DSH models: the agent's tool calls show as DSH tool cards and ask through DSH's approval dialog (RFC 0003). |
| [`apps/locale-pt-br-dsh`](apps/locale-pt-br-dsh/README.md) | `@automagik/locale-pt-br-dsh` | Português: the Bot team's Brazilian Portuguese under DSH's own Portuguese entry. Adds no language of its own, so Settings › General › Language keeps one Portuguese row; a pt-BR choice saved by an older pack moves to DSH's pt. |
| [`apps/desktop`](apps/desktop/README.md) | (the app) | The Automagik desktop app: DSH of its own with the Bot team, the welcome and Omni's channels and canvases. `omni desktop` opens it with Omni preloaded, `genie desktop` with Genie. |

Omni's own plugins (its channels and canvases) live with Omni, in [automagik-dev/omni](https://github.com/automagik-dev/omni) (`apps/omni-channels-dsh`, `apps/omni-canvas-dsh`), and carry Omni's version.

## Install

- **The desktop app**: download it from [Releases](https://github.com/automagik-dev/automagik/releases/latest), or run `omni desktop`. See [apps/desktop](apps/desktop/README.md).
- **Into your own DSH**: add the Automagik market to DSH's plugin market and install from there:

  ```
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/automagik-dev/dsh-marketplace/main/index.json
  ```

  Every Omni also serves a market at `https://<your-omni>/api/market/index.json` with the release of these plugins it was tested with.

Nothing here is published to npm. The plugins install as git sources pinned to a release commit, or from the tarballs each release carries (`plugins.json` lists their integrity).

## History

`@automagik/bots-dsh` and `@automagik/welcome-dsh` were `@automagik/omni-dsh` and `@automagik/omni-ai-dsh` in automagik-dev/omni (`apps/omni-ui-dsh`, `apps/omni-ai-dsh`), and the desktop app was automagik-dev/omni-desktop. They moved here with their history. What did not change with the names: plugin ids (`omni-ui`, `omni-ai`), routes and browser-storage prefixes. From 3.12 the team's home is Automagik's own (`~/.automagik/bots`, or `~/.automagik/desktop/bots` in the app), and the app's identity is Automagik's (`ai.namastex.automagik`): an app from 3.11.x or before is installed afresh, not updated.

- The Bot team's client bundle also answers to its former name, so channels and canvas plugins built before the rename keep working on it.
- In your own DSH: install `@automagik/bots-dsh` from the market. With both installed, the newer one runs (they share the plugin id); remove `@automagik/omni-dsh` when you like. A settings row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` that names `@automagik/omni-dsh` needs its `name:` changed to `@automagik/bots-dsh` to keep applying.

## Versions and releases

One version for the whole repository, `3.N` (semver `3.N.0`, N one above the last release: `scripts/version.ts`), above the 2.x builds omni-desktop released. Every merge into dev is a release: `release.yml` tags `v<version>`, publishes the plugin tarballs and `plugins.json`, builds the desktop app into the same release (`desktop-build.yml`), lists the release in [`marketplace/automagik.json`](marketplace/automagik.json), and moves `main` to it. `follow-omni.yml` moves the desktop app to each newer Omni release and cuts a release with it.

| Branch | What |
|---|---|
| `dev` | Integration: pull requests land here; releases are cut from it |
| `main` | The latest release, moved by `release.yml` only |

## Develop

Bun for the repository's own tooling; the plugins run on Node, as DSH does (`node --test`, esbuild), with Bun installing them; the desktop app uses npm for Electron.

```sh
bun install && bun run check                    # versions, release tooling, market index
cd apps/bots-dsh && bun install && bun run harness && bun run test
cd apps/welcome-dsh && bun install && bun run harness && bun run test
cd apps/desktop && npm ci && npm test
node scripts/boot-check.mjs                     # boot the plugins with Omni's in headless Chromium
```

## License

Apache-2.0. See [LICENSE](LICENSE) and [NOTICE](NOTICE).

# @as-one/plugin As One 网关的 **DSH(Cordis)插件** —— 宿主半 + client 半同一个包。它把 `@as-one/core`(纯 TS 核心,零 Electron 依赖)、`@as-one/panel`(面板方法)、 `@as-one/panel-ui`(React 页面)装进 DSH:打开 SQLite、构造 Scheduler + Router, 把 OpenAI 兼容网关面挂在 **`ctx.webServer`**(不是自建 `http.Server`),把面板页 挂进 DSH 侧栏,并且通过 **LLM adapter 把模型列表直接嵌进 DSH 原生模型选择器**。 > 安装形态:DSH 插件管理器按 `github:owner/repo` 安装时会剥掉 `#` 之后的全部内容, > **子目录装不了** —— 发布仓库的根必须就是这个插件包本身(`lib/` + `cordis.patch.yml` > + `package.json` 直接入库)。`lib/` 是构建产物,发布前要先 `pnpm -C packages/dsh-plugin build`。 ## 包结构 ``` packages/dsh-plugin/ ├── package.json # DSH 插件 manifest(dsh.bundle.patch / dsh.client / peer) ├── cordis.patch.yml # 注册条目(id: as-one-gateway, name: @as-one/plugin) ├── tsconfig.json # typecheck(noEmit) ├── tsconfig.build.json # 构建到 lib/ ├── scripts/ │ ├── bundle-host.mjs # esbuild 打 lib/index.js(自包含,只 import node 内置) │ └── bundle-client.mjs # esbuild 打 lib/client.js(内联面板 CSS + React 页面) ├── src/ │ ├── index.ts # Cordis 入口:resolveDirs → setupAsOne → 挂路由 / 面板 / llm adapter │ ├── context-types.ts # ctx.webServer / ctx.llm 的宿主服务结构镜像(零 Node 类型) │ ├── setup.ts # setupAsOne(options) 装配:DB + 凭据 + 调度 + 路由(可冒烟测) │ ├── repo.ts # AppSchedulerRepo: AsOneDatabase+ProviderRegistry → SchedulerRepo │ ├── upstream.ts # 转口 gateway-upstream.js 的 buildResolveUpstream(parity 副本) │ ├── gateway-upstream*.ts # ⚠️ apps/electron 的**逐字副本**(5 文件),见「与 Electron 的复用关系」 │ ├── models.ts # 转口 @as-one/panel/modelcatalog(/v1/models 清单唯一真源) │ ├── routes.ts # 网关面 GET /v1/models、POST /v1/chat/completions │ ├── panel-routes.ts # 面板数据面 /as-one/api/(PANEL_METHODS 白名单) │ ├── panel-host.ts # 把 AsOneRuntime 装成 PanelContext,复用 @as-one/panel 的 createPanel │ ├── llm-adapter.ts # ★ DSH LLM adapter:模型进原生选择器 + OpenAI delta → StreamChunk │ ├── llm-types.ts # dsh-llm 的类型结构镜像(宿主包只有 .js 无 .d.ts,不能 import) │ ├── wire.ts # readJsonBody / writeJson / toUpstreamRequest │ ├── panel-types.ts # 面板数据类型 type-only 镜像 │ ├── client.ts # client 半入口(platform "web") │ └── client/ # api.ts / panel.tsx / locales.ts / styles.ts / context.ts └── test/ # setup / api / gateway-max-tokens / llm-adapter ``` ## 与 apps/electron 的复用关系 两个宿主**共用同一份核心与面板**,只有装配层各写一份: | 本包文件 | 对应 electron 文件 | 复用方式 | | --- | --- | --- | | `src/setup.ts` | `apps/electron/src/main/assembly.ts` | 同装配顺序,去掉 `http.Server` 与窗口 | | `src/repo.ts` | `apps/electron/src/main/core-repo.ts` | 逐字段移植(只共享 core API) | | `src/gateway-upstream*.ts` | `apps/electron/src/main/gateway-upstream*.ts` | **逐字副本**,`cp` 同步 | | `src/panel-host.ts` | `assembly.ts` 的 createPanel 段 | 共用 `@as-one/panel` 的 `createPanel`/`dispatchPanel` | | `src/models.ts` | `assembly.ts` | **都只是转口** —— 真源在 `@as-one/panel/src/modelcatalog.ts`(见下) | ⚠️ **`/v1/models` 清单只有一份实现**。历史上它是两个宿主各一份逐字副本,漂移过一次 (插件版不过滤 `hidden`);现在 `listModelEntries` / `providersWithCredentials` / `dedupeLabels` 全在 `packages/panel/src/modelcatalog.ts`,`src/models.ts` 与 `assembly.ts` 都只做 re-export —— 改口径只需改一处,不会再两边跑。 | `src/client/` + `@as-one/panel-ui` | Electron 渲染进程 | 同一套 React 页面 | ⚠️ **`gateway-upstream*.ts` 是副本,会漂移**。改完 Electron 侧必须同步: ```bash cp apps/electron/src/main/gateway-upstream*.ts packages/dsh-plugin/src/ for f in gateway-upstream gateway-upstream-body gateway-upstream-errors \ gateway-upstream-peers gateway-upstream-stream; do diff -q apps/electron/src/main/$f.ts packages/dsh-plugin/src/$f.ts done ``` 历史上就漂移过一次:插件副本缺 qoder 通道整块、`canFailover(gerr)` 少传 `provider`, 导致 sensenova/workbuddy 的「429 不换档」在插件里完全失效(提交 390d876 修)。 关键坑(装配期已踩平,port 时保留注释): - **Router.plan 只吃 router 侧链项**:engine 的 `Endpoint` 实例不能直接喂 `Router.plan` —— `withEndpointViews` 把 `inCooldown/realModelKey/username` 挂成 不可枚举自有属性。必须经 `chainItemFrom` 显式搬运字段(`toRouterChain`)。 - **directChain 必须返回扁平行**:engine 直连路径把整行当端点 dict 喂 `Endpoint.fromData`;嵌套行会让 provider/base_url 全空。 - **webServer handler 抛错 = 400**:宿主 catch 住 handler 异常后只写 `writeHead(400)`+end。所以鉴权 401、未知模型 404、无可用上游 503 **必须在自己 handler 里 writeJson**,不能靠 throw。 ## ctx.webServer 挂载的路由表 宿主 `webServer` 契约(事实来源:已安装的 `@deepseek-ai/dsh-host-webserver` 包内 `lib/index.js`,需要时从宿主的 `resources/app.asar` 解包查阅): - `register(route)`:route = `{ kind: 'exact'|'prefix', path, handler }`; 重复 (kind, path) 直接 throw;返回 disposer(删表条目)。 - 匹配顺序:exact 表命中 → prefix 表最长前缀胜 → fallback(桌面包的 SPA dist 已占 fallback,**OpenAI 路由必须用 exact/prefix**)。 - gzip 中间件对 `text/event-stream` 显式放行 → SSE 流式不受缓冲。 | 方法 | 路径 | kind | 行为 | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | GET | `/v1/models` | exact | 鉴权 → `{ object:"list", data: ModelEntry[] }`(**`rt.listModels()` 是 async,必须 await**) | | POST | `/v1/chat/completions` | exact | 鉴权 → 读 body → resolveUpstream → `stream ? SSE : JSON` | | POST | `/as-one/api/` | exact × N | 面板数据面,白名单 = `panel-routes.ts` 的 `PANEL_METHODS`(64 项)+ `getUsageSummary`,共 **65 条 exact 路由** | 面板数据面 wire 形状(docs/client-half-design.md §5): `{ ok: true, value: T }` 成功 / `{ ok: false, error: { code, message } }` 失败。 新增面板方法要**五处登记**:`@as-one/panel` 的 `types.ts` 与实现、 `panel.ts` 的 dispatchPanel、`panel-ui/src/api.ts`、本包 `panel-routes.ts` 白名单。 SSE 流式复用 core 导出的 `forwardStream`(gateway/server.js):逐块 `res.write(ssePackChunk(chunk))`、收尾 `ssePackDone()`;客户端断开经 `clientDisconnectSignal` 感知,首块后失败不再向外抛。 ## LLM adapter:模型直接进 DSH 选择器 `src/llm-adapter.ts` 注册 provider `as-one`(显示名「As One · 合一」),DSH 的 模型下拉就多了这一组 —— **前端零改动**,数据源是唯一的: `dsh-api-session-controller` 的 `buildModelCatalog` = `ctx.llm.listProviders()` → 每 provider `listModels` → 每 model `resolveModelInfo`, `groups.filter(g => g.models.length > 0)`。所以 **`listModels` 返回空 = GUI 里没这个组**。 注册走 `ctx.inject(["llm"], child => …)` 而不是加进顶层 `export const inject`: 加进 inject 会让**整个插件**在宿主没有 llm 服务时(老版本宿主/纯 Web 形态)连网关 路由都不挂;`inject(deps, callback)` 是独立子 fiber,依赖不满足只是不执行。 注册本身必须在 `child.effect` 里 —— 宿主 `registerAdapter` 靠 `ctx.effect` 记账, 子 fiber 销毁(HMR/卸载)时不摘路由,下次 apply 就撞 `DUPLICATE_ADAPTER`。 四条硬规矩(逐条对着宿主源码核过,违反就是整条链路报错): 1. **流语法**(`dsh-llm/lib/types/invariant.js` `validateStream`): `block-start` 的 index 不得重复;`*-delta` 必须落在已开的**同型**块上; `block-end` 必须 index 已开且 `block.type` 一致;`usage` 最多一次; **`finish` 唯一、收尾时不得有未关闭块、finish 后再出 chunk 直接 fail**。 上游是 OpenAI delta 形态(没有块概念),所以块由 `translateStream` 合成, 按出现顺序分配 index,同类内容复用同一 index。 2. **错误形状**(`normalizeLlmFailure`):宿主只在「own `failure` 且 `failure.code === own code`」时复用失败信息,否则一律 `UNKNOWN` —— 状态码与 Retry-After 全丢。所以抛错必须用 `AsOneLlmError`(自带 `code` + `failure`), 且 message 优先取**上游原文**(`err.raw.text`),与网关的「原样透传」定案同口径。 3. **元数据边界**(`normalizeModelInfo`):`contextWindow` / `defaultMaxTokens` 必须是**正安全整数**(库里 NULL 就不给,别填 0);`reasoning.efforts` 不得是 空数组(空 → `INVALID_MODEL_REASONING`),所以只在真有名单时声明,且不填 `defaultEffort`(填了宿主会强制带强度)。 4. **方法表必须补齐**(`LlmAdapter` 基类)**—— 2026-11-01 踩过**。宿主基类为 `providerInfo` / `providerRetryPolicy` / `imageRequestPricing` / `imageRequestTarget` / `listModels` / `resolveModel` / `prepareCall` / `stream` 都写了默认实现,但本 adapter 是**普通类**(宿主只有 .js 没有 .d.ts), **一个默认实现都拿不到**。宿主调用处写成 `this.adapters.get(provider)?.adapter.imageRequestPricing(provider, model)`, 可选链只护前面的 `get()` —— 方法不存在时抛的是 `TypeError: … imageRequestPricing is not a function`,而且发生在**计量阶段**, 现象是「请求发不出去」而日志指向 llm runtime 深处。 声明了 `inputModalities: ["text","image"]` 之后宿主才会调图像计价/目标, 于是这个缺口在对纯文本模型时看不出、一上视觉模型就炸。 `test/llm-adapter.test.ts` 里有一条**逐字对照宿主方法表**的用例钉住它。 另外:`inputModalities` 按**能力事实**声明 —— 只有 `supports_vision === true` 才给 `["text","image"]`,否则 `["text"]`(宿主会把图片投影成文字)。声明 image 之后请求 侧必须真能接住图片(见 `toChatMessages` 的图片块转换),否则就是「声明了支持却丢图」。 `imageRequestPricing` 返回 `undefined`(不声明视觉 token 定价,由计量方回落中性估算); `imageRequestTarget` 原样透传宽/高/字节。基类文档要求的 `attributionHeaders()` 在这里 不适用:adapter 不发公网 HTTP,调的是**同进程内**的 `rt.resolveUpstream`, 归因头由各连接器在真正的出口负责。 **显示名**:`ModelEntry` 有两个字段 —— `name` 是这个模型自己填的人话名, `display_name` 是整张清单摆一起后**保证互不相同**的名字(`listModelEntries` 里 统一算:真实模型撞名追加 provider,逻辑模型只在填了 `logical_model.display_name` 时追加调用串,追加后仍撞用序号兜底)。adapter 取 `display_name ?? name ?? id`,所以选择器里看到的是 `deepseek-flash (sensenova)` 这种可分辨的名字,而**调用串 `id` 永远不变** —— 宿主 `normalizeModelInfo` 要求 `model.id` 逐字等于请求的 model,改 id 就是改 API。 `stream()` 结束会调 `rt.onRequestDone(...)`,所以 DSH 里发起的对话与外部 API 调用 记在**同一份** `logs/requests-YYYYMMDD.jsonl` 与同一套用量统计里。 ## 上下文长度:量,而不是猜 网关发包前的裁剪(`gateway-upstream-context.ts`)要一个 prompt token 数。这个数 **不能猜**:猜高了白扔用户的历史,猜低了请求被上游 400 打回,用户干等半分钟看到 一条红字。 DeepSeek V4 的官方 tokenizer 已经内联进来(`@as-one/core/src/tokenizer/`): ``` packages/core/scripts/build-deepseek-tokenizer.mjs # 官方 tokenizer.json → 1.1MB 的 TS 模块 packages/core/src/tokenizer/deepseek-v4-vocab.generated.ts # 只留 merges + 特殊 token 字面量 packages/core/src/tokenizer/deepseek.ts # 纯 TS 字节级 BPE,零依赖 packages/core/src/tokenizer/deepseek.test.ts # 官方 Python tokenizers 的黄金向量 ``` - **为什么内联而不是运行时读文件**:插件装进 `~/.dsh/profiles/

/node_modules/` 之后,`import.meta.url` 指向的是 esbuild 打出来的 `lib/index.js`, 再去按相对路径找资源就是在赌安装形态。内联之后不存在这种失败模式, 也不依赖 wasm/原生模块(Electron 侧同样吃); - **为什么只留 merges**:数个数只要「合并的先后顺序」;vocab(128k 条 token→id)、 normalizer、decoder 全是死重(6.3MB → 1.1MB); - **准到什么程度**:40 条逐 token 串对比 + 15 条边界 + 276 条随机样本,与官方 Python `tokenizers` **0 差异**; - **成本**:建表 ~100ms(`index.ts` 启动时预热),1.2M 字符 ≈ 1.0s,常规请求几十毫秒; - **谁用它**:`counterForModel(provider, model)` —— 名字带 `deepseek` 的走词表, 其它厂商(词表没拿到)继续用字符加权估算,日志里标 `deepseek-v4` / `heuristic`。 改词表(换了 tokenizer.json)之后重跑生成脚本即可,`deepseekMergeCount()` 那条 测试会盯着文件是否完整。 ### 装得进窗口 ≠ 装得进配额 量准了只解决「装不装得下」,不解决「一次能不能发那么多」。2026-11-02 凌晨 `/compact` 连试三次全红的记录: | 时间 | 报文 | 上游答复 | |---|---|---| | 22:43 | 2333 条 / 125 万字符 | `400 context_length_exceeded` | | 23:32 | 2337 条 / 126 万字符 | `400` 裸 `code: 3` | | 00:14 | 2338 条 / 126 万字符 | **`429 inference exceeds tpm/rpm limit`** | 前两条是窗口问题(裁到装得下就好了),第三条换了性质:请求约 60 万 token, 在 1M 窗口里,但**一次就吃掉了上游一分钟的配额**。压缩请求天生是这个形状—— 把整段历史再发一遍去做总结——所以硬等 60 秒回来它还是这么大,还是把下一个 窗口打满。 判据拆成两条(`isContextOverflow` / `isRateLimitOversize`): - 400 类 → 裁到装进窗口,并把「被拒的长度」记进 `observedCeilings` 供后续请求预裁; - **429 且请求 ≥ 窗口 50%** → 同样砍半重发,但**不写** `observedCeilings`。 429 只说明这一分钟配额不够,不说明窗口只有这么大;混在一起会把端点永久压到 一半窗口,之后每条正常消息都白丢历史。 50% 这条线是为了保住普通长对话:sensenova 实测 28.8 万 / 1M ≈ 27%,限流时该 原样退避重试,不该被顺手裁掉工具结果。 ## 鉴权 沿 core `EnvKeyProvider`:`ONE_API_KEY` 环境变量;未设置 → 放行 + 一次性 警告(missingKeyWarning)。请求携带方式:Authorization Bearer / x-api-key / `?key=`(core auth.ts 的 `extractPresentedKey` 语义)。 > ⚠️ 已知缺口:面板路由 `/as-one/api/*` 与 `/v1/models` 目前**不过 DSH 的 token > 校验**,同机任意进程可裸调。宿主 webServer 的鉴权只覆盖它自己的会话面。 凭据(上游账号的 secret)存在 **SQLite 的 `credential` 表**,经 `DbCredentialBackend` 读写 —— SQLite 是唯一真源,运行期没有 JSON 配置文件。 ## 路径与配置 `cordis.patch.yml` 注册 `id: as-one-gateway`、`name: @as-one/plugin`, `config.gatewayPort: 4000`(保留字段,宿主路由形态**不建端口**)。 路径解析(全部可被 patch 的 config 覆盖;`resolveDirs` in `src/index.ts`): | 配置键 | 默认 | 说明 | | --- | --- | --- | | `dataDir` | `config.dataDir` → `$AS_ONE_DATA_DIR` → `/.as-one` | 数据目录 | | `configDir` | `/config` | 保留字段(SQLite 为真源后不再放 JSON 配置) | | `dbPath` | `/as-one.db` | SQLite(WAL + foreign_keys) | | 明细日志 | `/logs/requests-YYYYMMDD.jsonl` | **显式按 dataDir 对齐**,不用 setupAsOne 的 `/logs` 缺省 —— 否则与独立应用共用 dataDir 时日志会分叉成两份 | 与独立 Electron 版默认同一个 `/.as-one`,所以两个形态**看到同一份数据**。 ## 构建与自测 ```bash pnpm install # 根工作区:链接 @as-one/core 等 workspace:* pnpm -C packages/dsh-plugin typecheck # tsc -p tsconfig.json (noEmit) pnpm -C packages/dsh-plugin build # lib/index.js + lib/client.js(自包含) pnpm -C packages/dsh-plugin test # vitest run(冒烟:tmp 目录,不上网) ``` `lib/index.js` 只 import node 内置(`node:os/path/fs/sqlite/crypto/https/stream/ perf_hooks`),**没有任何 `@deepseek-ai/*` 运行时依赖** —— 宿主那些包只有 .js 没有 .d.ts,类型全靠本包 `llm-types.ts` / `context-types.ts` 的结构镜像,运行时不 import。 冒烟测试只断言 setupAsOne 不抛、空配置返回空链/空计划、stub 配置能构造出链, **不依赖真实上游 token**。`test/llm-adapter.test.ts` 里的 `hostValidateStream` 是宿主 `validateStream` 的**逐字转录**(注释标了来源路径与行号),宿主改了要同步。 ## 与独立 Electron 版的差异 | 维度 | Electron 版(apps/electron) | 本插件(DSH 内) | | --- | --- | --- | | HTTP 服务 | `startGateway` 自建 `http.Server`(:4000) | `ctx.webServer.register` 挂路由,宿主管端口 | | 面板 | IPC(`createPanel` → preload) | HTTP `/as-one/api/*` + client 半 React 页 | | 模型选择器 | 自己的页面 | `llm-adapter.ts` 注册进 **DSH 原生选择器** | | 数据目录 | `/.as-one`(默认,同插件) | `/.as-one`(可 patch 覆盖) | | 热重载 | 需重启应用 | DSH HMR:apply 里现建现放,dispose 清理 | | 上游逻辑 | `gateway-upstream*.ts`(源) | 同名**逐字副本**,`cp` 同步 | ##
