evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-plugin-watchlist-autobet

A **paper-only** DeepSeek Harness Host bundle for the sportsdesk-ops watchlist autobet
pipeline. It exposes the repo's `cli/watchlist_autobet_cli.ts` as nine native DSH tools: five
read-only, four that append to the local paper ledger and therefore require `confirm: true`.

The plugin holds no engine logic, no credentials and no network client. Every tool shells the
one CLI and parses its JSON, so the gates, ledger, paper fill math and P&L have exactly one
implementation.

## The boundary (read this first)

- **No live order path.** `autobet_execute` paper-fills approved intents through the CLI's
  paper adapter only. Any other venue is refused by the CLI with `live_disabled`. There is no
  live adapter in v1, no live-order tool here, and no configuration value that turns one on:
  the CLI rejects any mode other than `paper` at config load time.
- **Live betting is not implemented.** The paper ledger is a local append-only JSONL file
  (`Scratch/watchlist-autobet/ledger.jsonl`, gitignored). No money moves.
- **Approval is a human decision.** `autobet_enqueue` only appends intents _awaiting_
  approval. `autobet_decide` records the approve/reject decision it is given; it does not make
  it. `autobet_execute` is a separate confirm-gated step.
- **Signals are advice, not orders.** Fixture-sourced, stale and no-price signals are shown by
  `autobet_signals` (with `includeRejected`) but are always ineligible.
- The plugin never writes the ledger itself and never reads a credential. Missing files are
  reported as missing (`exists: false`), never as zero.

## Tools

All nine tools return **one JSON object**. Read tools are concurrency-safe; the four writing
tools are not (they are serialized by the Host). Writing tools without `confirm: true` return
`{ "available": false, "reason": "confirmation_required", "message": "…re-run with confirm: true…" }`
and execute nothing.

| Tool              | Kind  | Arguments                                                                                                         | CLI command          |
| :---------------- | :---- | :---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | :------------------- |
| `autobet_status`  | read  | —                                                                                                                 | `status`             |
| `autobet_signals` | read  | `limit?` (1-200), `minConfidence?` (0-100), `includeRejected?`                                                    | `signals`            |
| `autobet_plan`    | read  | —                                                                                                                 | `plan`               |
| `autobet_queue`   | read  | `status?` (`queued`/`approved`/`filled`/`settled`/`rejected`/`expired`), `limit?` (1-500)                         | `list`               |
| `autobet_journal` | read  | `limit?` (1-500)                                                                                                  | `journal`            |
| `autobet_enqueue` | write | `actor?` (default `dsh-agent`), **`confirm: true`**                                                               | `enqueue`            |
| `autobet_decide`  | write | `intentId`, `decision` (`approve`/`reject`), `actor?`, `note?` (approve), `reason?` (reject), **`confirm: true`** | `approve` / `reject` |
| `autobet_execute` | write | `intentId`, `venue?` (default `paper`), **`confirm: true`**                                                       | `execute`            |
| `autobet_settle`  | write | `intentId`, `result` (`won`/`lost`/`void`), **`confirm: true`**                                                   | `settle`             |

`confirm` must be exactly boolean `true`. The strings `"true"` and the number `1` are refused.
`autobet_signals` also returns the advisory `candidates` array — capture accounts the watchlist
does not cover (see [New-account discovery](#new-account-discovery)) — alongside `counts.candidates`.

## The operator control plane (Web UI)

The bundle also ships a Client half: a **Watchlist autobet** icon in the left sidebar opens a
control-plane page in the main column. It never bypasses the engine — the page reads a
same-origin board composed from five read-only CLI calls (`status`, `list`, `journal`, `plan`,
`accounts list`) and a signals inspector composed from `signals`, then posts a closed action set
through the same CLI.

What the page manages for the operator:

- **Signals inspector** — a second tab over the watchlist itself: every signal with its market
  label, confidence vs required, distinct-account count, one-sided share, fair probability,
  reference price, risk and provenance age. Refused signals are shown with their failed gate
  reasons, and expanding one lists every check's actual/required/detail, so "nothing is
  eligible" is explainable in the UI instead of only via the agent. An eligible set carries one
  confirm-gated "Enqueue eligible signals" action; the view never approves or executes.
- **New-account discovery** — below the signal list, a "Not on the watchlist" section ranks the
  accounts the captures saw but the watchlist registry does not cover (login, agent, summed risk,
  last bet time and source), with an `Unwatched N` summary chip. It is advisory only: the engine
  still ignores those logins, and a payload without the list reads "unknown", never "none".
- **Accounts tab** — the watchlist the engine derives from: the code-defined built-in registry
  plus the operator overlay in the untracked `config/watchlist-accounts.json`. Built-in rows are
  read-only; an operator-added row (marked `operator`) can be removed with an explicit confirm
  step. The add form takes a customer login, an agent id, one of the six closed source
  categories and an optional note. Both add and remove record the header's operator name as
  `addedBy`/`actor` and are disabled until it is set; each mutation is confirm-gated, disabled
  while in flight, shows its refusal inline and refreshes from the board the action returns.
  Watching a login only feeds the same gates — it never queues, approves or executes an intent.
  A missing overlay reads as `exists: false` / "overlay not configured", never as zero accounts;
  a failed listing reads as unknown with the error shown, not as an empty registry.
- **Human-in-the-loop queue** — queued, approved and filled intents as cards with market label,
  stake, confidence/distinct accounts, fair probability, risk, age and expiry countdown; inline
  action forms for Approve (+ optional note), Reject (+ required reason), Execute paper and
  Settle won/lost/void. Every action needs an explicit confirm click, and the operator name typed
  in the header is recorded as the ledger `actor`.
- **Decision tracking** — a per-intent decision trail and a global recent-decisions feed built
  from the ledger's `intent_approved`, `intent_rejected`, `intent_filled`, `intent_settled` and
  `intent_expired` events (actor, time, note/reason, stake, status). The ledger remains the audit
  trail; the page is a view of it.
- **Operator context** — the selected intent's accounts (login/agent/archetype/risk), the closed
  gate checks that admitted it, provenance freshness/fixture/sources, paper fill and settlement
  math, plus the current `plan`: what would queue now, why the rest are skipped, and cap usage.
- **Attention banner** — stale signal sources (signals will be refused until captures refresh),
  approvals expiring soon, approved intents not yet executed, filled intents not settled, and
  eligible signals waiting to be queued.
- **Paper-only, always** — the safety badge reads the server's `safety.liveExecution`, execute is
  hard-coded to the paper venue server-side, and no route accepts a live venue.

Routes (same origin as the GUI, registered by the Host half when the browser carrier exists):

| Route                            | Method | Purpose                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| :------------------------------- | :----- | :-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/api/watchlist-autobet/board`   | GET    | Board: safety, config, sources, ledger counts, intents with UI derivations, paper summary, plan, decision feed, the account listing (`base`/`overlay`/`total` counts + rows, `exists` for the overlay) and CSRF token.                                                                  |
| `/api/watchlist-autobet/signals` | GET    | Signals inspector: the CLI `signals` payload (`includeRejected`, `limit`, `minConfidence` bounded server-side): sources, counts, per-signal gate verdicts and the advisory candidate list.                                                                                              |
| `/api/watchlist-autobet/action`  | POST   | Closed action set (`enqueue`/`approve`/`reject`/`execute`/`settle`/`addAccount`/`removeAccount`); requires `confirm: true`, the same Origin and the per-activation CSRF token, then returns CLI + board. `addAccount`/`removeAccount` need `actor` and write only the operator overlay. |

The routes are **local GUI plumbing, not an authentication boundary**: the carrier's own page
asks for DSH web auth, but these paths do not, so any process able to reach the loopback
listener can read the board and the signals (watchlist/risk/config data) and — with a fetched
CSRF token and a forged Origin — drive paper mutations. Keep `dsh web` loopback-bound while this
bundle is installed, or gate these routes with the carrier's session auth (or a separate bearer
token) before exposing the GUI beyond loopback. They are guarded against cross-site pages
(mutations require the exact same Origin, the per-activation CSRF token from the board, JSON
content type and a 32 KiB body bound); the whole surface is paper-only. Every malformed request
is 400 `invalid_body` (including a wrong content-type and an oversized body).
The board is cached server-side for 4 s and each signals query for 4 s; every action answer
carries a force-refreshed board. After installing or updating the bundle, reload the GUI page
once so the Client module and sidebar entry load. A page reload is **not** enough for a
Host-side change (`index.js`): replacing an installed package requires a Host restart to load a
fresh JavaScript module generation, so a linked checkout that was edited while DSH runs keeps
serving the old action surface until DSH restarts. The Accounts tab detects that stale pairing —
a board with no `accounts` block — and disables add/remove with an explicit restart notice
instead of failing every attempt as `invalid_action`; the CLI
(`bun run autobet accounts add <login> --agent <id>`) keeps working in the meantime.

## The paper lifecycle

1. `autobet_status` — is the pipeline configured, is the ledger present, is live execution
   still off (`safety.liveExecution: false`)?
2. `autobet_signals` — watchlist signals with their gate results. `includeRejected: true`
   shows ineligible ones and their failed checks (`fixture_provenance`, `freshness`, …).
3. `autobet_plan` — dry run: what `enqueue` _would_ queue and which caps would bind. Writes
   nothing.
4. `autobet_enqueue` with `confirm: true` — appends paper intents for eligible, non-duplicate
   signals, bounded by the desk-day stake caps. Re-running is idempotent.
5. `autobet_queue` — inspect derived statuses. Expiry is computed at read time, so a past-due
   approval reads as `expired` and cannot be approved or executed.
6. `autobet_decide` with `confirm: true` — the operator's decision. `approve` is legal only
   from `queued`; `reject` requires a reason and releases the reserved stake.
7. `autobet_execute` with `confirm: true` — paper fill of an approved, unexpired intent with
   the configured slippage; recorded P&L is paper P&L.
8. `autobet_settle` with `confirm: true` — record `won`/`lost`/`void` and fold it into the
   ledger summary.
9. `autobet_journal` — the raw append-only audit trail plus the folded summary.

Every illegal transition is a refusal from the CLI (`invalid_transition`, `intent_expired`,
`live_disabled`), never a silent no-op.

Every ledger-writing command (`enqueue`, `approve`, `reject`, `execute`, `settle`, and each
`watch` cycle) takes a cross-process lock file next to the ledger (`<ledger>.lock`, `O_EXCL`), so
an operator command and a cron/`watch` loop cannot interleave a read→append pair and poison the
append-only log. A lock held past the wait timeout is refused with `ledger_locked` (exit 1) and
nothing is written; a lock left by a crashed process is only broken after 30 s. Read commands
need no lock because one appended JSONL line becomes visible atomically.

## New-account discovery

The signal engine deliberately ignores logins that are not on the watchlist rather than
attributing them to someone else. That is correct for derivation and blind for discovery: a
genuinely new account can bet in the desk's own captures and leave no trace in the inspector.

`autobet candidates` (and the Signals inspector's "Not on the watchlist" section) closes that
gap. It re-parses the same three artifacts and returns every login the registry does not cover,
ranked by summed capture risk, with `agentId`, `wagers`, `sources`, `leagues`, `lastBetAt`,
`ageSeconds` and up to three `sampleMarkets`. It is advisory: no gate consumes it, nothing is
queued or written, and promoting an account stays a deliberate operator act — add it to the
operator overlay from the Accounts tab (or with `autobet accounts add`), then re-derive. The
overlay lives in the untracked `config/watchlist-accounts.json`; the code-defined registry stays
read-only.

```sh
bun run autobet candidates --json                       # all unwatched accounts, ranked
bun run autobet candidates --min-risk-usd 100 -l 20     # risk-ranked shortlist
bun run autobet accounts list --json                    # built-in + operator rows, counts, exists
```

An unparseable market still surfaces its account: the market sample is omitted, the login and
risk are kept. Logins are normalised (upper-case, trailing punctuation stripped) before ranking.

**Two clocks.** `docs/graph-live-feed.json` rows age from the feed's generation time, but the
two capture artifacts age from the bet's own timestamp (`Report/Pending` `acceptedAt`,
`getBetTicker` `InsertDateTime`) with the capture time only as a fallback. A frozen portal that
keeps answering with the same old tickets therefore reads as stale activity even though the
artifact was written seconds ago — "fresh capture" is no longer mistaken for "fresh betting".
The portal wall-clock carries no zone; measured 2026-11-04, live-captured rows sit 3.7 minutes
before the measurement instant only when read as **America/New_York** (UTC is ~5 h early, the
desk's Central clock ~56 min in the future), so the engine reads it in the portal's Eastern zone.
A timestamp that still lands in the future (> 120 s) is treated as a broken clock and refused as
stale, never as freshness.
The window itself is `config.maxSignalAgeSeconds`, supplied once by the CLI: the source chip,
`status`, the engine's per-row `stale` flag and the `freshness` gate all use it, so the inspector
cannot say "sources fresh" while the gate says "engine marked this signal's provenance stale".

## Configuration

`cordis.patch.yml` inserts one row:

```yaml
- insert:
    - id: watchlist-autobet
      name: dsh-plugin-watchlist-autobet
      config:
        repoPath: /Users/nolarose/code/sportsdesk-ops
        bunPath: bun
        configPath: config/watchlist-autobet.json
        timeoutMs: 60000
```

| Key          | Meaning                                                                                                          |
| :----------- | :--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `repoPath`   | The sportsdesk-ops checkout; also the spawn `cwd`.                                                               |
| `bunPath`    | `bun` (resolved from PATH/known installs) or an absolute path.                                                   |
| `configPath` | Repo-relative paper config, passed as `--config`. The CLI requires `mode: "paper"`, `allowLiveExecution: false`. |
| `timeoutMs`  | Per-command timeout (default 60 000). A timeout is reported as `cli_timeout`, never as a pass.                   |

The bundle declares no dependencies and no `Config` schema (a linked directory install cannot
resolve peer packages from the profile), so the config is normalized defensively in `index.js`
and a malformed value falls back to its default.

## CLI mapping

Every invocation is:

```sh
bun run cli/watchlist_autobet_cli.ts <command> [validated flags] \
  --json --root <repoPath> --config <configPath>
```

with `cwd: repoPath`. Arguments are built as an **argv array** from a closed command set plus
validated values; no shell string is ever assembled, so user text cannot become a shell word.
`limit`/`minConfidence` are range-checked, `status`/`result`/`decision` are closed sets,
`intentId` is pattern-checked, and free text is length/control-character checked.

The CLI documents itself, so the plugin never re-implements help:

```sh
bun run autobet --help              # command table, global flags, exit codes, examples
bun run autobet <command> --help    # arguments, long + short flags, defaults, examples
```

Global flags are accepted before or after the command, long or short: `-h/--help`, `-j/--json`,
`-r/--root <path>`, `-c/--config <path>`, `-n/--now <iso>`.

| Command      | Short flags      | Effect                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| :----------- | :--------------- | :----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `status`     | –                | config, ledger and source freshness                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `signals`    | `-l`, `-m`, `-i` | gate verdicts; `-i` includes rejected, `-m` pre-filters confidence                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `candidates` | `-l`             | accounts the captures saw that the watchlist does not cover; read-only                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `plan`       | –                | dry run of `enqueue`; writes nothing                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `enqueue`    | `-a`             | idempotent queue of eligible intents; never approves or executes                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `list`       | `-s`, `-l`       | intents by derived status (expiry computed at read time)                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `approve`    | `-a`, `-o`       | human decision: queued -> approved                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `reject`     | `-a`, `-R`       | queued/approved -> rejected; reason required, releases stake                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `execute`    | `-v`             | paper fill of an approved intent; any other venue -> `live_disabled`                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `settle`     | `-e`             | won/lost/void for a filled intent, folds paper P&L                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `journal`    | `-l`             | append-only event tail plus the folded paper summary                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `accounts`   | –                | operator overlay: `list`; `add <login> --agent <id> [--category <cat>] [--archetype <text>] [--note <text>] --actor <name>`; `remove <login> --actor <name>` (built-in rows are read-only; writes only the untracked `config/watchlist-accounts.json`) |
| `watch`      | `-i`             | enqueue loop (interval ≥ 30 s); queues only, never executes                                                                                                                                                                                            |

## Failure shape

A CLI success payload is returned unchanged (`success: true`, `schemaVersion: 1`,
`command`, `generatedAt`, command payload). A CLI failure is preserved and wrapped:

```json
{
  "available": false,
  "reason": "live_disabled",
  "message": "live venue refused: paper mode only",
  "command": "execute",
  "exitCode": 3,
  "details": { "venue": "live" },
  "cli": {
    "success": false,
    "schemaVersion": 1,
    "command": "execute",
    "error": { "code": "live_disabled", "message": "…" }
  }
}
```

`reason` is the CLI's own error code (`config_missing`, `config_invalid`, `ledger_corrupt`,
`ledger_locked`, `intent_not_found`, `invalid_transition`, `intent_expired`, `live_disabled`,
`usage_error`, `internal_error`, and for the account overlay `account_invalid`, `account_exists`,
`account_not_found`, `account_read_only`, `overlay_invalid`, `overlay_unreadable`) when the CLI
answered, or a wrapper code when it could not: `confirmation_required`, `invalid_arguments`,
`cli_missing`, `cli_timeout`, `cli_failed`. The wrapper never throws out of `execute`. The
control-plane action route preserves the same CLI error under `cli.error` for the Accounts tab.

## Verification

```sh
node --check dsh-plugin-watchlist-autobet/index.js
node --check dsh-plugin-watchlist-autobet/verify-load.mjs
node dsh-plugin-watchlist-autobet/verify-load.mjs
```

`verify-load.mjs` is dependency-free and runs under plain Node. It registers the plugin
against a fake context, asserts the nine fixed names and each raw ToolDefinition, asserts read
tools are concurrency-safe and writing tools are not, asserts every writing tool refuses
without `confirm: true` (and that the refusal is reached before validation / before the CLI),
asserts malformed arguments are refused, asserts a missing CLI yields a structured answer
rather than an exception, and asserts the disposer releases all nine registrations. It points
`repoPath` at a non-existent temp directory, so it needs neither the CLI nor a real ledger.

The CLI surface is covered by `bun test tests/watchlist_autobet.test.ts` (65 tests): paper
lifecycle, gate/config/ledger corruption, concurrency safety, the read-only `candidates`
discovery pass, and the CLI help contract —
root command table, every command's `--help` (usage, arguments, long and short flags, examples),
short-flag parsing (`-j -r -c -n` globals plus `-l -m -i -a -o -s -R -v -e -i` command flags),
and actionable unknown-flag/unknown-command errors.

The operator control plane adds these checks:

```sh
node --check dsh-plugin-watchlist-autobet/client.js
node Scratch/watchlist-autobet/http-harness.mjs      # Lead harness (Scratch is gitignored)
```

The Client half passes `node --check`, `bun fmt --check`, oxlint and the repo's fetch/innerHTML
scanners, plus a fake-loader/render harness covering both slot registrations, en/zh dictionary
agreement, the Queue/Signals/Accounts tabs, the operator-name gate (approve, signals-enqueue and
account add/remove refuse without sending any mutation), the POST wire format (`confirm: true` +
the CSRF header), the Accounts add/remove bodies (normalized login/agent, closed category), the
base-row read-only rule, inline success/CLI-refusal copy, and unmount aborting in-flight reads
while clearing every timer/listener. The Host routes are exercised by the Lead harness against
the real CLI (44 checks: board shape/honesty; signals query validation, keyed cache,
include-rejected gate verdicts and payload honesty; foreign-origin/CSRF/confirm refusals;
operator-required approvals; structured missing-intent refusals; malformed-body status
alignment) and were also run live against the running Harness carrier (15 checks). The accounts
surface was additionally exercised against a fake CLI (board composition and a degraded listing
that keeps the board usable, the add/remove argv arrays, operator-required/confirm/CSRF/category
guards, refreshed board and preserved CLI error codes) and once read-only against the real CLI
(51 built-in + 25 operator = 76 listed rows). Visual rendering and the live Client boot remain
unverified without browser control: **reload the GUI page once after installing or upgrading** so
the Client module and sidebar entry load.

## Installing

Installation is an operator action, not a tool: install the bundle directory with
`plugin_manager` `install_bundle` (current profile), confirm the nine tools are listed and the
operator page appears in the sidebar (reload the GUI page once after install/upgrade). Installing
does not enable live execution — that path does not exist.

### Multiple browser sessions (web profile)

The desktop app is a single authenticated carrier: its auth is not shareable with an external
browser, so a plain desktop-port tab answers 401. Multiple simultaneous clients use the **web
profile**: `dsh web` (or `dsh --profile web`) prints a `dsh web:` URL carrying the process launch
token; each browser/tab opens it once, receives its own signed cookie (30 days), and afterwards
the clean URL keeps working. The same web Host serves the control plane when the bundle is in that
profile:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add /Users/nolarose/code/sportsdesk-ops/dsh-plugin-watchlist-autobet
# profile manager adds the dependency; ensure "dsh-plugin-watchlist-autobet" is in
# ~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json -> dsh.profile.bundles, then restart/refresh the web GUI
```

On this machine both entries are in the `web` profile (backup:
`~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json.bak-controlplane`) and the running multi-client web Host serves
the control-plane board (`GET /api/watchlist-autobet/board` → 200, paper-only, same repo ledger).
Every authenticated browser client sees the same root-scoped page/queue; each browser sets its own
operator name, decisions are actor-attributed, and the cross-process ledger lock serializes
concurrent actions across the desktop and web Hosts. Keep `dsh web` loopback-bound or behind its
trusted proxy/Cloudflare Access: the control-plane routes intentionally bypass the carrier cookie
auth (paper-only, local plumbing).

## Not implemented in v1

Live execution, a live adapter, automatic approval (approval is human), and a `watch`
tool (the CLI's `watch` loop is documented there and remains a shell command). There is no
tool that records a live order because there is no code that places one.

# dsh-plugin-sportsdesk-ops

A **read-only** DeepSeek Harness (DSH) plugin for this repository. It exposes the
desk's operator surfaces as native tools the agent calls directly, instead of
shelling out and scraping stdout.

```
sportsdesk_status    the local desk stack: checkout state, webview service health AND build age
sportsdesk_data      what the desk has on disk: dataset inventory, record counts, ages
sportsdesk_downline  questions over the downline snapshot: summary, one agent, top agents
sportsdesk_customer  customer-book questions with every count DERIVED at call time
sportsdesk_links     canonical GSLive Manager deep links per customer, incl. canceled + Filters values
sportsdesk_markets   staged combo/CLV reports: identity gates, wallet attribution, 4-week counterfactual
sportsdesk_ticker    the bet ticker and pending report, derived from the capture files
sportsdesk_wagers    the snapshot wager-state table: legs vs wagers, deduped wagerRisk, spanning, quality, automation health, capture trends
sportsdesk_endpoints endpoint evidence scan: tiers, captures, probe catalog, spec gaps, route surface
sportsdesk_security  security scan: secrets, capture redaction, classified F402 identifiers, calibration
sportsdesk_sharp     sharp-money scan: p90 cutoff, sensitivity, collinearity, agents, leagues
sportsdesk_weblogs   getWebLog evidence: captures, modes, redaction, whether IP rows exist
sportsdesk_dev       the repo's verification gates, reported not_run until executed
```

The four scan tools answer a different question than the rest: not "what is the
number" but "what does the evidence actually prove". They read
`docs/evidence/ledger.json`, `dist/openapi.json`, the capture manifest and store,
`enriched_customers_full.json`, `lib/forensic_diagnostic_modes.ts` and the
`PROBE_OPS` capture-suite catalog, and they never call the live manager API.
`sportsdesk_endpoints` separates the ledger's `capturedResponse` claim from the
existence of a capture file (they are different claims and are not merged), joins
the probe catalog against the ledger (measured 2026-11-03: 24 of its 36 operations
had no ledger row; the tool reports the current count), reports the evidence trend
read from the capture store's `applied-*.json` journal and, with
`report:"service"`, runs the repo's `check:route-surface` comparison of served
routes, ledger surfaces and the published spec; `sportsdesk_security` runs the
repo's own `check:secrets` and its `lib/identifier_scan.ts` (through Bun, because
the Host runtime cannot import TypeScript), splits hits into known downline agents
and unclassified identifiers, calibrates itself against the labeled-safe fixtures
and returns counts and paths only — never an identifier literal or an IP;
`sportsdesk_sharp` derives its default cutoff from the book's own p90 (not a
checked-in 70), reports a 50/60/70/80/90 sensitivity grid, the plateau a cutoff
sits in, the CLV rule's incremental value and the sharp/CLV correlation, then
recomputes the candidate set, cohort p90 cutoffs and per-agent/per-league split at
call time; and `sportsdesk_weblogs` reports whether the getWebLog capture carries
response rows at all (`provenance.body: "none"` and a 21-byte body, measured
2026-11-03), so a missing row cannot be read as "no shared IPs".

Measured on 2026-11-03, the sharp calibration is the clearest example of the
principle: the book's p90 is 47.22, every cutoff from 50 to 90 selects the same
21 candidates because the OR rule's CLV arm already holds them, the sharp-only
count over that grid falls 21 → 21 → 21 → 14 → 0, the sharp/CLV correlation is
0.8745, and the CLV rule adds 0 candidates. The tool says that in the answer — a
plateau, a sharp-only series, an incremental value and a correlation — instead of
presenting 70 as if the data chose it. That does not make the fixture a market
prior: the same answer carries the `generated-fixture` verdict.

`sportsdesk_markets` is the staged-report surface: `combo-uniqueness.json` (identity gates,
dedupe, unresolved legs), `cross-domain-bridge.json` (customer↔wallet attribution, ranked
leads, quarantined count) and `backtest-4wk-cfb-nba.json` (4-week counterfactual with combo
families, guard attribution, CLV). Every answer carries the artifact's `generatedAtIso` and
file age, because a staged report is not a live number.

`sportsdesk_wagers` reads the v2 wager-state artifact
(`scratch/gslive-wagers-by-state.summary.json`, produced by
`scripts/gslive_wagers_by_state.ts --json`) and returns `identity`, `totals`, per-state rows
and the producer's computed `quality` block. The contract matters: `legs` is one source row
per leg, while `wagers` counts distinct `Ticket`s; `wagerRisk` is deduped/allocated by ticket
spanning and must not be summed from the leg rows, and `legToWin`/`legResult` stay leg-scoped
diagnostics rather than wager P&L. The tool never recomputes those numbers, so it cannot drift
from the artifact; it adds the freshness of the DATA (`window.ageMinutes`, recomputed from
`observedEnd`) next to the age of the FILE (`source.ageMinutes` from its mtime). A missing
artifact is `MISSING` (never zero states), an unparseable file is an explicit error, and any
`schemaVersion` other than 2 is `UNSUPPORTED` instead of a best-effort parse. The artifact
lives in gitignored `scratch/`, so this is a snapshot, not a live feed — the plugin config
field `wagersArtifact` points it at another path when needed.

The same tool answers two automation questions from the files
`scripts/wagers_by_state_capture.ts` writes next to the artifact, per the frozen
`scratch/wagers-automation.schema.v1.json` contract:

| Report       | Answers                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Source files (each independently MISSING-able)   |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `summary`    | identity, totals, limited state rows and the producer's quality block, with data age and file age.                                                                                                                                                                                                 | `wagersArtifact`                                 |
| `states`     | the per-state rows, optionally filtered by one observed state.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     | `wagersArtifact`                                 |
| `quality`    | the producer's computed quality block and the flags derived from it.                                                                                                                                                                                                                               | `wagersArtifact`                                 |
| `automation` | artifact age/stale and provenance; journal `lastSuccess`, `lastFailure` and the last 5 runs; current alerts and their severity split. Each file's status is reported separately.                                                                                                                   | `wagersArtifact`, `wagersStatus`, `wagersAlerts` |
| `trends`     | the last `limit` successful captures from the append-only JSONL history: per-capture `capturedAt`, totals and state rows, the latest line's `delta.migrations`/`newTickets`/`goneTickets`, and its alerts. Malformed lines are skipped and counted; rotation is never inferred from JSONL content. | `wagersHistory`                                  |

The honesty rule for these two reports is that they never borrow one file's evidence for
another: a missing journal is `MISSING` and the attempt outcome is unmeasured — never
`"no failures"`, `"no runs"` or a synthesized zero. A missing alerts document is not "zero
alerts"; an empty `alerts: []` in a document that WAS read is a measured zero. The journal
is authoritative for success/failure, alerts are derived from the latest successful
capture, and the artifact is only a snapshot. `history` lines are successful captures
only, so the history is not an attempt log, and it carries no ticket ids by contract —
counts, deltas, timestamps and alert text only. `state` filters each history capture's rows
too, and `limit` (1-100, default 10) selects the newest captures.

Every count in the answers is DERIVED at call time, never checked in: `sportsdesk_customer`
computes the customer count, sample-ticket count, totals and rankings from
`enriched_customers_full.json`, and the verifiers parse the same files to derive the
counts they assert (so a changed book changes the expectations, not a hand-edited
number). Rankings take a window: `lifetime` (default) or `7d` for net/volume; clv, sharp
and churn exist only in the lifetime rollup and are refused on 7d. `sharp` returns the
DERIVED sharp audit (sharp_score cutoff or positive CLV), never a scripted playbook list.

Customer intelligence is derived, not scripted. `profile` returns one customer's cohort
percentile ranks (volume, net, CLV, sharp, churn, hold, wager limit, delay), the sampled-
ticket behavior (risk distribution, ROI, win rate, leagues, markets, channels, UTC hour
histogram, days since the last sampled ticket), agent-peer position, shared-`ip_subnet`
peers and the flags that follow from those — with the cohort p90 cutoffs and the flag
definitions returned in the same answer. `signals` ranks cohort-wide derived signals
(sharp money, high churn, whales, book-profitable, dormant, multi-account networks), each
stating the cutoff its rule used. `compare` places 2–5 `customerIds` side by side using
the same profile. Every cutoff is recomputed from the book at call time; a field with no
finite value reports `null` rather than `0`, and the book is a curated cohort, not the
platform-wide customer base.

That caveat is also measured, not assumed. `integrity` audits the book's provenance —
RFC 5737 documentation IP ranges, sequential third-octet subnets, placeholder selections
(`Selection #N`/`Game Matchup N`), generated id families, coarse `placed_at` grids,
uniform sample sizes and duplicate rollups — and returns a `character` verdict derived
from how many features matched. `profile`, `signals` and `compare` carry the same compact
`bookIntegrity` block, and `signals.multiAccountNetworks` states whether its clusters are
subnet-fixture construction rather than observed multi-accounting. The point is that a
whale ranking computed over a synthetic fixture must not read as an observation of real
customers.

`sportsdesk_links` is the one surface that returns URLs instead of numbers: it builds the
GSLive Manager (Partner 118) deep links for one customer — the 7-day, 14-day and churn
`#/reports/users` windows plus the `#/events/bet-history` calcTime/betTime sidecars — and the
per-player bet-history link over `windowDays` desk days, filtered by SPA `state` and by the
URL-expressible Filters-panel values (`agent`, `betId`, `betGroupId`, `freeBetId`, `kind`,
`groupName`, `period`, `sportId`, `marketIds`). The vocabulary is the shipped SPA bundle's own
(`assets/index-DB17VVxN.js`, read 2026-11-03): the state select has eleven values (`""` = All),
Group Kind is `player`/`agent`/`custom`/`line-type`, bet ids lose their `b`/`g` prefix and are
space-joined, market ids are comma-joined, and `period` may be a code (`s3`) or a console label
(`3rd Quarter`), resolved per sport against the captured `sportPeriods` payload
(`tests/fixtures/gslive-sport-periods-2026-11-03.json`, 102 periods / 10 abbreviations / 40 period
names, captured 2026-11-03 from the unauthenticated `{"a":"sportPeriods"}` POST documented in
`docs/gs-manager-contracts.md` §2.2) — a label needs `sportId`, and an unknown label is refused
with the sport's codes and labels rather than guessed. The grid's
own "Filters" tool panel is client-side AG Grid state with **no URL representation** — "Bet
price" is a hidden grid column over `fVal_new`, not a query parameter — so no link can filter on
it; the tool refuses it rather than inventing a parameter. `canceled` was captured in the operator
console on 2026-11-03 as
`partnerUserId=ccc107&state=canceled&from=1793163600&to=1793685600&toTime=86399` — 7 desk days
ending 2026-11-03, so the window spans the CDT→CST change and is derived, never hardcoded. The
tool shells `bun cli/sportsdesk_cli.ts gslive … --json`, so the window/DST/filter contract has
one implementation, and it never calls the live manager API. The `getBetReport` payload's
`state` field is left `""` because only the hash-route filter was observed.

Live capture has one entry point now: `bun run capture:all --agent <id> --customer <id>` runs
every read-only operation in `PROBE_OPS` (plus `getBetTicker`, which the probe suite does not
carry), rebuilds `data/live-bets.json` from `Report/Pending` and `data/live-wagers.json` from
`getBetTicker`, writes raw bodies to the gitignored `scratch/f402-captures/`, and records one
PII-free run per source in `data/capture-health.json`. A failed or empty response never replaces
a good artifact; the run is reported as failed and the old file is left in place.
`sportsdesk_data` report `"capture"` reads that journal and each artifact's own provenance stamp
(`capturedAt` / `observedAt` / `extractedAt` / `generatedAt`), compares it against the freshness
budget, and reports an absent journal as MISSING rather than as zero sources.

The same report says how each artifact can be refreshed, which is the distinction that was
missing: `capture:all` can only rebuild what an API operation serves (`live-bets`,
`live-wagers`), while scoreboard, Game Admin, Contests and the stored CP analysis are
**operator pastes** — the portal renders them and no API contract proves them. Those are
installed with `bun run capture:dom --input <dir>`, which validates each paste against that
artifact's own reader, requires it to state `observedAt`, installs the normalized content and
records the input's SHA-256 and mtime. A paste that does not validate is refused and the
previous artifact is left alone. The capture report therefore lists `capturePath` and a
`refresh` command per artifact, plus `stalePasteArtifacts` for the ones only a paste can fix.
`sportsdesk_dev` also offers `ci-all` (`bun run ci:local --keep-going`) for a full failure
inventory in one call.

It lives in the repo it operates on (unlike `dsh-plugin-fourc-odds`, its sibling in
`~/4c-odds-intergration/dsh-plugin`), so the commands it shells and the files it
reads version together with it.

## Why read-only

Deploying (`./bin/dx deploy`, `ship`), capturing feeds, dispatching Telegram
reports, syncing R2 and the Fantasy402 `wire` mutations all **change state**. Letting
a model trigger those as a side effect of answering a question is the wrong default,
so they stay shell commands where a human is in the loop.

`sportsdesk_dev` and `sportsdesk_security` are the tools that **execute** something,
and the boundary is deliberate rather than incidental: `sportsdesk_dev` runs the
repository's own verification gates over a **closed set**, and refuses any other
name — the same refusal `sportsdesk_downline` applies to an unknown subcommand;
`sportsdesk_security` runs exactly two repo commands, `bun run check:secrets` and the
`lib/identifier_scan.ts` scanner, and accepts no command from the caller at all.
Those gates and scans read artifacts and check invariants; they never deploy, capture
or mutate. A caller-supplied gate name is looked up with `Object.hasOwn` on a
null-prototype table, so `toString`, `constructor` and `__proto__` are refused instead
of resolving through the prototype chain.

## What it deliberately does not expose

`cli/sportsdesk_cli.ts` answers `winners`, `losers` and `leaderboard` with
**hard-coded demo rows** — verified 2026-11-02 by reading `printWinners` and the
leaderboard printer, which build literal arrays rather than querying a dataset.
Exposing them as tools would feed a model fabricated numbers with a real-looking
shape. `sportsdesk_downline` instead reads `sportsdesk_downline_data.json` itself and
always reports the file's path, mtime and age, because a checked-in snapshot is not a
live F402 feed.

The four scans add one more boundary: **no live manager call**. `sportsdesk_weblogs`
reads the capture store rather than `Manager/getWebLog`, so it can say "the capture
carries no response rows", but it cannot say "these customers share an IP" — IP
matching needs a capture that recorded rows. `sportsdesk_security` reads what is on
disk; it cannot rotate a credential or edit a capture, and it returns identifier
counts and paths rather than the identifiers themselves.

## Honesty rules baked into the tools

| Rule                                                     | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Missing is `exists:false` / `available:false`, never `0` | "No file" and "empty dataset" are different problems; this repo's most repeated bug is a plausible metric computed from evidence nobody gathered.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| Gates default to `not_run`                               | "I did not look" is not "it passed". `ok` is `null` when nothing was executed.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| A reachable `/health` is not "current"                   | The service answers `/health` on every revision. The tool also probes `/api/status`, a route the current source defines, and checks the `/health` body for the current build's `ingress` field. A 404, or a missing `ingress`, means the running process predates the checkout. Measured on 2026-11-02: the live process on `:4020` was ~5 days old, 404'd every `/api/*` route, and its `/health` had no `ingress`.                                                                 |
| Staleness is flagged, not hidden                         | `sportsdesk_data` reports `ageMinutes` for every file and one `stale` boolean derived from `staleAfterMinutes` (a stated heuristic, not a verdict).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| Both sides of a diverged branch                          | `ahead` alone hides commits the push has to reconcile.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| A ledger capture is not a capture file                   | `sportsdesk_endpoints` keeps `ledgerCaptured` (`capturedResponse`) and `manifestCaptured` (a redacted file exists) separate, so neither claim can borrow the other's authority.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| An unrecorded body is not zero rows                      | `sportsdesk_weblogs` reports `rows:0` and `bodyRecorded:false` for a capture whose `provenance.body` is `"none"`; "no shared IPs" cannot be read out of "no IP rows were recorded".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| A security scan must not become the leak                 | `sportsdesk_security` returns counts and paths for identifiers and masked values for secrets, so calling the tool cannot publish the data it reports.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| A cutoff the data cannot identify is flagged             | `sportsdesk_sharp` reports the sensitivity grid and plateau around its cutoff. Measured 2026-11-03: 50, 60 and 70 all select 21 candidates, so `thresholdIdentified` is false for 70 instead of the number reading as chosen by the data.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| An OR rule must prove its increment                      | The same scan reports `incrementalByClv` and the sharp/CLV correlation; a rule that adds 0 candidates is called out as non-independent instead of being presented as a second signal.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| A scanner is calibrated before its findings are trusted  | `sportsdesk_security` runs the identifier shape over two labeled-safe fixtures and reports `calibration`; a hit there means the scanner drifted, and the verdict becomes `uncalibrated` rather than `findings`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| A snapshot is not a trend                                | `sportsdesk_endpoints` reads the `applied-*.json` journal and reports tier growth, upgrades, skips and rejections; the file count and the rejection rate are separate signals, so "more rejected" is not reported as "improved".                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| No artifact is not an empty table                        | `sportsdesk_wagers` distinguishes MISSING, unparseable and UNSUPPORTED; none of them returns `states: []` or `totals: 0`, because a gitignored `scratch/` artifact is absent in a fresh checkout and "no rows" is the number that would look plausible.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| A missing journal is not "no failures"                   | The `automation`/`trends` reports read the capture journal, history and alerts document per file. An absent journal reports its attempt outcome as unmeasured (`lastSuccess`/`lastFailure` null), never as a clean or failing pipeline; an absent alerts document reports `count: null`, never zero; malformed JSONL lines are counted and skipped, never thrown.                                                                                                                    |
| A join claim is measured, not asserted                   | `sportsdesk_ticker`'s `reconcile` report derives the pending↔ticker ticket-id overlap from the two captures on every call. Measured 2026-11-04 20:00Z: 223 of 250 pending ticket ids appear as ticker `WagerNumber`s, so `scope` is `overlapping` and the note says so; an earlier capture measured 0 and reported `disjoint`. The tool never repeats a hard-coded disjointness claim the files now contradict, and a missing capture reports overlap as unmeasurable rather than 0. |
| A missing description is not a new type                  | `sportsdesk_ticker` splits `parseWarnings` into `parseWarningKinds.emptyShortDesc` (a data gap) and `.unknownWagerType` (a code the ticker dictionary lacks), and the verifier pins the split against the source rather than asserting "0 warnings" on a rotating capture. The `E` code was added to the dictionary only after 5 live rows measured it as an Over/Under total prefix.                                                                                                |

Nothing here reimplements a repo behaviour. Whatever runs is the existing command
(`bun run …`, `git …`); whatever is read is the same file, route or checkout an
operator would read. There is one implementation of each behaviour and no drift
between the plugin and the desk's own tooling.

## Two runtimes, and the trap that shapes this plugin

|                  | Runtime             | `typeof Bun` | Does                       |
| ---------------- | ------------------- | ------------ | -------------------------- |
| Repo commands    | **Bun 1.4.4**       | `object`     | the CLI, gates and tests   |
| Host plugin shim | **Electron's Node** | `undefined`  | runs `apply()`, spawns Bun |

`Bun` is a global injected by the Bun runtime, not a library you can import. DSH is an
Electron app, so its main process is Node, where `Bun` does not exist. The reference
plugin's first version used `Bun.spawn`; it loaded fine and all its Bun-run tests
passed, then the first real tool call failed with `"Bun is not defined"`.

This plugin therefore:

- spawns **Bun** through `node:child_process`;
- is plain **JavaScript**, not TypeScript: Node cannot import a `.ts` entry, so the stage-2
  host-runtime test could not import the real module;
- is **dependency-free**: it imports only `node:` builtins and builds raw `ToolDefinition`
  objects itself. This is not minimalism for its own sake — a directory-installed bundle is
  a _link_, and Node resolves a linked module's imports from its realpath (this checkout),
  not from the profile. Importing `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` there was measured to fail with
  `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` unless the bundle carries hand-made peer symlinks. Zero dependencies
  is what the documented "a Host-only bundle needs no dependencies" contract means, and it is
  also why the bundle declares no `Config` schema: a Schemastery schema would reintroduce the
  peer import, so `apply` normalizes the row config itself (bad values fall back to defaults);
- resolves the bun binary as: explicit absolute `bunPath` → the running binary when we
  already are Bun → `~/.bun/bin/bun`, `/opt/homebrew/bin/bun`, `/usr/local/bin/bun` →
  bare `bun` so a spawn failure is reported as "could not start", never as an empty
  result.

The trade-off of raw registration: `defineTool` wraps `execute` with argument validation,
and raw `register` does not. Every tool therefore validates its own arguments and returns a
structured `{ available: false, reason, message }` refusal instead of throwing.

## Config

`cordis.patch.yml` ships working defaults. The bundle declares no `Config` schema (see
above), so the loader passes the row config through unvalidated and `apply` keeps only
values of the right shape, falling back to the defaults in `DEFAULT_CONFIG`:

| Key                 | Default                                       | Meaning                                                                |
| ------------------- | --------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `repoPath`          | `/Users/nolarose/c

# dsh-teleagent-skill-builder

把 [TeleAgent](https://www.teleagent.tech) 技能制作规范做成一个 **DSH 插件**：装一次，之后每个会话都自带 `teleagent-skill-builder` 技能——规范全文、校验器、脚手架、打包器、安装器全在里面，产出的技能第一次导入就能过平台审核（包括那条最容易踩的 `.pyc` 禁令）。

> DeepSeek Harness plugin that ships the TeleAgent skill-authoring standard as a ready-to-use DSH skill. Zero dependencies, no network calls, writes only one directory.

## 它做什么

DSH 启动时，把 `assets/skills/teleagent-skill-builder/` 复制到 `~/.dsh/skills/teleagent-skill-builder/`。复制时过滤 `.pyc` / `.pyo` / `__pycache__`，装完再删一次。

技能里带四件工具：

| 脚本 | 作用 |
|---|---|
| `scripts/scaffold_skill.py` | 按平台硬约束生成目录与 frontmatter 骨架 |
| `scripts/validate_skill.py` | 复刻平台 `quick_validate` 并加工程检查；**字节码直接判失败** |
| `scripts/pack_skill.py` | 打包 `.skill`（zip 顶层唯一技能目录，自动排除字节码） |
| `scripts/install_skill.py` | 校验通过后装进本机 TeleAgent 技能目录 |

`references/teleagent-spec.md` 是规范全文副本，按章节导航。

## 安装

```bash
# A. 从 GitHub 装（不需要 npm 账号）
dsh plugin add github:caigou114/dsh-teleagent-skill-builder

# B. 从 GitHub Release 的预构建包装（免源码安装）
dsh plugin add "https://github.com/caigou114/dsh-teleagent-skill-builder/releases/download/v0.1.0/dsh-teleagent-skill-builder-0.1.0.tgz"

# C. 从本地目录或 tgz 装
dsh plugin add "file:D:/path/to/dsh-teleagent-skill-builder"
dsh plugin add "D:/path/to/dsh-teleagent-skill-builder-0.1.0.tgz"

# D. npm 发布之后
dsh plugin add dsh-teleagent-skill-builder
```

也可以在插件市场里搜 `teleagent`：条目在「技能 / skill」分类下，卡片名 `caigou114/dsh-teleagent-skill-builder`。

装完重启 DSH，插件页「已安装」里会出现，`~/.dsh/skills/teleagent-skill-builder/` 里就是最新标准。

## 为什么必须禁止 .pyc

TeleAgent 审核对包内扩展名做白名单，命中 `.pyc` 会整包拒收，报「存在恶意扩展名文件」。本项目三重拦截：

1. 插件复制时过滤字节码，复制后再删一次；
2. `validate_skill.py` 把 `.pyc` / `__pycache__` 判为 **FAIL** 而不是警告；
3. `npm run check`（也就是 `prepack`）扫描全仓库，发现字节码直接失败；CI 每次 push 也跑一遍。

## 仓库结构

```
lib/index.js                                  # Cordis 入口：apply(ctx, config)
cordis.patch.yml                              # bundle patch：把插件挂进 profile
assets/skills/teleagent-skill-builder/        # 随插件分发的技能标准
  ├── SKILL.md
  ├── references/teleagent-spec.md
  └── scripts/{scaffold,validate,pack,install}_skill.py
tools/check-no-pyc.mjs                        # 字节码自检
.github/workflows/check.yml                   # push 时自动自检
.github/workflows/publish.yml                 # 打 v* 标签时发 npm（可选）
```

## 配置（可选）

`~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/cordis.patch.yml`：

```yaml
- id: teleagent-skill-builder
  config:
    skillsDir: "D:/my-skills"   # 换落盘目录，默认 ~/.dsh/skills
    install: false              # 只挂插件、不复制文件
```

## 开发与升级

```bash
node tools/check-no-pyc.mjs      # 自检
npm pack                         # 出 tgz（prepack 会再自检一次）
```

升级标准内容时，记得把 `lib/index.js` 顶部的 `STANDARD_VERSION` 加一，否则已安装的用户不会重新复制。

## License

MIT

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-wikiskill-experience

跨会话、跨项目的**经验编译器**：把 agent 踩过的坑与验证过的打法，编译成一份不可篡改的持久 wiki，并在之后的会话里以一段短描述性索引的形式注入；在此之上再叠一个**证据闸门控制、永不自动发布**的程序性回路（提案 → 用户批准 → 可回滚的 `SKILL.md`）。

设计来源：[WikiSkill: Compiling Agent Experience into Persistent Knowledge for Skill Evolution](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.27454v1)（arXiv:2608.27454v1）+ 本仓库的**双回路**改造。Host-only Cordis bundle，无运行时依赖、无网络访问、插件内部不调用 LLM。

> **English summary.** A Host-only Cordis bundle for DeepSeek Harness that compiles agent experience into a persistent wiki, injects a short descriptive index into later sessions, and adds a gated procedural loop (P2 proposals, P3 user-approved `SKILL.md` publication) that can never self-publish and can be rolled back independently of the wiki. Four tools: `wikiskill_record`, `wikiskill_hint`, `wikiskill_propose`, `wikiskill_release`.

---

## 1. 它解决什么问题

一次会话里学到的教训，默认活不过这次会话；写进 `AGENTS.md` 又会被下一次"优化"冲掉，且无法回滚、无法整体重来。

本插件把经验拆成两层，**两层走完全不同的演化路线**：

| | 回路 ① 描述性（P0 + P1） | 回路 ② 程序性（P2 + P3） |
|---|---|---|
| 产出 | wiki：`raw/` → `patterns/` → `index.md` | `SKILL.md`（可执行技能） |
| 默认 | 常开 | 常开，但**闸门 + 只干预演** |
| 失败代价 | 低：只是"看过什么根因"的知识 | 高：会真的改变 agent 行为 |
| 回滚 | **永不回滚**（它是审计底账） | **可以回滚**（删 `SKILL.md` 即可） |
| 谁能触发 | agent 调 `wikiskill_record` | 提案：agent；发布：**只能用户本人** |

**关键隔离**：门控结果**永不**回写 `patterns/`。wiki 和 skill 是两条独立可审计的账，互不污染。

## 2. 安装

要求：DeepSeek Harness（带 `plugin_manager`），Node.js ≥ 20。插件是 Host-only bundle，**不需要**重启进程，装完即生效。

版本窗口：`engines.node >= 20`，`engines.dsh = ">=0.2.2-rc.1 <0.3.0-0"`（本地实测运行时是 `0.2.2-rc.1`；DSH 会在**安装前**就按这个范围拦不兼容版本，不会等装完才炸）。

### 方式 A：从本地目录安装（已验证）

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target="<绝对路径>/wikiskill-plugin"
```

### 方式 B：从打包产物安装

```bash
cd wikiskill-plugin
npm pack --pack-destination dist      # 产出 dist/dsh-wikiskill-experience-0.1.0.tgz
```

然后把 `dist/*.tgz` 的绝对路径作为 `install_bundle` 的 `target`。

### 方式 C：从 GitHub 直装（git 渠道，已发布）

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target="git+https://github.com/CHIPINGHSIEN/dsh-wikiskill-experience#<commit-sha>"
```

不给 `#<commit-sha>` 就用默认分支 HEAD（不推荐：内容会随仓库变动）。固定 commit 才是可复现的安装，市场索引里的 git 条目也是这个形态。

> **本机（`github.com:443` 不通）请用 SSH/443 等价形式**，已实测装通：
> ```
> plugin_manager action=install_bundle target="git+ssh://git@ssh.github.com:443/CHIPINGHSIEN/dsh-wikiskill-experience.git#ca7fa719b62cdf6be1a25e5d005ba1f7ecde7db1"
> ```
> 上面的 `git+https` 形式在能访问 `github.com` 的网络上是标准写法，本机无法验证。

### 方式 D：从 npm 安装（**尚未发布**）

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target="dsh-wikiskill-experience@0.1.0" registry="https://registry.npmjs.org/"
```

> 包还没有发到 npm（前置条件见 §11）；这条路径在发布之前装不上。

### 装完怎么确认

1. `cordis_inspect_query host / Tool / listTools` 里应出现 4 个工具：`wikiskill_record`、`wikiskill_hint`、`wikiskill_propose`、`wikiskill_release`（后两个由 `p2Enabled` / `p3Enabled` 控制）。
2. 数据根目录被创建：默认 `<DSH_HOME>/experience/wiki/`。
3. 插件管理页的 bundle 详情应显示标题 "WikiSkill experience" 与本地化描述、自有图标（`locale/en.json`、`locale/zh.json`、`icon.svg`）。

### 卸载

```
plugin_manager action=remove_bundle target="dsh-wikiskill-experience"
```

卸载只移除插件：`<DSH_HOME>/experience/wiki/` 里的数据**不会被删**（那是你的经验底账），已发布的 `SKILL.md` 也留在 skill root，需要时用 `wikiskill_release` 的 `rollback` 单独处理。

## 3. 四个工具

| 工具 | 作用 | 会写文件吗 |
|---|---|---|
| `wikiskill_record` | 记录**一条**经验（九个结构化字段）；追加 `raw/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl` + `logs.md`，然后重编译 wiki | 会（只写自己的 root） |
| `wikiskill_hint` | 只读：返回最近轮次观测到的**候选**触发信号（工具失败 / step 报错 / 疑似用户纠正） | 不会 |
| `wikiskill_propose` | P2：`status` 报资格闸 / `draft` 产原子草案进 `p2/deferred-proposals.md` / `reset` 清队列 | `draft` 时写队列，**绝不**写 `SKILL.md` |
| `wikiskill_release` | P3：`status` / `publish`（默认 DRY-RUN，需用户 token，且只发布队列里已存在的草案）/ `rollback` / `receipts` | 仅经用户批准后写/删一个 `SKILL.md` |

### `wikiskill_record` 的九字段

`patternId`、`kind`（failure/strategy）、`title`、`errorDescription`、`rootCause`（**必须回答 WHY**）、`when`（可迁移的场景条件）、`general`（策略级回避方法）、`projectContext`（只属于本项目的上下文）、`evidence`（证据指针）；另有 `transfer`（`universal` / `conditional` / `project-only`）。

`rootCause` 讲不出 WHY、`general` 写成底层 workaround 的记录，就是坏记录——而 wiki 永不回滚，坏记录会永久留下。所以**语义判断由 agent 做，插件只做确定性编译**。

### P2 资格闸（三条阈值 + rubric 冻结）

`minCases ≥ 20` **且** 最大重复次数 `≥ 5` **且** 去重场景数 `≥ 3` **且** `rubric.md` 已冻结，四条全过才允许 `draft`。参数可用 `minCases` / `minRepeat` / `minScenes` 显式覆盖，覆盖值会在返回值里**明确报告**，不静默。

> **P2 打开 ≠ 绕过闸门**：真实库只有 4 条记录时，`status` 会返回 `eligible:false` 与 `4 < 20`，按规则"停止、不启动演化"。这是设计，不是故障。

### `USER-APPROVED` 契约

`publish` / `rollback` 只有在**用户本人**在自己的指令里给出 `approvalToken: "USER-APPROVED"` 时才真正执行；否则一律 DRY-RUN。工具描述里写死了 "agent tools cannot self-approve"——agent 自己伪造这个 token 等同于不生效。

## 4. 硬保证

- 会话日志**只读**；不新增任何 `SessionEvent` 类型。
- 确定性信号只进内存 hints，**绝不**自动写入 `raw/` 或 `index.md`。
- 可靠性契约：可选服务故障**永不**让工具调用 reject；`ok:true` 时 `raw/` 与 `logs.md` 始终一致；编译/读取失败**显式诊断**，绝不谎报"空库"、绝不把陈旧索引当当前状态；同输入编译出同字节。
- wiki **永不回滚**；门控结果**永不**改写 `patterns/`。
- 发布出去的 `SKILL.md` 落在 watched skill root，删掉即可回滚，**不牵动 wiki**。
- 插件只写自己的 `root`（及配置的 skill root）；**不**读写 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml`。
- 所有注册都由 effect 托管，卸载即清理。

## 5. 配置

bundle 自带 `cordis.patch.yml`，默认值如下。要改就在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里用同一 `id`（`wikiskill-experience`）覆盖——**注意：覆盖会替换整个 `config`**，请复制整块再改。

| 键 | 默认 | 说明 |
|---|---|---|
| `root` | `''` | `''` = `<DSH_HOME>/experience/wiki`；也可给绝对路径 |
| `enabled` | `true` | `false` 仅关掉注入与工具注册 |
| `injectSection` | `true` | 是否每步注入短索引 |
| `mirrorProjectLayer` | `false` | 另在 `<cwd>/.dsh/experience/raw/` 写一份镜像（尽力而为，失败不阻塞主写入） |
| `maxIndexLines` | `12` | 注入索引最大行数（1–50） |
| `topN` | `8` | 注入条目上限（1–20） |
| `p2Enabled` | `true` | 注册 `wikiskill_propose` |
| `p2MinCases` | `20` | 闸门：最少标注案例数 |
| `p2MinRepeat` | `5` | 闸门：单一模式最大重复次数 |
| `p2MinScenes` | `3` | 闸门：去重场景数 |
| `p3Enabled` | `true` | 注册 `wikiskill_release` + 命中回执 |
| `p3SkillRoot` | `''` | `''` = `<DSH_HOME>/skills`（rank 400 的 watched root，写入即热加载） |

数值型配置在激活时会被夹到合法区间（越界不报错，取边界），所以手写配置不会把插件弄崩。

## 6. 数据布局

```
<root>/                              默认 <DSH_HOME>/experience/wiki
├── raw/YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl             不可变经验记录（append-only，内容视为 untrusted data）
├── patterns/<patternId>.md          一页一模式（确定性编译产物）
├── index.md                         短目录：PROBLEM + ROOT CAUSE + FIX
├── logs.md                          append-only 演化日志
├── stats.md                         只读统计（绝不作为闸门输入）
├── manifest.json                    schemaVersion / 启用阶段
├── README.md                        说明
├── skills/                          永远为空 —— 描述性回路与程序性回路的分界线
└── p2/                              rubric.md / deferred-proposals.md / ...（仅 p2Enabled）
<DSH_HOME>/skills/wikiskill-*.md     （仅 P3 发布后）
```

`p3/` 目录（`releases.md`、`hit-receipts.md`、`README.md`）在启用 P3 时创建。

## 7. 验证状态（诚实版）

**已在真实环境验证：**

- 插件以 `dsh-wikiskill-experience@0.1.0` 在 Desktop profile 中 `link` 安装并激活（`application: applied`、`warnings: []`）；`Tool.listTools` 中四个工具**各出现恰好一次**（无新旧重复注册），profile 的 bundles 列表已无旧名。
- 端到端 P3 实机链路：资格闸在默认阈值下正确拒绝（`4 < 20; max repeat 2 < 5`）→ 显式覆盖被报告 → 无 token 时 DRY-RUN → 用户给出 `USER-APPROVED` 后写出 `SKILL.md` → `skill` 工具成功加载 → skill 目录里出现该技能 → 命中回执 `0 → 1` → wiki 未回滚。
- `node tools/verify.mjs`：默认 **50/50** 通过（注册面 / 布局 / 描述回路写入一致性 / 闸门拒绝 / dry-run 不落盘 / 输出 schema 一致性）；`node tools/verify.mjs --publish` **64/64** 通过（额外覆盖「无草案的批准发布被拒绝」→ 显式降阈值造草案 → 批准发布 → 回滚）。
- 打包物自证：`npm pack` 产出 10 个文件 / 33.3 kB；把 tgz 解到独立临时目录后 `node --check index.js` 与 `node tools/verify.mjs --publish` **64/64** 通过 —— 打出来的包自包含、可自证。
- 改名重装不影响数据：`<DSH_HOME>/experience/wiki` 的记录/patterns/p2/p3 与已发布 skill 均未被触碰。

**未验证 / 已知盲区：**

- 工具返回值最终由 Harness 的 `defineTool` 按 `output.schema` 校验（`additionalProperties:false`）。随包自检只能断言顶层 schema 一致性，**无法复现**该层；真实校验以 Harness 运行结果为准。
- `files` 白名单只对 `npm pack` 生效；**本地目录安装是 link 整目录**，不受 `files` 过滤。
- 无 Client UI、无设置面板。`settings.section` 等槽位可用，但 Client 半边的数据通道未在本安装中确证，按"无证据不猜"不实现。
- P2 闸门从未在真实数据上放行过（4 < 20），`draft` 只在测试与显式降阈值时跑通过。
- 改名重装后本次进程内无法区分「新代码代际」是否已生效（不真做一次批准发布就无法观察守卫分支）；进程重启后必然加载新代际。
- Windows 下无法用 `chmod` 造出真实的 EACCES，权限类失败路径只有代码级保证。

## 8. 已知边界与设计取舍

- **Host 插件没有 LLM**：论文里 "Wiki Maintainer" 的根因分析由 agent 调 `wikiskill_record` 时填九个字段承担；插件只做确定性编译与注入，每步 0 次模型调用。
- **触发不等于自动写经验**：确定性信号只产生候选 hints，语义判断留给 agent。否则 wiki 会被低质量记录永久污染（它永不回滚）。
- `cwd` / `sessionId` 归属是 best-effort，取不到记 `unknown`，不影响主流程。
- 每条 raw 记录带 `wikiInjected`，标记该会话是否真的看到过注入索引，供将来筛"干净 rollout"。
- 发布名规范化：`wikiskill-<patternId>`，`_`/`.` 转 `-`，以满足 skill 名 `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*` 的硬约束（不满足会被静默跳过）。

## 9. 开发

```bash
node --check index.js        # 语法
npm run verify               # 自检（临时目录，不碰真实 wiki）
npm pack --dry-run           # 查看真正会被发布的文件
```

源码刻意保持**纯 ASCII**（Windows 上的字节级编辑曾两次破坏 UTF-8）；中文只出现在 locale JSON、README 与文档里。`index.js` 不 import 任何 `@deepseek-ai/*`——本地 link 安装无法解析 profile 的 `node_modules`，所以一切通过 `ctx.*` 服务与 Node 内置模块完成；`export const inject` 必须声明每个用到的 `ctx.<service>`。

## 10. 版本与许可

- 版本策略：SemVer。当前 `0.1.x`——首个公开版本，配置键与工具名已稳定，但 P2 放行路径尚无真实数据验证，**故意不标 1.0**。
- 许可：MIT。第三方图纸/素材若引入须保留署名；本包图标为原创。
- 改了什么：见 [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md)。

## 11. 发布（给维护者）

### 社区现状（2026-11-09 实测）

DSH 插件有两条真实分发路径，DSH 都能装：

1. **npm 公共 registry**（`https://registry.npmjs.org/`）——主流。社区插件索引 1000 条里绝大多数是这个来源，install target 形如 `name@version` + registry。
2. **Git 直装**——少数。install target 形如 `git+https://github.com/<repo>#<commit>&path:/...`，固定 commit，不需要 npm 账号，但每发一版都要手换 commit、没有 semver 升级。

社区收录走 `awesome-dsh-plugin` 列表聚合（自动抓 GitHub 上带 `dsh-plugin` topic 的项目，再人工复核后收录），**收录不代表安全审查**。

### 两条渠道的实施状态（2026-11-09）

| 渠道 | 状态 | 落地内容 |
|---|---|---|
| **git**（GitHub 直装） | ✅ **已发布** | 公开仓库 [CHIPINGHSIEN/dsh-wikiskill-experience](https://github.com/CHIPINGHSIEN/dsh-wikiskill-experience)，`main` = `ca7fa71`，tag `v0.1.0`，topics 含 `dsh-plugin`（市场爬虫按 topic 发现）；已实测 `plugin_manager install_bundle` 从固定 commit 安装成功（`application: applied`，工具在线） |
| **npm** | ⏳ 未发布 | 清单已就绪、包名可用，唯一缺的是 **npm 账号认证**（见下）；认证后一条 `npm publish` 即可 |

双渠道并存不冲突：npm 包负责"能 semver 升级 / 市场索引可自动读版本"，git 仓库负责"源码可见、可固定 commit、不依赖任何 registry"。市场索引按包名一条记录，同一个包通常只会展示其中一个来源。

### 本机网络约束（实测，会影响你复制命令）

| 目标 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| `api.github.com:443`（gh CLI 走这个） | ✅ 通 |
| `ssh.github.com:443` | ✅ 通，且已有 SSH key 完成认证 |
| `github.com:443`（git over HTTPS 走这个） | ❌ 20 秒超时，**不通** |

所以：**推送**用 SSH/443（仓库 remote 已设为 `ssh://git@ssh.github.com:443/CHIPINGHSIEN/dsh-wikiskill-experience.git`）；**安装**时 `git+https://github.com/...` 在本机会卡住，等价可用的形式是 `git+ssh://git@ssh.github.com:443/...#<sha>`。市场索引里记录的 canonical 形式是 `git+https://github.com/...`——那在能访问 `github.com` 的网络上是标准形式，本机无法验证，不要把两者混为一谈。

### 前置条件

- **git 侧不需要单独配 git token**：本机 `gh` 已登录 GitHub（token scope 含 `repo`），仓库内已配置 `credential.https://github.com.helper = !gh auth git-credential`，推送直接用已有登录态。只有要在**别的机器**上推送时才需要新凭据（`gh auth login` 或 SSH key）。
- **npm 账号并已登录**：`npm whoami --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/`。本机当前返回 `ENEEDAUTH`（未登录），需要 `npm adduser`（交互式，2FA 会要 OTP）或 granular access token。
- **包名可用**：`npm view dsh-wikiskill-experience version --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/` → 返回 404 才说明没被占。
- **registry 要对**：本机 npm 默认 registry 是 `https://registry.npmmirror.com`（国内镜像，**不能 publish**），发布必须显式 `--registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/`。
- 清单已就绪：无 `private`、有 `license`/`README`/`CHANGELOG`/`LICENSE`、`files` 白名单、`dsh.bundle.patch`、`exports` 含 `./locale/*.json` 与 `./icon`、**无构建步骤**（纯 JS）、`engines.dsh` 已声明。
- 建议补：`author`、`repository`、`homepage`、`bugs`（npm 页面与插件详情页会用到；当前留空）。

### 步骤

```bash
node --check index.js
node tools/verify.mjs --publish                 # 64/64
npm pack --dry-run                              # 复核真正会发布的文件列表
npm publish --registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/
```

发布后用户侧安装：

```
plugin_manager action=install_bundle target="dsh-wikiskill-experience@0.1.0" registry="https://registry.npmjs.org/"
```

> npm 上同一个版本号不可复用：0.1.0 一旦发出去，后续改动必须升版本。

Cross-session memory injection and publication therefore retain an unresolved authorization boundary. No candidate code or lifecycle hooks were executed; runtime safety and compatibility are unproven.

# dsh-graft-slice

<!-- INSTALL:BEGIN -->
## 安装

两条路都可用。**按你需要选一条**，不要混装同一插件。

## 路线 A：npm registry（beta 通道）

四个包都发布在 `@corvus-dsh/*` 作用域下，当前通道是 **beta**：

```bash
dsh plugin add @corvus-dsh/dsh-paradise@beta
dsh plugin add @corvus-dsh/dsh-memory@beta
dsh plugin add @corvus-dsh/dsh-graft-slice@beta
dsh plugin add @corvus-dsh/dsh-observer@beta
```

先确认 registry 上是哪一版：

```bash
npm view @corvus-dsh/dsh-paradise@beta version
```

## 路线 B：GitHub 直装

```bash
dsh plugin add github:corvus-dsh/dsh-paradise
dsh plugin add github:corvus-dsh/dsh-memory
dsh plugin add github:corvus-dsh/dsh-graft-slice
dsh plugin add github:corvus-dsh/dsh-observer
```

## 两条路的区别（选之前先读这三行）

| | registry（路线 A） | GitHub 直装（路线 B） |
|---|---|---|
| 拿到的是什么 | **已发布、已固化**的产物 | **仓库当前状态**（可能含未发布提交） |
| 复现某版本 | 可以：`@corvus-dsh/dsh-paradise@0.9.1-beta.1` | 不可以（要 checkout 对应 tag 再装） |
| 适合 | 部署、回归、报 bug 时给出确切版本 | 跟进最新修复、本地开发 |

**顺序有意义**：`dsh-paradise` 是内核，其余三个都依赖它提供的协议。先装内核，后装业务插件。

## 装完确认

```bash
dsh plugin list
```

应该看到四行，`fiberPhase` 都是 `active`：

```
include:dsh-paradise       dsh-paradise        active
include:dsh-graft-slice    dsh-graft-slice     active
include:dsh-memory         dsh-memory          active
include:dsh-observer       dsh-observer        active
```

如果某个是 `null` 或显示「异常」，看宿主日志里该包的启动错误——最常见的原因是 Node 版本低于 22.5。

## 卸载

```bash
dsh plugin remove dsh-observer
dsh plugin remove dsh-graft-slice
dsh plugin remove dsh-memory
dsh plugin remove dsh-paradise
```

## 从源码运行（不装插件）

如果只是想跑独立宿主和 Web UI，不需要 DSH：

```bash
git clone https://github.com/corvus-dsh/dsh-paradise
cd dsh-paradise
node dist/harness-server.js
# 浏览器打开 http://127.0.0.1:38080
```

详见《星火 OS 独立运行指南》。

## 要求

| 项 | 版本 |
|---|---|
| Node | ≥ 22.5.0（`node:sqlite` 需要） |
| DSH | ≥ 0.2.1-rc.5 |
| 外部依赖 | **零**。全部只用 Node 内置模块 |

## 为什么包名带作用域

npm 上的**裸名** `dsh-memory` 和 `dsh-observer` 已被第三方注册，包内容与我们无关。
我们不愿为一个名字支付赎金，也不愿让用户装到别人的包，所以改用作用域命名
（`@corvus-dsh/*`）——**请始终用带作用域的名字**，裸名指向的不是本项目的包。
