`dsh-hourness` 是 DeepSeek Harness 的编排层，对任何模型生效：项目图及其右侧栏面板（一个项目一张图，一个项目一个主 Agent）、执行边界（guard）、审计流水（派遣决策、记忆、违规）、`/hourness` 晨报与用量面板，以及规范板（规则与峰值模式）与循环板（何时做什么）。设计行用 `/wish` 让一个会话成为项目的主 Agent。十二个独立行按 `cordis.patch.yml` 声明，在插件管理器逐行启停，停用任意一行会话优雅降级；不装 `dsh-glm-zcode` 也能用。发布后 `dsh plugin add dsh-hourness` 安装；发布前用检出路径安装（见上）。`data` 行的项目目录默认指向开发检出，装好后按行配置自己的 `projectHome`。许可：本仓自有代码按 PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 授权（`LICENSE`，商用需另行联系 northgod@qq.com）；第三方材料见 `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`。

# GLM-Hourness

GLM + House + Harness，两个目标各由一个包实现（`docs/CHARTER.md` §3）。House：GLM 以 ZCode 3.17.1 的训练分布住进 DeepSeek Harness（DSH），质量与官方 ZCode 一致，由 GLM 通道包 `dsh-glm-zcode`（`packages/glm`）实现。Harness：任何模型在 DSH 里沿项目图干活，开发体系由 harness 保证实施，由编排层包 `dsh-hourness`（`packages/hourness`）实现。两个包同仓，都是 DSH 第三方 bundle，各自多行，按各自的 `cordis.patch.yml` 独立启停，可以只装其中一个；GLM 方言不影响非 GLM 会话。

## 分层

| 包 | 层 | 行 | 作用 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dsh-glm-zcode` | 底层 · 通道 | `glm-llm`、`glm-login` | 原生 ZCode 客户端通道：账号登录与加密凭证、身份头、签名 V4、端点路由、Anthropic Messages 传输、coding-plan / start-plan 双档；`/glm-login`、`/glm-status`（凭证状态与各行健康）、`/glm-logout` |
| `dsh-glm-zcode` | 底层 · 方言 | `glm-prompt`、`glm-compact` | 提示词与工具面镜像 ZCode 3.17.1、local 工具检索（LocalToolSearch / DeferredToolCall）、todo 提醒 10/10、压缩镜像 |
| `dsh-hourness` | 编排层 | `data`、`guard`、`memory`、`workflow`、`hourness`、`graph`、`graph-panel` | 数据目录服务、执行边界、记忆与审计流水、决策日志与晨报、用量报告、项目图；`/hourness`、`/hourness-status`（两个包各行的健康） |
| `dsh-glm-zcode`（客户端面） | 呈现 | `glm-ui` | 设置页与会话输入框 pill（默认启用） |
| `dsh-hourness`（客户端面） | 呈现 | `ui` | 右侧栏项目图面板 |

编排层的完整设计（项目图即主 Agent、设计循环、决策卡、规范体系等）见 `docs/ORCHESTRATION.md`，目前大部分处于规划阶段。

## 文档

| 文件 | 内容 |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/CHARTER.md` | 宪章：目标、三问四答、分层、调校原则、工程美学、度量 |
| `docs/DESIGN.md` | 总体架构与底层设计 |
| `docs/ORCHESTRATION.md` | 编排层设计 |
| `docs/ROADMAP.md` | 实施路线 |
| `docs/FACTS.md` | 外部事实账 |
| `docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` | 开发与交付流程 |
| `docs/HANDOFF.md` | 当前状态与已知问题 |

## 门禁

```
npm run build      # tsc（含 adapter 契约检查），产物在 packages/glm/dist/、packages/hourness/dist/
npm run preflight  # 目录表、两包清单与 patch、产物齐全、client 半一包一源
npm test           # preflight + 逐字门禁 + 检查器门禁 + 全部 spec
npm run lint       # ESLint、knip、jscpd 对照基线（只减不增）；lint:update 缩小基线
npm run deps:check # pnpm outdated 与 pnpm audit，标出处理方式（docs/DEVELOPMENT.md §11）
npm run smoke      # 免登录真网探针
npm run smoke:authorized  # 需凭证：coding-plan 端到端请求
```

安装前后均须通过 build、preflight、test；涉及 loader 组合、新包、新行的改动先在临时 profile 用 headless 沙盒验证（`docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` §3）。

## 安装

两个包各自的 `package.json` 声明 `dsh.bundle.patch`，`cordis.patch.yml` 是 Loader 方言（`insert` 行）；根 `package.json` 只是开发工作区，不是 bundle。先 `npm run build`，再把两个包装进 profile（`docs/DEVELOPMENT.md` §3）：

```
dsh plugin --profile <名字> add <本仓库绝对路径>/packages/glm <本仓库绝对路径>/packages/hourness -w
```

只要其中一层就只装那一个包。每个包的界面是它自己的客户端面（`ui/` 下），由它自己的 patch 插行，不用另装；`ui/src/` 只是客户端源码。桌面版自己的 profile `desktop` 只能在桌面版关闭时，经安装目录里的 `resources\runtime\cli\bin\dsh.cmd` 操作（`docs/FACTS.md` §3）。

行配置：`glm-prompt` 的 reportingDepth（汇报细度，原名 persona，旧键照读）/ tier 等在插件管理器中可调（导出了 Schemastery `Config`）；设计行（默认禁用）的 `persona` 是主 Agent 的人设，默认为空，只作用于主 Agent；`guard` 对所有路由与模型生效，圈禁根默认取调用方 agent 的会话目录，每个会话的系统提示词末尾列出生效的规则，组合里有 `workspace-changes` 时另以影子模式记录 shell 写入（`docs/ORCHESTRATION.md` §6）；用户级目录与项目目录由 `data` 行提供，`memory`、`workflow`、`hourness` 配了 `home` 时以行配置为准（`docs/DESIGN.md` §2.4）。首次使用在任意会话输入 `/glm-login` 完成浏览器授权，`/glm-status` 确认后在模型选择器中选 `glm-zcode` 路由；`/glm-status` 同时按包列出各行在本会话是否生效及原因，`/hourness-status` 只列这张表，不装 GLM 通道包时也能看（`docs/DESIGN.md` §2.5）。激活期任何行都不抛错。

## 许可

本仓库自己的代码按 PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0 授权（全文见 `LICENSE`，授权人 NorthGod）：任何非商业用途都已授予，商业用途需要另行取得授权，联系 northgod@qq.com。

许可只管本仓库自己写的代码。仓库携带或依赖的第三方材料（含源码里逐字复现的 ZCode 3.17.1 提示词文本、依赖的许可清单）见 `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`；参考源与移植来源另见 `docs/FACTS.md` §4。

## Vendored schemastery

`src/shared/schemastery.ts` is vendored from DeepSeek Harness `vendor/schemastery` @ 3.18.5 (MIT, upstream https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness, directory `vendor/schemastery/src/index.ts`). The DSH plugin manager only projects native Schemastery `Config` exports into its forms, and `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` is not resolvable from an installed profile bundle, so the dialect row ships the schema factory itself. Local divergences from upstream, kept minimal and listed here: (1) the refs-branch `options.list`/`options.dict` assignments are guarded conditionals because the upstream `x = x && f(x)` form fails this repo's `exactOptionalPropertyTypes`; (2) `ValidationError` assigns `this.options` explicitly after `super()` instead of a TypeScript parameter property, which Node strip-type mode cannot execute. Runtime dependency: `@deepseek-ai/cosmokit` (peer).

# dsh-plugin-local-machine

A DSH (DeepSeek Harness) bundle that adds **Local machine** to the left sidebar: a full local system dashboard with system information, CPU, memory, GPU, disk, network, temperature, fan, and top-process monitoring. It runs on Linux, macOS, and Windows.

[中文说明](README.zh.md)

## What it adds

- A sidebar row **Local machine** (本机管理) placed after **Plugins** and **Schedules**, directly above **More**.
- A global panel with:
  - a header showing the live collection state, last sample time, the automatically detected operating system, an auto-refresh interval (2 s, 5 s, 10 s, or off), and a manual **Refresh** button;
  - a system identity card: OS release, kernel/version, hostname, architecture, desktop/shell, uptime, and boot time;
  - KPI rings for CPU, memory, GPU, and the root disk;
  - a 60-second trend chart for CPU, memory, and GPU;
  - a logical-core grid with per-core utilization, Intel/Apple performance/efficiency core labels when the OS exposes them, and the load average;
  - memory used/cache/free, available memory, swap (or the Windows page file), and the memory-module description when the OS exposes it;
  - GPU utilization, VRAM, power, fan, driver, CUDA, core/memory clocks, and temperature;
  - disk usage plus read/write throughput, network link speed, IPv4 address, cumulative traffic, and transfer rates;
  - temperature sensors and one system fan;
  - the top 8 processes by CPU with PID, user, a CPU bar, resident memory, and NVIDIA compute VRAM when available.
- Simplified Chinese and English copy, with light and dark themes.
- No native module, build step, elevated permission, or background sampling timer: the panel samples when it mounts, on refresh, and on the chosen interval while mounted. Hidden tabs skip automatic samples.

> The design mock used a **System** dropdown to switch between demo data for three operating systems. The real panel always reads this machine, so that demo control is replaced by a system chip showing the detected OS; all data stays real. The panel does not show fabricated values.

## Requirements

- DSH `>= 0.2.0` (declared as `engines.dsh`).
- Linux, macOS, or Windows. No `sudo` or administrator rights are required.
- Linux reads procfs and sysfs. macOS uses system tools such as `vm_stat`, `sysctl`, `ioreg`, `netstat`, `ifconfig`, `df`, and `mount`. Windows uses Node's `os` module plus Windows PowerShell 5.1 (`powershell.exe`) CIM queries.
- Optional tools: `nvidia-smi` for NVIDIA utilization and per-process VRAM; `system_profiler` for macOS memory modules. When a counter is unavailable the panel shows **—** or an explicit reason instead of guessing.

## Install

### From a plugin index (Discover)

1. Open **Plugins** → **Experimental plugins** and switch on **Custom plugin indexes** (bundle `@deepseek-ai/dsh-experimental-plugin-market-bundle`).
2. Open the **Discover** tab, add the index URL below, then install **Local machine**.

```text
https://swjybky.github.io/dsh-local-machine/index.json
```

### From Git

```text
plugin_manager install_bundle
  target: git+https://github.com/swjybky/dsh-local-machine.git#<40-character-commit>
```

### From a local checkout

```text
plugin_manager install_bundle
  target: /absolute/path/to/this/folder
```

A directory install links the checkout, so edits to `client.js` are picked up by the client bundle watcher. Changes to the Host half (`index.js`, `lib/`) need a DSH restart before the new route code is loaded.

## Usage

Click **Local machine** in the sidebar. The panel samples once when it opens, then follows the selected auto-refresh interval; press **Refresh** to sample immediately. Leaving the panel unmounts it and stops its timer. The trend chart is built from samples collected while the panel is open, so it fills over the first minute rather than showing invented history.

When the client is newer than the running Host half (for example after updating the plugin), the panel shows an amber **Restart DSH** banner instead of silently blank fields. The Host collector is loaded only at DSH startup, so a page refresh alone cannot load it.

## How each value is measured

| Value | Linux | macOS | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OS release, kernel/version | `/etc/os-release`, `uname` | `sw_vers`, Darwin kernel release | `Win32_OperatingSystem` |
| Hostname, architecture, uptime, boot time | `os.hostname()`, `os.arch()`, `os.uptime()` | Same | Same |
| Desktop / shell | `XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP`, `XDG_SESSION_TYPE` | `Aqua` | `Explorer` |
| CPU utilization | Two `/proc/stat` reads about 200 ms apart; falls back to `os.cpus()` deltas | `os.cpus()` deltas | `os.cpus()` deltas |
| Per-core utilization | Per-CPU `/proc/stat` lines | Per-core `os.cpus()` deltas | Per-core `os.cpus()` deltas |
| Performance/efficiency cores | SMT sibling counts in sysfs: SMT cores are P, single-threaded cores are E | `hw.perflevel0/1` sysctls | Not exposed; all cores are shown as logical |
| CPU model, base clock | `os.cpus()`, `cpufreq/base_frequency` | `os.cpus()`, `hw.cpufrequency` | `Win32_Processor` |
| 1/5/15-minute load | `os.loadavg()` | `os.loadavg()` | Not exposed (omitted from the hint) |
| Memory | `/proc/meminfo`: used = `MemTotal` − `MemAvailable`; cache = available − free; swap from `SwapTotal`/`SwapFree` | `vm_stat` + `hw.memsize`; free = free pages, cache = inactive + speculative; swap from `sysctl vm.swapusage` | `os.totalmem()` / `os.freemem()`; page file from `Win32_PageFileUsage` |
| Memory modules | Not exposed to an unprivileged process; shows **—** | `system_profiler SPMemoryDataType` | `Win32_PhysicalMemory` |
| GPU (NVIDIA) | `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=...` (utilization, VRAM, power, fan, temperature, driver, clocks); CUDA version from the plain report | Same when installed | Same when installed |
| GPU (AMD) | amdgpu sysfs: `gpu_busy_percent`, VRAM counters, hwmon temperature/fan/power, `pp_dpm_*` clocks | `ioreg` IOAccelerator `Device Utilization %` when exposed | Model and driver only through `Win32_VideoController` |
| GPU (Intel/other) | DRM/sysfs model, plus `gt_busy_percent` when exposed; otherwise model only | `ioreg` model; utilization when exposed | Model and driver only |
| Disk usage | `/proc/mounts` + `statfs`, local filesystems deduplicated by device and capped at four | `df -kP` + `mount`; the macOS data volume and external volumes | `Win32_LogicalDisk` (fixed drives) |
| Disk throughput | `/proc/diskstats` deltas across whole physical disks | `ioreg` IOBlockStorageDriver byte counters | `Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfDisk_PhysicalDisk` |
| Network interface, IP | `/proc/net/dev`, `/proc/net/route`, `os.networkInterfaces()`, sysfs link speed | `netstat -ibn`, `ifconfig` media speed, `os.networkInterfaces()` | `Get-NetAdapter` + `Get-NetAdapterStatistics`; perf counters as a fallback |
| Network rates | Cumulative counter deltas | Cumulative counter deltas | Cumulative counter deltas from adapter statistics |
| Temperatures and fan | hwmon (`coretemp`, `nvme`, `acpitz`, `amdgpu`, …) | No unprivileged system sensor API; NVIDIA GPU temperature appears only when `nvidia-smi` is available | `MSAcpi_ThermalZoneTemperature` and `Win32_Fan`, plus NVIDIA GPU temperature |
| Top processes | `ps` by CPU, plus total threads from `/proc/loadavg` | `ps` by CPU; thread count from `sysctl kern.num_threads` | `Win32_PerfFormattedData_PerfProc_Process` |
| Process GPU VRAM | `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` when an NVIDIA GPU is reported | Same | Same |

The panel never invents a percentage. A missing counter is reported as `—`, **Usage unavailable**, **Driver unavailable**, or **No GPU detected**. Windows process user names are not exposed by the process performance counters, so that column shows **—** on Windows. On Linux and macOS the per-process CPU column is the lifetime average reported by `ps`; Windows uses the instantaneous performance counter. Per-process GPU VRAM is available only for NVIDIA compute processes.

## Host endpoint

The Host half registers one same-origin route behind the connection trust fence:

```text

```

Notes on the payload:

- `schemaVersion` is `2`. A payload without it comes from an older Host half, and the client asks for a DSH restart instead of showing blank fields.
- `platform` is Node's `process.platform` (`linux`, `darwin`, or `win32`).
- `cpu.cores` remains the logical thread count for backward compatibility; `cpu.physicalCores` is the physical core count. `cpu.load` is the 1-minute load for compatibility; `cpu.loadAverage` carries all three values.
- `cpu.perCore[].kind` is `p`, `e`, or `null`; `hybrid` is true only when the OS exposes both core classes.
- `gpu.available` means GPU utilization is readable. `gpu.reason` is `driver-unavailable` when the model is known but the driver cannot be queried, `unsupported` when the OS exposes no utilization counter, and `not-detected` when no GPU is found.
- `null` means the platform did not expose that value. `diskIO`, `network`, `processes`, and `fan` can be `null` when the platform has no usable source.
- `sensors[].key` is `cpu`, `gpu`, `nvme`, `board`, or `other`. A GPU temperature reported by `nvidia-smi` is merged into this list, and unclassified ACPI zones use `other` with their raw label.

## Files

| Path | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `index.js` | Host half: the `/local-machine/metrics` route and its admission checks |
| `lib/platform.js` | Host half: cross-platform probes, caching, rate sampling, and snapshot assembly |
| `lib/parsers.js` | Host half: pure parsers for procfs, sysfs, and command output |
| `client.js` | Client half: the sidebar entry and the full dashboard page |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Bundle patch that inserts the `local-machine` row |
| `locale/*.json` | Plugin Manager title and description per language |
| `icon.svg` | Plugin icon |
| `test/` | Parser fixtures for all three OSes, a live snapshot test, fallback test, and route tests |
| `scripts/make-index.mjs` | Writes `docs/index.json` (plugin market index, format 1) from the manifest and `HEAD` |
| `docs/` | Published plugin index and its icon (GitHub Pages) |

## Development

```bash
npm test
```

The fixtures exercise the Linux, macOS, and Windows output shapes on any machine. The live snapshot and route tests read the machine running the suite, so run `npm test` once on each OS before a release.

The client is plain React with no build step: `client.js` registers a factory with the DSH module loader, and the Host serves it. Edits to `client.js` reach an open page through the client bundle watcher; changes to `index.js` or `lib/` need a DSH restart.

## Publishing a release (maintainer)

```bash
# 1. bump the version in package.json, commit the code
git add -A && git commit -m "feat: ..."
git tag v2.0.0

# 2. regenerate the index (pins the new commit), then commit and push
node scripts/make-index.mjs
git add docs && git commit -m "chore: publish market index"
git push && git push --tags
```

GitHub Pages serves `docs/`, so the index stays at

evidence.readmeExcerpt: # 最近会话 · dsh-recent-sessions 中文 · English > 像官方「工作区」一样长在左侧栏里的「最近会话」—— 收藏、运行中、等待你的回应、完成未读、最近活跃，一屏直达； > 不用时**一键收起到一行**，标题右侧 🔍 还能**就地搜索**，**每个会话行都有 ☆ 一点即收藏**。 示意图：演示数据，非真实会话 收起态：整段只剩一行（36px），点标题随时展开，选择会被记住；工作区立即拿回全部高度 🌐 **落地页 / 在线说明**： 给 [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) 的**左侧栏**加一个「最近会话」分区。它和官方「工作区」共用同一套网格与交互（36px 分区标题 / 34px 分组行 / 32px 会话行 / 28px 溢出行），看起来就是官方侧边栏的一部分：不另开页面、不是悬浮面板，也不改变官方会话浏览区的任何行为。 **顺手的地方**： - **每个会话行都带 ☆**——包括官方的会话列表，悬停即可一键收藏 / 取消，不用打开会话、也不用拖拽； - 整段可以收起到一行（不占工作区列表的高度，选择会被记住）； - 标题右侧的 🔍 直接把标题行变成输入框，命中文字高亮、`Enter` 打开第一条；`↑`/`↓` 可在分区内键盘浏览； - 收藏里可以拖拽排序，悬停收藏行还会出现 ↑「移到最前」； - 对某个分类手动展开或收起后，硬刷新也会保持你的选择；分区内的滚动位置也会记住； - 黄点行直接写「待授权 / 待回答」，不用点进去才知道在等什么。 - 会话行悬停时给出与官方同一套动作：**⋯ 更多 / 归档 / ☆ 收藏 / 置顶**；「⋯」菜单里有 置顶 · 收藏 · 移到最前（仅收藏行）· 归档 · 复制会话 ID； - 悬停会话行时，**状态点会变成十字准星**，点一下就在下方工作区列表里定位并展开它所属的项目； - 点标题右侧的 ⤢ 打开**面板页**：五个分类展示**全部**会话，顶部可搜索、可按状态筛选，分类标题吸顶，长列表按 60 条分片加载； - 置顶的会话在**每个分类里排最前**，并显示与官方一致的图钉图标（置顶状态与下方官方列表是同一份）。 **它解决什么问题**：任务一多，「哪个在跑、哪个跑完了还没看、哪个在等我授权或回答、我常回访的是哪几个」就得在会话列表里翻半天。这个分区把 **收藏 / 运行中 / 等待你的回应 / 完成未读 / 最近活跃** 五类固定在最上面，配黄 / 蓝 / 绿状态点，一眼就知道下一步该点哪里；收藏可以点 ☆，也可以把会话行直接拖进「收藏」分组。 它以插件形式接管左侧栏外壳，因此这个分组**就在工作区分组上方**，而不是另开一个页面；官方会话浏览区（搜索、会话 `…` 菜单、拖拽排序、归档筛选、工作区增删改）原样保留、原样工作。 默认只统计**属于某个工作区**的会话：未分组的会话（例如在 `/tmp` 里用 CLI 跑的一次性任务）**只有在你需要回应它时**才会出现（等待授权 / 待回答），其余情况（空闲、运行中、完成未读）都留在下方官方列表的「未分组」里。 ## 视觉与交互细节 - **分区标题**与「工作区」同规格：高 36px、14px/20、`label-tertiary`、左侧 4px 内边距，标题完整显示不截断；标题可点击，右侧三个 28×28 图标动作：`搜索会话`、`收起/展开`、`在面板中打开`。 - **一键收起到一行**：点标题（或「收起」）整段折叠成一行 36px，工作区列表立刻拿回全部高度；状态记在浏览器里，下次打开保持。 - 面板页不再占用左侧面板列表的一行（它与分区重复），需要时点标题右侧的 ⤢ 打开。 - **分区内搜索**：点标题右侧的 🔍 直接把标题行变成输入框，按会话标题 / 工作区名筛选本分区里的会话；`Esc` 或 × 退出，`Enter` 打开第一条，命中文字高亮。 - **分类**与工作区分组行同规格：高 34px、16×20 图标槽、标题 14px/20；**悬停时图标换成实心三角**，点击折叠/展开；右侧显示 10px 数量。 - **默认展开规则**：**收藏永远默认收起**（为空时右侧显示「拖入或点 ☆ 收藏」，非空时显示数量）；有「等待你的回应 / 运行中 / 完成未读」时，这些分类默认展开、最近活跃默认收起；三类都没有时，最近活跃默认展开。 - **你的折叠选择会被记住**：一旦手动展开/收起了某个分类，该选择写入 `localStorage`，**硬刷新或重开页面后都会恢复**（包括"收藏是展开的"这个状态）。 - **会话行**与官方会话行同规格：高 32px、状态点占 16×20 槽、标题 14px/20、右侧 10px 相对时间；**悬停时隐藏时间、浮出 ☆**；当前打开的会话常驻选中底色。 - **溢出行**沿用官方 `展开其余 N 个会话 / 收起`（28px、12px、`label-tertiary`）。 - 行间距 2px、分组间距 4px，与官方列表同一套节奏；分类之间与工作区之间用 1px 分隔线区隔。 ## 收藏 三种方式： 1. 会话行悬停时点 `☆`（官方会话行上的新增按钮）； 2. 把会话行**拖进「最近会话」分组**（从下面官方列表直接拖上来即可）； 3. 点分区标题右侧的 ⤢ 打开面板页，在里面拖到「收藏」区，或拖到某条收藏上调整顺序。 收藏顺序即展示顺序，保存在本机浏览器（见「数据」）。 收藏不会把会话从「最近活跃」里拿走：最近活跃是**纯时间列表**（最近碰过的 5 个会话，不管有没有被收藏）；已收藏的行**只用一个信号**——行尾那颗金色 **★**（收藏按钮本身，常驻显示），不再额外叠加标记，避免一行出现两个星。 ## 安装 **插件市场（推荐）**：Plugins → Discover → **Add index source**，粘贴下面的索引地址，然后在卡片上点安装： ``` https://tianxiaz.github.io/dsh-recent-sessions/market/index.json ``` > GitHub Pages 缓存约 10 分钟，发版后很快生效。若该地址在你所在网络不通，可换用 jsDelivr 镜像（分支缓存约 12 小时）： > `https://fastly.jsdelivr.net/gh/tianxiaz/dsh-recent-sessions@main/market/index.json` **命令行**： ```bash dsh plugin --profile <你的 profile> add "git+https://github.com/tianxiaz/dsh-recent-sessions.git" ``` **本地目录**（开发/自用）： ``` plugin_manager install_bundle <绝对路径>/dsh-recent-sessions ``` 安装后**硬刷新页面**即可。 ## ⚠️ 侧栏接管说明（重要） DSH 左侧栏的两个关键位都是**单占位槽**，插件无法"在官方分组旁边插入一节"： | 槽 | 官方占用者 | 性质 | |---|---|---| | `sidebar` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar` 的 SidebarRoot | 整个左列外壳（品牌行、新会话、面板列表、页脚） | | `sidebar.workspaces` | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-workspace` 的 WorkspaceBrowser | 会话浏览区 | 所以本插件的做法是：**接管外壳、复用会话区**。 - bundle patch 里 `- id: ui-sidebar` + `disabled: true`，禁用官方外壳； - 本插件注册 `sidebar` 占位，声明与官方**同名**的 8 个子槽（`brand.mark` / `brand.name` / `toggle.badge` / `panellist` / `panellist.actions` / `workspaces` / `settings` / `footer.action`），并把 `sidebar.workspaces` **原样渲染**官方 WorkspaceBrowser； - 同时提供 `shell.leading`（macOS 侧栏完全收起时的"打开侧栏 / 新会话"两个窗口按钮），否则收起后无处点开。 这意味着： - 品牌行、新会话按钮、面板图标列表、页脚由本插件渲染（几何与配色对齐官方，但**不是逐像素一致**）； - DSH 官方侧栏以后若改动，本插件需要同步更新（见下）； - 不想要了，禁用/卸载本 bundle 即可恢复官方侧栏（会同时失去面板页与 `☆` 按钮）。 **崩溃隔离**：接管意味着"插件挂了 = 左栏没有占位者"，所以侧栏整体套了一层 error boundary。任何子组件抛错时不会留下空白列，而是退化为：顶部一句提示 + 「重新加载」按钮 + **原样渲染的官方会话列表**（仍可正常选会话、切工作区）。 **空间分配**：始终优先保证工作区列表 —— 工作区至少拿到可用高度的 **55%**（且不少于 160px），「最近会话」最多占 **45%**、上限 420px 并在内部滚动；窗口被压得很矮时，最近会话会**只保留标题一行**，把高度全部让给工作区。拖动工作区里的会话时，「最近会话」还会**临时折叠成一行**，把高度让出来，标题同时变成投放区。 ## 兼容性与维护 - 目标版本：DSH `^0.2.1-rc.5`（`engines.dsh`）。 - 已知失败模式：若某版 DSH 里 `ui-sidebar` 这个行 **id 改名或消失**，patch 会 warn + skip，本插件注册 `sidebar` 时与官方外壳冲突 → 本插件整体不生效（官方 UI 保持不变）。修复：更新 `cordis.patch.yml` 里的行 id、必要时重新对齐外壳。 - 升级 DSH 后的核对清单（都在 `client.js` 的 `sidebar shell` 区）： 1. `sidebar` 槽的 owner props 是否仍是 `{ collapsed, width }`； 2. 需要声明/渲染的子槽集合是否仍是那 8 个； 3. 官方 `SidebarRoot` 的几何（logo 行 60/36px、新会话按钮 38/36px、面板行 36px、折叠内边距 18/10/6）是否变化 → 同步 `SHELL_CSS`； 4. `sidebar.panellist` 的 owner props（`size` / `active`）与 `sidebar.workspaces` 的 owner props（`wide` / `expandSidebar`）； 5. `shell.leading` 的挂载条件（macOS 且侧栏收起）； 6. 官方 WorkspaceBrowser 是否仍以 `sidebar.workspaces` 单占位方式注册。 ## 数据与隐私 - 纯前端插件，**不发起任何网络请求**（除 DSH 自身）。 - 收藏与折叠状态存在当前浏览器 `localStorage`： `dsh.recent-sessions.favorites.v1`（收藏的会话 id，按展示顺序）、`dsh.recent-sessions.inline.open.v1`（整段是否收起到一行）、`dsh.recent-sessions.cats.v1`（每个分类手动折叠/展开的选择）。 - 已归档会话不出现在快捷列表里（收藏仍保留，取消归档后自动回来）；收藏按站点区分，换浏览器/换域名不共享。 ## 许可 MIT，见 [LICENSE](./LICENSE)。

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-opencode-go-router

[![CI](https://github.com/TLEWA/dsh-opencode-go-router/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/TLEWA/dsh-opencode-go-router/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![npm version](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/dsh-opencode-go-router.svg)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-opencode-go-router)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE)

**简体中文** · [English](./README.en.md)

一个 DeepSeek Harness（DSH）宿主插件：当一条 OpenCode Go 的 DeepSeek 系列会话请求**即将**打不中上游前缀缓存、并且最近的请求很慢时，为这条请求换一个新的路由 id。预测发生在请求发出之前，所以切换正好作用于这条请求本身，不会额外增加一次缓存 miss。

它还维护一个两级热路由 id 池：前缀相似的新会话可以接手已有缓存的 id，从而省掉冷启动。

这是 DSH 插件（内部 id 为 `opencode-router`）的 npm 包。它只修改 OpenCode Go 的路由请求头，不是模型适配器。

## 为什么需要它

OpenCode Go 用 `x-opencode-session` 请求头把一条会话钉在某个上游后端上，由该后端为重复的提示词前缀提供缓存。前缀变化时缓存就会失效：billion-context 的上下文折叠会改写上下文，系统提示词变化会改写提示词本身。折叠重建之后，重建请求本身是冷的，但紧随其后的请求马上又变热，因为重建刚刚把新前缀写进了那个后端的缓存。

因此唯一有意义的切换时机，是在一条**本来就会冷**的请求发出之前。本插件在每条合格的请求发出前，用当时已知的信号预测它的缓存命中率——前缀是否变化、空闲了多久、上一次实测命中、上一次请求是否刚刚完整 prefill 了大前缀——当预测值 `<=` `cacheHitThresholdPct`（默认 25%）**且**最近的请求很慢时，就换路由 id。由于预测发生在 `llm/stream` 钩子里、请求头组装之前，新的路由 id 就作用于这条被判冷的请求：新后端为它建立缓存，不会再额外多出一条冷请求。

只有 OpenCode Go 的 DeepSeek 系列会话符合条件。即使状态文件里存在路由，其他模型也不会被本插件路由。

系统提示词改写和消息历史被压缩，是前缀一定变化的两种情况，所以携带这两种变化的请求总是被判为冷。但“判冷”本身不足以触发切换：最近的请求必须同时很慢。

如果连续切换后仍落到打不中基础目标的会话上，插件会放宽下一次的触发条件，而不是重复等价切换：每个“切换后窗口仍然慢于 `ttftThresholdMs` 或 `throughputThresholdTps`”的完整窗口都会让步进加一，使下一次判定多出 `stepTtftGraceMs`（默认 2 秒）的 TTFT 余量、少要求 `stepThroughputGraceTps`（默认 5 tok/s）的吞吐。切换后窗口达到基础目标，步进归零。失败永远按基础目标判定，不会按已经放宽后的目标判定。

插件本身不压缩任何内容，也不改动提示词或会话日志。它只改一个路由请求头，并在本地保存计时计数。

## 工作方式

- **实测缓存证据。** 它包装合格请求的 `llm/stream`，读取最后一个 `usage` 块。一次请求的缓存命中率是 `cacheReadTokens / (inputTokens + cacheReadTokens)`；新输入加缓存读取量就是上游实际计费的提示词长度。样本保存 TTFT、输出吞吐（token/秒）、提示词 token 数、缓存读取量和命中率；每个 DSH 会话使用最近 `sampleSize` 个有效样本。
- **折叠账本（仅作诊断，可选）。** 它同时读取 billion-context 的会话状态文件（`sessions/openai/<host>_<sha256(conversationId).slice(0,24)>.json`），跟踪 `metadata.cacheLedger.folds`。billion-context 的 `conversationId` 取自优先级最高的会话请求头，在 DSH 里是 `x-bili-plugin-conversation`（DSH 会话 id）；`x-opencode-session` 的优先级更低，所以轮换它不会改变文件名。最新的折叠只作为“刚才那次大冷请求是重建”的证据，不再直接触发轮换。插件不修改自身之外的任何文件：0.5.0 移除了 0.4.0 那个需要给 billion-context 打补丁的折叠前衔接。
- **适用范围。** 只处理来自已配置 provider（默认 `opencode-go`）且模型 id 以 `deepseek` 开头（大小写不敏感）的请求。`models` 可以收窄到具体的 DeepSeek id。其他模型被忽略；如果最近一次普通会话请求用的是不合格的模型，则跳过轮换。声明了 `purpose` 的辅助请求不会改变这一状态。
- **预测。** 在合格请求发出前，插件按以下顺序预测它的缓存命中：系统提示词变化或消息历史变短 → 0%；还没有任何实测请求 → 未知，绝不轮换；空闲达到 `cacheTtlMs`（默认 1 小时）→ 0%；上次命中 `>=` 80% → 沿用；上次请求完整 prefill 了大前缀（`>=` `prefillMinTokens` 且命中低）→ 按热处理（实测 95–99%），因为那次 prefill 已经把前缀写进缓存（即折叠重建的情形）；这是概率判断，不是保证——若那条请求实际仍冷，下一条会按 cache-miss-persists 判冷并轮换；其余情况沿用上次实测命中，命中 `<=` `cacheHitThresholdPct` 即判冷。
- **判定。** 只有在预测为冷、最近样本很慢（平均 TTFT `>=` 默认 12000 ms，或平均吞吐 `<=` 默认 60 token/秒，会按失败步进放宽）、最近一次普通请求合格、且 `minRotationGapMs` 已过时才轮换。记录里保留预测依据（`system-rewrite`、`history-compacted`、`idle-expired`、`cache-miss-persists` 等）和预期命中率。
- **路由。** 一个持久化的路由把 DSH 会话 id 映射到生成的 `ses_...` 值。`llm-pi-ai/request-headers` 瀑布流在 pi-ai 组装好请求头之后、请求发出之前执行，因此在那里设置 `x-opencode-session` 会真正上线，预测写入的路由也作用于同一条请求。在参考配置里，`dsh-opencode-ip-guard` 之类的配套注入器会提供等于 DSH 会话 id 的基线值；路由存在时本插件替换它，注入器的“不覆盖”回退则会保留新值。
- **没有 billion-context 也能工作。** 如果会话目录或会话状态文件不存在，折叠诊断保持空闲，设置页会明确说明。其余功能——实测缓存命中、TTFT/吞吐统计、池替换记录和轮换历史——都来自插件自身的请求采样，所以预测照常工作，不会把异常抛进 DSH，页面上的统计也不会消失。

会话的第一个请求没有实测样本，因此不会因预测而轮换；插件启动后看到的第一个折叠只作为诊断基线。轮换只改变上游路由 id，billion-context 仍为同一个 DSH 会话写同一个状态文件，所以监视器可以一直跟踪下去。

## 热路由 id 池

一个路由 id 绑定一个上游后端及其缓存。会话结束之后，这个 id 对前缀重叠的新会话仍然有价值。池就是为这种交接准备的。

**入池。** 会话连续 `poolIdleMs`（默认 3 分钟）没有产生有意义的事件，且没有进行中的回合、工具调用、确认或后台任务，宿主也报告 agent 空闲时，它的 code 进入池。改标题、写请求头、LLM 重试这类被动事件不会重置计时。会话被归档时立即入池。入池后不活跃超过 `poolExpireMs` 的 code 会被剔出池，之后不会再交给新会话；只要它仍然空闲，所属会话复苏时仍可收回。

**前缀摘要。** 每条合格请求发出前，插件为系统提示词、工具定义、消息文本、工具参数和工具结果生成摘要；只保存分块的 SHA-256，不保存原文。命中率等于共同的前缀块数除以新会话的块数。一级池的老 code 至少要覆盖新前缀的 `poolMatchPct`（默认 60%）；二级池没有命中率下限。

**两级池。** 一级池是不活跃时间小于 `poolTier1Ms`（默认 1 小时）的 code；二级池是 1–24 小时的 code。候选还必须满足：绑定该 code 的实测样本不少于 `poolSampleSize` 条、平均 TTFT 不超过 `poolMaxTtftMs`（8 秒）、平均吞吐高于 `poolMinTps`（80 tok/s）。一级候选按前缀命中率取最大（并列时取吞吐更高、TTFT 更低、最近更活跃者）。只有一级没有任何合格候选时才下落到二级，而且要求换入确实能提速：借出 code 的平均吞吐必须达到会话基线（会话自身已绑定样本不少于 `poolSpeedMinSamples` 时用它，否则取最近 200 条请求吞吐的中位数）的 `poolSpeedGainRatio` 倍（默认 1.1），两边的样本都不少于 `poolSpeedMinSamples`（5）；测不出基线时门槛放行。二级没有前缀命中率下限：只要通过样本与速度门槛，即使命中率更低也会优先于新生成 code。

**交换。** 新会话先新生成一个 code。若有合格候选，两者交换：新会话拿到老 code，连同它的摘要和绑定样本；老会话拿到新生成的 code，摘要与样本清空，并进入休眠，下次请求后空闲再重新入池。没有合格候选时，新会话保留自己的新 code。复苏不是借入：老会话只要自己的 code 还空闲，就一定拿回自己的 code，不参与 match、样本、层级或速度判定；如果 code 已经交给别的会话，就保留交换时得到的新 code，绝不改借其他 code。

只有已经生成前缀摘要、绑定样本不少于 `poolSampleSize`、平均 TTFT 与吞吐落在借出目标内（不超过 8 秒、高于 80 tok/s）、未过期且不在休眠的会话 code 才会入池；样本不足或实测偏慢的 code 会保持活跃，让所属会话继续使用。

**效果。** 池页面会把借入 code 后的首条请求与全新（`pool-initial`）会话的首条请求做对比。对比使用持久化的首请求标记；借入事件还会使用池事件里保存的首请求快照，所以即使首请求已经离开 200 条请求记录，仍按快照计入。早于快照机制、且首请求也已离开记录的借入事件，或首请求已离开记录的全新会话，会被跳过，而不会拿后面某条热请求顶替。页面显示借入/全新的样本数、首请求平均命中率、平均匹配率，以及以百分点表示的 `deltaPct`。0.6 之前创建、还没有摘要的旧路由会保持活跃，直到会话发出下一条请求。`poolMaxEntries` 限制池大小，超出时淘汰最久不活跃的 code；被淘汰的 code 在会话重新活跃前不会再次入池。

池开启时，会话的第一条合格请求就会创建持久化路由，即使当次不需要轮换。这个路由就是之后入池、交给别人的对象。把 `poolEnabled` 设为 `false` 可保留 0.6 之前的行为：只有发生轮换才创建路由，未轮换会话沿用宿主或配套注入器提供的请求头。

## 环境要求

- DSH 带 `llm-pi-ai` 适配器，并配置了 OpenCode Go provider（默认 `opencode-go`），其中至少有一个 DeepSeek 系列模型（模型 id 以 `deepseek` 开头）。
- billion-context 是可选的：安装并持续保存会话状态时，它的折叠账本会喂给折叠诊断；没有它，插件仍会测量每条请求、保留统计，并记录池替换与缓存命中。
- DSH 0.2.1-rc.5 或更新，且低于 0.3.0。
- Node.js 20 或更新。

## 从 npm 安装

```bash
dsh plugin add dsh-opencode-go-router --profile <profile>
```

也可以在 DSH 插件管理器的“添加插件”输入框里填 `dsh-opencode-go-router`。包内声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch`，正常安装会自己创建 `opencode-router` 行；不要为它再加一条独立的 profile 行。

## 从本地仓库安装（开发）

1. 把本仓库放在稳定位置，例如 `C:/Users/me/DSHs/opencode-router`。
2. 在 profile 的 `package.json` 里：
   - 把 `dsh-opencode-go-router` 加入 `dsh.profile.bundles`；
   - 把 `"dsh-opencode-go-router": "link:C:/Users/me/DSHs/opencode-router"` 加入 `dependencies`。
3. 让 profile 的 `node_modules/dsh-opencode-go-router` 指向本仓库（Windows 上目录联接/符号链接即可）。
4. **不要**在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里为这个插件加独立行。包内声明了 `dsh.bundle.patch: ./cordis.patch.yml`，会自己插入插件行。没有 `insert` 的 profile 行只是覆盖，无法创建行。
5. 重启 DSH。插件管理器里应出现 `dsh-opencode-go-router` 这个 profile bundle，带一行 `include:opencode-router`。如果声明 bundle 之前宿主已经在运行，需要通过插件管理器重新加载它，或重启 DSH。
6. 访问 `http://127.0.0.1:<DSH Web 端口>/opencode-router/status` 查看实时状态。

要改默认值，在 profile 的 `cordis.patch.yml` 里按行 id 覆盖：

```yaml
- id: opencode-router
  config:
    cacheHitThresholdPct: 25
```

插件的入口每次 `apply` 都会带缓存破坏参数重新加载 `lib/impl.js`，所以改实现后通常只要触碰一次插件配置就能试新代码。在运行中的宿主里，通过插件管理器把 profile bundle 关掉再打开，也会重新加载静态导入（`lib/core.js`、`lib/store.js`、`lib/monitor.js`）；0.1.2 -> 0.1.3 的阈值改动就是这样验证的。如果宿主一直报告旧版本号，就重启 DSH。

## 配置

| 键 | 默认值 | 含义 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `enabled` | `true` | 总开关。关闭时钩子直接放行，监视器不运行。 |
| `providers` | `["opencode-go"]` | 有资格被路由的 provider；模型仍必须是 `deepseek*` id。 |
| `models` | `[]` | 可选的精确 DeepSeek 模型白名单；为空表示该 provider 下任意 `deepseek*` 模型。 |
| `cacheHitThresholdPct` | `25` | 只有下一条请求的预测缓存命中率低于或等于此值才轮换。 |
| `predictiveRotation` | `true` | 预测下一条请求的缓存命中并在其发出前轮换。设为 false 则完全不做切换。 |
| `cacheTtlMs` | `3600000` | 空闲达到该值即预测为冷。实测显示 15–60 分钟仍会命中，所以默认取 1 小时；`0` 关闭空闲规则。 |
| `prefillMinTokens` | `4000` | 一次冷请求如果计费提示词不少于该值，就视为完整 prefill，下一条请求预测为热（属于假设；该请求实测若仍冷，会在再下一条纠正）。 |
| `ttftThresholdMs` | `12000` | 平均首内容 token 时间达到该值即视为慢（基础目标）。 |
| `throughputThresholdTps` | `60` | 平均输出吞吐低于或等于该值即视为慢（基础目标）。 |
| `stepTtftGraceMs` | `2000` | 每连续失败一次，下一次 TTFT 目标放宽这么多。 |
| `stepThroughputGraceTps` | `5` | 每连续失败一次，下一次吞吐目标降低这么多（下限 `0.01`）。 |
| `sampleSize` | `5` | 参与性能判定的最近请求数。 |
| `requireFullSamples` | `true` | 轮换前要求攒满 `sampleSize` 个样本。 |
| `routingIdPrefix` | `"ses_"` | 生成路由 id 的前缀。 |
| `statePath` | `$DSH_HOME/storages/opencode-router/state.json` | 持久化的路由与计时样本。 |
| `dryRun` | `false` | 只记录轮换，不真正选择新的请求头值。 |
| `debug` | `false` | 额外的 info 日志。 |
| `overrideExistingHeader` | `true` | 替换已存在的 `x-opencode-session`。设为 false 则保留原值。 |
| `pollIntervalMs` | `2000` | 会话活跃时的轮询间隔。 |
| `requestCheckDelaysMs` | `[400, 1500]` | 请求结束后额外的状态文件检查时间点。 |
| `biliSessionsDir` | `null` | 覆盖 billion-context 的会话根目录。 |
| `biliProtocol` | `"openai"` | 状态子目录。 |
| `biliUpstreamHost` | `"opencode.ai"` | 状态文件名里的 host 标签。 |
| `maxSamples` | `20` | 每个会话保留的最大样本数。 |
| `sessionActiveMs` | `600000` | 会话空闲超过该时长后停止轮询。 |
| `minRotationGapMs` | `0` | 同一会话两次轮换之间的最小间隔。 |
| `poolEnabled` | `true` | 启用热路由 id 池。 |
| `poolIdleMs` | `180000` | 无待办工作时，空闲多久后 code 入池。 |
| `poolMatchPct` | `60` | 一级池老 code 必须覆盖的前缀摘要命中率下限（二级池无下限）。 |
| `poolSpeedGainRatio` | `1.1` | 二级池借出 code 相对会话基线所需的最低吞吐倍数。 |
| `poolSpeedMinSamples` | `5` | 借出方与基线各自需要的绑定样本数，之后速度门槛才做判断。 |
| `poolMinTps` | `80` | 老 code 样本的平均吞吐下限（须严格高于）。 |
| `poolMaxTtftMs` | `8000` | 老 code 样本的平均 TTFT 上限（8 秒含边界）。 |
| `poolSampleSize` | `5` | code 成为候选前要求的绑定样本数。 |
| `poolTier1Ms` | `3600000` | 不活跃时间小于该值的 code 属于一级池。 |
| `poolExpireMs` | `86400000` | 不活跃超过该值就从池中剔除，之后不再交出。 |
| `poolMaxEntries` | `50` | 池中 code 上限；超出时先淘汰最久不活跃者。 |
| `poolDigestChunkChars` | `512` | 每个前缀摘要块的字符数。 |
| `poolDigestMaxChars` | `262144` | 参与摘要的前缀最大字符数。 |

## 状态路由

`GET /opencode-router/status` 返回 JSON，包含生效配置、持久化路由、池内容、轮换历史和每个会话的监视状态：

- `history` —— 最近的路由记录，最新的在前，含 `sessionId`、`at`、`reason`（`predicted-cold`、`pool-adopted` 或 `pool-donated`）、`basis`、`foldSeq`、`cacheHitPct`（预期命中率）、`step`、路由 `value`、切换前后 TTFT 与吞吐、样本进度，以及 `backfilled` 标记。新记录还带 `version` 与 `thresholds`（基础/生效 TTFT 与吞吐目标、失败步进）；池记录为 `thresholds: null`，并带 `poolMatchPct`、`poolTier`、`poolScore`、`poolSourceSessionId`、`poolRole` 和首请求标记 `firstRequestAt`；
- `routes` —— 持久化路由；前缀摘要脱敏为 `digestChunks`（块数），绑定样本概括为 `poolSamples`；
- `pool` —— `enabled`、`speedGainRatio`、`speedMinSamples`、各项上限、`total`、`tier1`、`tier2`、`eligible`、`lastAdoption`、`lastRevival`、`effect`（`adopted`/`baseline` 首请求命中汇总、`deltaPct` 与最近 `samples`），以及每个条目的 `sessionId`、`code`、`tier`、`eligible`、`samples`、`avgTtftMs`、`avgTps`、`score`、`digestChunks`、`digestChars`、`ageMs`、`pooledAt` 与 `lastActiveAt`；
- `activity` —— 每个会话的进行中回合、工具调用、确认、后台任务和最近活动时间；它们决定能否入池；
- `eligibility` —— 已配置的 provider 和固定的 `deepseek` 模型前缀；
- `baselineReady` 与 `lastFoldSeq` —— 折叠诊断的游标；
- `latestFold` —— 最新的折叠记录（含 `hPct`）；
- `watchingId` —— 正在跟踪的 billion-context 状态文件对应的 DSH 会话 id；
- `route` —— 当前轮换后的路由 id，或 `null`；其 `reason` 为 `predicted-cold`、`pool-adopted` 或 `pool-donated`，`basis` 为预测或池的依据，`step` 为当次切换使用的失败步进；
- `targetActive` —— 最近一次普通会话请求是否为合格的 OpenCode Go DeepSeek 请求；`false` 会阻止轮换；
- `lastPrediction` —— 最近一次请求前预测：依据、预期与上次命中率、是否判冷、空闲时长、样本数、性能摘要、步进、`rotated`，以及 `skipReason`（`predictive-rotation-off`、`cache-expected-warm`、`not-target`、`cooldown`、`performance-ok`、`pool-adopted`、`pool-revived`）；
- `predictions`、`predictiveRotation`、`cacheHitThresholdPct`、`cacheTtlMs` —— 已做预测次数与预测设置；
- `systemPromptFp`、`messageCount`、`lastSample` —— 预测用于比较的最新前缀输入；
- `stepping` —— `step`、`consecutiveFailures`、基础与生效的 TTFT/吞吐阈值，以及每步放宽量；
- `samples` —— 样本数、平均 TTFT、平均吞吐；
- `billionContext` —— `{ detected, root }`：billion-context 的会话目录是否存在（最多每 30 秒探测一次），以及探测的根目录；
- `statistics` —— 设置页标题栏用的请求汇总：`window.requests`、`window.poolEvents`、`requests.total/measured/avgHitPct/warm/cold/avgTtftMs/avgTps`，以及 `pool.swaps/revivals/lastSwapAt`；
- `requests` —— 最近 100 条实测请求，最新的在前：`sessionId`、`at`、命中率、TTFT、吞吐、输入与缓存读取 token 数；
- `poolEvents` —— 最近 100 条池替换与复苏记录，最新的在前：`role`（`adopted`/`revived`）、会话 id、code 与借出 code、命中率、层级、分数、借出方的 TTFT/吞吐/样本数，以及借入事件的 `firstRequest` 首请求快照（时间、命中率、TTFT、吞吐、输入与缓存读取 token）；
- `rotations`、`lastRequestAt`、`lastTickAt`、`lastError`；
- `routing` —— 请求头钩子的计数与最近一次判定：`checks`、`applications`、`lastCheckedAt`、`lastCheckedSessionId`、`lastAppliedAt`、`lastAppliedSessionId`、`lastAppliedValue`、`lastReason`。`lastReason` 取值 `applied`、`no-route`、`existing-header`、`no-headers`、`disabled`、`not-target`。

当宿主的 Web 服务器绑定在 localhost 时，该路由只在 localhost 可访问。请把这份 JSON 当作诊断信息。

## 设置页

在 DSH Web 客户端打开插件管理器，选择本 bundle。详情页会在 bundle 配置行上方显示 **静默切换性能记录**。

每条路由记录会显示时间、短会话 id、触发原因（`预测冷请求`、`系统提示词改写`、`池复用` 或 `池借出`）、预测依据与折叠编号、预期缓存命中率、失败步进（大于 0 时）、切换前的平均 TTFT 与吞吐、切换后前 `sampleSize` 个合格样本，以及百分比变化。池复用行没有自己的基线：其「切换前」一栏是借入 code 在来源会话的历史，因此百分比只表示同一 code 迁移后的漂移，不是复用收益；这类行不计入标题栏的平均变化，复用收益看上方「池效果」。每条记录还会标出写入时生效的阈值；没有记录阈值的旧版本行会标记为旧版记录，而不会拿今天的默认值去评判。标题栏显示池大小、两级数量、合格数、最近活跃会话的步进与生效阈值，面板里解释了每一步的放宽量。下方是「两级池 session code」列表，按一级/二级分组显示每个 code 的会话、code 原文、是否合格、TTFT、吞吐、样本进度、评分、空闲时长、摘要大小与入池时间；不合格条目会说明原因。记录每五秒从 `GET /opencode-router/status` 刷新一次。切换后窗口攒满 `sampleSize` 个样本后即冻结，之后的流量不会改写历史。

页面还会显示一行最近请求汇总（平均命中率、热/冷次数、平均 TTFT 与吞吐），并在记录下方显示两个日志：**池替换记录**（哪个 code 被复用/收回、来自哪个会话、命中率、层级、借出方速度）和**缓存命中记录**（只显示每次从池中复用 code 后的第一条请求；同一会话收回自己的 code 不算池替换，不显示；首请求快照随池事件持久化，200 条请求记录淘汰后仍可查看；每条显示命中率、TTFT、吞吐、提示词与缓存读取 token 数）。未检测到 billion-context 时，页面会提示折叠诊断不可用、统计来自插件自身采样，并隐藏折叠标记。

0.2.0 之前创建的路由会被回填为每个仍已知路由一行，并标记为 `Reconstructed`；它们的切换后数值来自该次轮换之后保留的样本。面板只存在于 Web 客户端，不影响宿主路由。

## 隐私与安全

- 保存的数据仅限 DSH 会话 id、生成的路由 id、折叠编号、缓存百分比、TTFT、吞吐、路由历史、逐请求缓存命中与池事件日志、时间戳，以及用于池匹配的分块 SHA-256 前缀哈希。不保存提示词、消息、工具输出或 API 密钥；摘要无法还原成原文。
- 每个宿主回调都自行捕获异常。未安装 billion-context 只会关闭折叠诊断；状态文件格式异常只会产生一条日志。
- 修改请求头只是路由提示，并不保证网关一定选中不同的物理后端。如果网关忽略未知或新的会话值，插件无法强制迁移。
- billion-context 的状态文件是内部格式。如果其布局变化，折叠诊断可能看不到折叠并保持空闲，插件不会破坏任何数据。

## 开发

```bash
node --test
```

测试覆盖折叠解析、缓存命中测量、预测规则与依据、性能判定与连续失败步进、仅 DeepSeek 的适用范围、状态持久化、轮换历史、请求与池事件日志、统计汇总、收紧后的入池门槛、监视器、请求头路由、流式测量、客户端 bundle 注册与两级池 code 列表、前缀摘要、两级池、池交换与复苏、首请求标记、首请求快照与池效果归因、空闲/归档入池，以及活动跟踪。

## 我的其他 DSH 项目

上下文路由只是 DSH 的一小块。下面这些插件也都由我维护，按需取用。

- **[dsh-sidebar-row-menu](https://github.com/TLEWA/dsh-sidebar-row-menu)** —— 侧栏行右键菜单：工作区行、会话行与会话正文各有自己的右键菜单，含「打开方式」「更多操作」二级菜单。
- **[dsh-sidebar-organizer](https://github.com/TLEWA/dsh-sidebar-organizer)** —— 七区域布局整理器：侧栏、侧栏底部、对话标签、输入框、会话头部、右侧栏、设置导航都能长按拖拽排序，面板可以收进「更多」再拖回来。
- **[dsh-better-choice](https://github.com/TLEWA/dsh-better-choice)** —— `ask_user_question` 增强：右键选项补备注，选之前先拿同一份上下文旁问模型一句。
- **[dsh-if](https://github.com/TLEWA/dsh-if)** —— `/if` 命令：让模型结合上文判断条件，成立才把下面的指令作为用户消息发出。
- **[dsh-utf8-output](https://github.com/TLEWA/dsh-utf8-output)** —— 修复 Windows 下 DSH 子进程 GBK/CP936/CP932 输出乱码。

## 许可证

MIT

# dsh-decision-trace

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that records the decisions an agent makes — as a card in the conversation and as a per-session timeline — **without adding a single session event type**.

```
 ●─ d-8   accepted  architecture              3 minutes ago
 │    One pure fold for ids and for the view
 │
 ●─ d-7   accepted  security                  18 minutes ago
      The status route exposes only the mode…
```

![The Decisions view: session tree with two agents, status and category filters, and the timeline where d-7 is dimmed and marked as replaced by d-8](docs/decisions.png)

## Why

An audit plugin that records without permission contradicts its own premise. This one is **off by default**: while it is off, it registers no tool and no prompt section, so it costs nothing per request. It stays visible anyway — the Decisions view exists in both states, so it is discoverable before it is enabled.

## What it does

- Registers one tool, `decision_record`, with eight fields: `title`, `category`, `rationale`, `alternatives[]`, `status`, `weight`, `supersedes`, `files[]`.
- Assigns the visible ids (`d-1`, `d-2`, …) by folding the session log, so a reload, a fork, or a replay reconstructs the same sequence.
- Shows each decision as a card where it was made, and as a timeline entry with relative time, status colour, and one-click evidence.
- Starts the timeline at the session's own beginning and interleaves the prompts that framed each decision, so the view reads as the session's story rather than a list with dates.
- Reports which agent the session belongs to — root or subagent, delegation depth, preset — read from the session header, so a delegated session is never anonymous.
- Lists the session tree with a decision count per agent, and opens any of them, so a delegated fleet is visible without leaving the view.
- Filters the timeline by status and category, and clusters supersession: a replaced decision dims and names the one that replaced it.
- Exports the session's decisions as Markdown from the Decisions view.

## Install

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/tlfnico/dsh-decision-trace.git
plugin_manager install_bundle <path to the clone>
```

Then enable it with a row in the profile's `cordis.patch.yml`:

```yaml
- id: dsh-decision-trace
  config:
    mode: "on"
```

Reload the page once: the browser half reads the mode when it loads. Nothing else is required.

## Config

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `"off"` | While off, neither the tool nor the system-prompt section is registered |
| `maxDecisions` | `200` | Hard cap on decisions recorded in one session |

The interface language follows the Harness locale; English is the source dictionary and Spanish ships beside it.

## The tool

```jsonc
{
  "title": "Assign ids by folding the log",   // required, ≤120 chars
  "category": "architecture",                 // architecture | dependency | data | api | security | process | other
  "rationale": "A projection unit would need…", // required
  "alternatives": [{ "option": "…", "rejected_because": "…" }],
  "status": "accepted",                       // proposed | accepted | rejected | superseded
  "weight": "major",                          // major moved the course; minor refines an earlier decision
  "supersedes": "d-3",                        // visible id of an earlier decision
  "files": ["src/index.ts"]
}
```

It returns `{ "id", "title", "status" }` — bounded on purpose. Everything the interface needs that the model does not (the full record, and the raw reference to the decision it replaces) travels in the result's presentation meta, which is part of the session log like any other tool result. Resolving that reference against earlier decisions is the fold's job, not the meta's.

Rules worth knowing:

- **Ids are assigned, never chosen.** The next id is the highest recorded id plus one, so a rejected record takes no number and leaves no gap.
- **`supersedes` is not a blocker.** An id that does not resolve is recorded anyway and shown as orphaned in the view.
- **Minor decisions are first-class.** `weight: minor` keeps a small choice in the record without letting it compete with the ones that moved the course; the view dims it and counts it separately. The prompt section asks for product and interface choices too, not only architecture — a gap in the record is worse than a late entry.
- **Calls are serialized.** Two records folding the same log at once would compute the same id.

## Guarantees

- **Zero new event types.** The plugin never appends to the session log; it only reads `tool/call` and `tool/result`. Uninstalling it leaves every session intact and readable.
- **The log is the only source of truth.** There is no plugin storage. The Decisions view and the Markdown export both derive from the same fold the tool uses to pick ids.
- **Replay is stable.** The fold is pure: no clock, no module state, no random. The same log produces the same timeline and the same meta.

### The two routes, and what they do not carry

The browser half cannot read the row config or the log, so the host serves two exact paths:

| Route | Answers |
|---|---|
| `GET /decision-trace/status` | `{plugin, mode}` — which state the plugin is in |
| `GET /decision-trace/agents?session=<id>` | the session tree: ids, delegation depth, preset, and two counts |

Neither carries session content — no titles, no rationale, no messages — and the shipped Web composition binds to loopback. Everything a reader actually sees comes from the session projection, which the client reads through the platform's authenticated session transport. A decision to keep those routes content-free is recorded in the plugin's own log (see `d-6` and `d-9` in the demo session).

## How it is put together

| Piece | Role |
|---|---|
| `fold.js` | The whole decision model, as one pure fold with no imports: ids, supersession, evidence, agent context |
| `index.js` | Tool, prompt section, session projection, the two routes |
| `client.js` | Inline card, Decisions view (timeline + list + detail + filters), fleet table, Markdown export, `en`/`es` dictionaries |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | One row, `config: {}` — off by default |
| `test/fold.test.js` | 22 cases over the fold's rules |
| `test/client.render.test.js` | 3 cases that execute the view with a fake React and a fake module loader — no browser, no dependencies |

Three seams, no more:

1. `tools` — `decision_record` and its presentation callbacks.
2. `systemPrompt` — a short section on *when* to record, mounted only with `mode: on`.
3. `conversation.view` + `tool.call.toolview` — the two surfaces the scope allows.

The session projection (`decisionTrace`) publishes the same fold as a client-visible view; the browser half never reads session events itself.

Because the browser half is built from the client graph and does not receive the row config, the mode reaches it through one exact route, `GET /decision-trace/status`, which answers in both states and exposes nothing but the mode.

## Development

No build step and no dependencies of its own — two peers, resolved from the Harness installation.

```powershell
node --test          # 25 cases: the fold and the view's render
node --check index.js fold.js client.js
```

`node --test` needs nothing installed: `fold.js` has no imports, which is why the model can be tested without a Harness, and the render test runs the view against a fake React. CI runs the same two commands on every push.

## Limits of v0.1

- No automatic detection of decisions — that is the next milestone and the one that needs inference.
- The fleet table shows the tree and per-agent counts; it does not merge other agents' timelines into one list.
- No editing from the interface, no comparison between sessions.
- A child whose agent already finished is listed with unknown counts, because its session is no longer live.
- No diffs: the card references the tool that changed a file instead of duplicating its diff.

## License

MIT.

# dsh-resume

This folder is a frozen snapshot of the files the compatibility sample audits.
Its `engines.dsh` range is the real one from `L3n3L/dsh-resume@0.1.3`:

## Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness `>=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0`

```json
"engines": {
  "dsh": ">=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0"
}
```

The heading is here on purpose: the sample isolates the host-range verdict, and
the remote audit still checks README requirements. Upstream's localized README
does not use a `## Requirements` heading, so a live audit of the repository can
also add a `readme` failure to the same row.

## The panel

![The Plugin doctor tab, on a plugin that fails two checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/panel.png)

The same checks, in the right sidebar: type a folder, an `owner/repo`, or a GitHub link, and it says which one would fail and why. Nothing is installed and nothing is written.

## Three paths

| You are… | Start with | Then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| writing your first plugin | [`init`](#1-write-a-plugin) | `doctor`, `fix`, `verify` |
| changing a panel that is already installed | [`dev`](#2-develop-a-panel) | `mount`, the testkit, `audit` |
| shipping a version | [`verify`](#3-ship-a-version) | `release`, `index` |

It also installs as a plugin. `dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-toolkit` puts a
**插件体检 / Plugin doctor** panel under the conversation and a tab in the right
sidebar. Give it a folder that holds a plugin's `package.json`, or just
`owner/repo` — or a repository name, which it searches GitHub for and lists the
candidates to pick from. It then runs the same checks `verify` runs and says
which one would break the install, with the reason on the line — the same
answers as the CLI, without leaving the app.

```
$ dsh plugin add dsh-plugin-toolkit
```

### 1. Write a plugin

[`init`](#start-from-a-plugin-that-already-passes) writes the files whose absence shows up as a failed first publish — `engines.dsh`, the patch file, a `files` list that ships the code, a client bundle, a test for it, and the CI that runs both. `doctor` then checks the same things without writing anything, and [`verify`](#prove-the-tarball-works-not-just-the-repository) checks the tarball instead of the working copy.

If a plugin already exists, `doctor --fix` turns the failing checks into a
repair plan. It names the file and the edit for every problem, writes nothing
until you add `--write`, and then runs the checks again. `fix --engines` is
still there when the host range is the only thing you need to change.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest init ./my-panel --name my-panel
cd my-panel && npm install && npm test && npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest doctor .
```

### 2. Develop a panel

A plugin's client code is one file that calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({factory})` — there is no module to import, so the usual React test setup does not apply. [`testkit`](#test-a-panel-without-a-browser) supplies the missing half, and [`dev`](#edit-a-plugin-that-is-already-installed) pushes a rebuilt bundle into the running app.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest mount ./client.js     # what a user would see, without the app
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

### 3. Ship a version

`verify` first (it is the only check that reads the tarball), then `release`, which tags, waits for the registry, writes the index entry with the publish time the registry reports, and — with `--pr --merge` — opens and merges the pull request.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest verify .
npx dsh-plugin-toolkit@latest release . --pr --merge
```

## What `verify` actually does

![Five steps, and the failure each one catches](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/main/docs/pipeline.svg)

The order matters. Packing first means the check reads the file list npm will publish, not the folder you have. Installing the tarball means the root is imported by its bare specifier — the package name the loader uses — not by a file path taken from `main` or `exports["."]`. Node ignores `main` once `exports` exists, so a package whose `exports` map has no `"."` entry fails with `ERR_PACKAGE_PATH_NOT_EXPORTED` at that step even though the file is present. Mounting means the client bundle is actually executed, in jsdom, with a host that records what it registered.

Each step exists because a plugin once got past the step before it and still installed into nothing.

## Why this exists

Releasing one plugin fifteen times taught me three things the ecosystem's tooling does not cover:

1. **A version is not shipped when npm accepts it.** Registry propagation took two to eight minutes every time. `npm view` answered from a stale local cache, so I repeatedly believed a release had failed when it had not — and once believed it had succeeded when the market still could not see it.
2. **The market index is a second release, done by hand.** Each version needs an entry carrying `publishTimestamp` from the registry and `engines.dsh` from the manifest. Forget the range and the index validator rejects the PR with `Engines mismatch` — after the tag is already public.
3. **Reading a manifest is not the same as checking it.** A plugin can have a valid `package.json` and still be uninstallable: `files` that omit the entry the manifest points at, a bundle patch that does not exist, a README that never states the host range it declares.

The five failures behind these checks — a red dot with no panel, a row the host drops, an app that disables every plugin after one unguarded `apply()`, a tab nothing can open, and a checker that was wrong — are written up with their exact error text and how to reproduce each one: [Five plugins that installed and did nothing](https://github.com/WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit/blob/main/docs/why-it-exists.md).

### Four ways a plugin installs and still does nothing

Each of these shipped in a real version of this toolkit before the check below existed. A manifest check passes on all four.

| What you see | What it was | Caught by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| The tab is a red dot and the panel never opens | `exports["."]` pointed at the CLI, so the loader's row had no plugin to apply | `root export` |
| The plugin is installed, the app never serves it | `dsh.client` declared, `exports["./client"]` missing — the host drops the row | `client declaration` |
| The app says the third-party plugin is unsupported and disables all of them | `apply()` read `ctx.webServer` without declaring it; cordis throws instead of returning `undefined` | `verify` (calls `apply` on a context that has no services) |
| The tab registers, and nothing in the UI opens it | `sidebarRightTabs.register()` registers a *type*; the sidebar lists what `tabs.guide()` returns | a testkit test, not `doctor` |

The first three are static: `doctor` and `verify` catch them without the app running. The fourth is a UI contract, so it needs the panel mounted and the registration inspected — that is what [`testkit`](#test-a-panel-without-a-browser) is for.

## Test a panel without a browser

A plugin's client code is one file that calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({factory})` — there is no module to import, so the usual React test setup does not apply. `testkit` supplies the missing half: a DOM, the real React, and a host context that records what the panel registers.

```sh
npm install --save-dev jsdom react react-dom
```

```js
import { mountClient, createFetch } from 'dsh-plugin-toolkit/testkit';

const panel = await mountClient({
  file: 'client.js',
  copy: { 'my-plugin': { title: 'My panel' } },
  fetch: createFetch({
    '/my-plugin/report': { body: { score: 71, noise: 3 } },
    '/my-plugin/apply': () => ({ status: 201, body: { score: 92 } }),
  }),
});

await panel.click('[data-testid="optimize"]');
console.assert(panel.text().includes('92'), 'the score on screen did not move');
console.assert(panel.must('[role="status"]').textContent.includes('92'));
await panel.unmount();
```

`unmount()` is async: it lets React finish the work its own unmount schedules before the DOM goes away. Skipping the `await` surfaces as `ReferenceError: window is not defined` *after* the test has already passed, which is a confusing way to learn it.

What you get back: `text()`, `html()`, `query(selector)`, `must(selector)` (throws with the rendered HTML when it misses), `click(selector)`, `type(selector, value)`, `press(selector, key)`, `focus`, `attributes(selector)`, `snapshot(dir, name)` for a normalised DOM baseline, and `host` for assertions about what the bundle registered.

### Keep a visual baseline

The DOM is the baseline: normalising class order and whitespace gives a file that fails for the reasons a screenshot would — a lost label, a control that stopped rendering — and can be reviewed in a diff instead of by eye.

```js
import { expectSnapshot } from 'dsh-plugin-toolkit/testkit';

const panel = await mountClient({ file: 'client.js' });
expectSnapshot(panel.html(), '__snapshots__', 'panel');   // throws with the element that moved
await panel.unmount();
```

First run writes nothing: it tells you to re-run with `UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1`, so a baseline is always a decision, never a side effect. That rerun writes the normalised HTML and returns `{ status: 'written' }`; later runs return `same` or fail with the element that moved.

### Check what assistive tech sees

```js
panel.expectAria('[role="tab"][aria-selected="true"]', { label: 'Protection', selected: 'true' });
assert.match(panel.must('[role="status"]').textContent, /Score moved 71 → 77/);
```

`expectAria()` compares the attributes a screen reader actually reads — `role`,
`label`, `live`, `selected`, `expanded`, `checked`, `pressed`, `disabled` — and
names the one that differs:

```
[aria-live="polite"]: expected aria text to be "9", but it is "0"
```

A missing attribute is reported as `nothing`, not as an empty string, because
those are different bugs. `panel.aria(selector)` returns the same object when you
want to assert on it yourself.

`must()` throws with the rendered markup when the selector misses, which is the difference between "the assertion failed" and "here is what the user actually got".

## See what is installed, and what the app loaded

`doctor` checks one folder you name. The question that actually gets asked is
"why is my plugin not in the sidebar?", and the answer needs three things at once:
what is installed, whether each installed copy is valid, and which of them the
running app actually loaded.

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
dsh-aiignore           0.37.1    loaded       ok
demo-panel             0.3.0     not loaded   ok  — dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json does not list it, and the loader mounts only listed bundles
                                            fix: add "demo-panel" to dsh.profile.bundles in /Users/me/.dsh/profiles/desktop/package.json (or run `dsh plugin add demo-panel`), then restart the app

1 installed plugin(s) are not in the running app:
```

"Not loaded" has three different causes, and `audit` names the one that applies
instead of offering a blanket restart:

- **Not in `dsh.profile.bundles`.** `pnpm add` (or `npm install`) installs the
  package but does not tell the loader to mount it. Add the package name to
  `dsh.profile.bundles` in `~/.dsh/profiles/<profile>/package.json`, or run
  `dsh plugin add <name>`, then restart the app.
- **No `dsh.bundle`.** The package declares `dsh` but no patch file to mount.
  Add `dsh.bundle.patch` to its `package.json` and ship the patch file, then
  reinstall.
- **Listed, but the app predates the install.** The profile is already correct;
  restart the app once to read the new list.

Advisories (`engines.dsh`, README Requirements) are counted apart from problems:
the market index needs them, the loader does not, so they should not bury a plugin
that is actually broken.

`audit` exits `1` when an installed plugin has a hard failure **or** when the
running app did not load at least one installed plugin, so CI can gate on a
profile where the app silently skipped a plugin. It exits `0` when every
installed plugin is loaded and valid. If no graph was read (`--host` omitted),
the loaded column is `?` and only hard failures change the exit code.

Without `--host` the loaded column is `?`, because guessing would be worse than
saying nothing. Only packages that declare a `dsh` field are audited — the rest of
`node_modules` is ordinary dependencies, and auditing those is noise.

An installed package whose `package.json` cannot be read is the exception: the
`dsh` field that would mark it as a plugin is in the file that failed to parse.
If its name is still in `dsh.profile.bundles`, `audit` reports a `manifest`
failure naming the unreadable `package.json` and exits `1` instead of treating
the folder as an ordinary dependency. A truncated manifest from an interrupted
install therefore cannot make the plugin disappear from the report, and a valid
sibling plugin is still listed on the same run. The exception stays narrow: a
damaged `package.json` in a package that is neither in `dsh.profile.bundles` nor
readable enough to expose a `dsh` field is still an ordinary dependency and is
skipped, so one broken transitive install does not fail every audit.

A declared bundle can also be missing entirely. If a name stays in
`dsh.profile.bundles` after its `node_modules/<name>` folder is removed (an
interrupted install, or a package deleted by hand), `audit` prints a `missing`
row with an `install` failure naming the absent folder and exits `1`, while
still listing the healthy plugins on the same run. An absent package that the
profile never declared is not an install record, so it is not invented in the
report; a regression test removes the name from the profile and requires the
shipped CLI to exit `0` without printing it.

## Edit a plugin that is already installed

The host already swaps a rebuilt bundle without a page reload: it watches each plugin's entry artifact and reports a `rebuilt` frame on `/plugins/events`. `dev` puts the new file where the host is looking, then **proves** the frame arrived instead of asking you to check by eye.

```sh
npx dsh-plugin dev . --host http://127.0.0.1:54133
```

![dsh-plugin dev printing the revision the app reported](docs/dev.gif)

*Recorded from a real run against the running app: the last line is the revision the app sent back on `/plugins/events`, not a message the tool printed on faith.*

```
demo-aiignore: /work/plugin/client.js -> ~/.dsh/profiles/desktop/node_modules/dsh-aiignore/client.js
initial: copied 163647 bytes at 1:18:43 AM
reloaded dsh-aiignore (rev e0c0230c4fc9)
watching /work/plugin
```

That last line is the whole point: the revision came back from the app's own event stream, so "it reloaded" is a fact, not a hope.

A plugin the running app never loaded cannot be reloaded, and the app says so by leaving it out of the graph it sends first. `dev` reads that graph, so a freshly installed plugin gets the sentence that fixes it instead of a timeout:

```
copied, but not confirmed: the running app has not loaded demo-panel, so it will not report a reload; restart the app once after installing it
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `--dest <dir>` | write into this installed copy instead of searching `~/.dsh/profiles/*/node_modules/<name>` |
| `--entry <file>` | copy this file instead of `dsh.client.entry`, `client.js`, `lib/client.js` |
| `--build <command>` | run this before each copy (a failed build copies nothing) |
| `--host <url>` | confirm the reload against the app at this URL; without it the copy still happens and the tool says it is unconfirmed |
| `--once` | copy once and exit, for scripts |

Two things it does not do, because the host does not: React state inside the reloaded plugin is lost, and a failed swap does not roll back to the previous bundle.

## Use it in CI

The same checks run as a GitHub Action, so a tag cannot go out on a plugin that would not install:

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@v4
- uses: WJDdidi-1/dsh-plugin-toolkit@v1
  with:
    dir: plugin        # the folder holding the plugin's package.json
    command: verify    # pack it, install the tarball, mount the panel
```

`verify` is the default because it is the only check that reads what a user
actually installs: `doctor` reads the working copy, so a `files` list that
forgets `client.js` passes it and fails only after `npm i`.

`command: doctor` stops at the manifest checks (fast, no install), and
`command: index` audits `market/index.json` instead, failing on any version whose
`engines.dsh` is missing or is not a semver range (a malformed value such as
`>=banana`, or a single pinned version such as `0.2.0`, both fail). Pin
`version:` if you would rather not track the latest release.

## Check a plugin you have not cloned

The panel takes three kinds of input: a folder, `owner/repo`, or a GitHub URL.
A bare name is a search, not a guess — it asks GitHub, lists the matches with
their stars, and checks the one you pick. A repository is downloaded once as a
tarball into a temp folder, so nothing is cloned into your workspace and
nothing is installed.

The CLI reads a repository straight from the GitHub API:

```bash
dsh-plugin doctor --remote V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
```

```text
dsh-plugin doctor: 1 problem(s) in V1ki/dsh-plugin-subscriptions
  ⨯ engines.dsh: engines.dsh is missing, so a host that enforces the range rejects the install as "incompatible with dsh"; declare the range you support, e.g. "engines": { "dsh": ">=0.2.0" }
```

That is the whole reason this mode exists: the plugin hub files failed installs
back into plugin repositories, and the report is a sentence — `plugin install
failed`, `plugin does not support the DSH version in use` — that never names a
file. Reading `package.json` over the API is enough to name it.

What it can see, and what it cannot:

- Manifest checks (`engines.dsh`, `dsh field`, `files`, `dsh.client`,
  `exports`) run on the real `package.json`.
- README checks (`readme`) run on the text GitHub serves: the README must have
  a `Requirements` heading and must state the host range `package.json`
  declares. A repository whose checkout fails `readme` fails the remote check
  too, with the same sentence.
- File checks (does `exports["./client"]` point at a file that exists, does the
  root export `apply`) need the tree. A package that runs `prepack`,
  `prepublishOnly`, `prepare` or `build` publishes files it does not commit, so
  those checks are **skipped with a note** instead of calling a working plugin
  broken.
- Public repositories work anonymously, but GitHub allows 60 requests an hour.
  Export `GH_TOKEN` (or `GITHUB_TOKEN`) to audit more than one or two.

To check a whole list in one pass, put one `owner/repo` per line in a file and
pass it with `--from` (`-` reads standard input):

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt
```

Repositories are read four at a time by default. `--jobs N` changes that width;
values above `8` are capped at `8`, and `--jobs 1` walks the list one repository
at a time, the timing the command had before batching. The output — and the
`--json` array — still follows the input list, and every verdict is the one the
sequential run produced, so a diff between two runs compares repositories rather
than scheduling.

When GitHub answers `403` or `429`, the shared quota is gone, so the batch stops
starting new repositories and marks every entry it could not read as
`rate-limited` instead of `clean` or `unreadable`. If the response carries
`x-ratelimit-reset` (or `retry-after`), the reset time is printed with the
verdict, and the remaining entries are reported without another request.

### Will this plugin install on my DSH?

The eight compatibility reports, from four repositories, all end with the same
question. Add `--host <version>` to a remote audit and it answers that question
for one repository. This is the output for `L3n3L/dsh-resume`, a real plugin
whose declared range stops before DSH 0.2.0, checked against the
`0.2.2-alpha.3` canary from the reports. The checked-in sample is a frozen 0.1.3
snapshot, so the line stays true as the upstream repository changes:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote L3n3L/dsh-resume --host 0.2.2-alpha.3
incompatible  L3n3L/dsh-resume  0.1.3 (host >=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0) [incompatible with dsh 0.2.2-alpha.3; declares ">=0.1.0-rc.6 <0.2.0-0"]

summary: 1 repository — 0 clean, 1 failing (1 problem), 0 unreadable, 0 rate-limited
```

The verdict comes first: `incompatible` means the range in `package.json` does
not accept the host, so the installer rejects the plugin before it unpacks it.
This run exits `1`. The same answer is reproducible without a GitHub request:
the checked-in snapshot under `examples/compatibility-sample/` keeps the 0.1.3
manifest fields that decide compatibility, and its `## Requirements` heading
isolates the host-range answer. This command feeds that snapshot through the
real CLI path:

```sh
$ node scripts/compatibility-sample.mjs
```

(`npm run compatibility` runs the same script.) The test suite runs that
command and compares its output with the block above, so the sample cannot
drift from the formatter or from the README. Running
`dsh-plugin audit --remote L3n3L/dsh-resume --host 0.2.2-alpha.3` without the
sample audits the repository's current default branch instead; a README or
manifest change since 0.1.3 can add another `readme` or manifest failure to the
same row.

The line carries the range `package.json` declares and one of `compatible`,
`incompatible`, or `unknown` against that host version. `unknown` is the honest
answer for a missing or malformed range — there is nothing to compare — while a
range that excludes the host is `incompatible`, counted as failing, and exits
`1`. npm's pre-release rule is part of the answer: `>=0.2.0` does not accept
`0.2.2-alpha.3`, because a range only opts into a pre-release when it names one
of the same `major.minor.patch`. A canary host can therefore be `incompatible`
with a range that will accept the final release. The same flag works in the
batch mode, so one `--from` run answers the whole list:

```sh
$ dsh-plugin audit --remote --from repos.txt --host 0.2.2-alpha.3
```

The compatibility flags are `--remote <owner/repo>` for one repository,
`--from <file>` for a list (`-` reads standard input), `--host <version>` for
the DSH version to compare against, and `--json` for the machine-readable
finding. `--jobs <n>` sets the batch width, and `--patch-dir <dir>` writes the
host-targeted repair for each repository that needs one. The help text lists
the same flags; a test fails if this section names a flag the CLI does not have.

`--host` still names the running app URL for a local `audit`; on `--remote` it
is the DSH version to compare against. With `--json`, each finding gains
`host` and `compatibility` beside `hostRange`.

Each repository gets one line with its verdict — `clean`, `failing`,
`unreadable`, or `rate-limited` — and the run ends with a counted summary:

```text
clean         demo/plugin  1.2.3 (host >=0.2.0)
failing       demo/broken  — engines.dsh: engines.dsh is missing, so a host that enforces the range rejects the install as "incompatible with dsh"
rate-limited  demo/blocked — GitHub rate-limited this request (403) for package.json; set GH_TOKEN or GITHUB_TOKEN to raise the limit; the limit resets at 2026-11-04T20:00:00.000Z
rate-limited  demo/next    — GitHub rate-limited the batch before this repository was read, so it was not requested; the limit resets at 2026-11-04T20:00:00.000Z

summary: 4 repositories — 1 clean, 1 failing (1 problem), 0 unreadable, 2 rate-limited
```

The parenthesised count is the number of failed checks, not the number of failing
repositories: one repository that fails both `engines.dsh` and its client
declaration prints `1 failing (2 problems)`. A repository whose `package.json`
has an empty `dsh` field and no `dsh.bundle.patch` is `failing` here too: the
batch runs the same `dsh field` check as `doctor`, and the `--json` finding
carries that failure even though no patch path was declared to check. A README
with no `Requirements` heading is treated the same way: the batch asks the same
`readme` question as a checkout, so the row is `failing`, the `--json` finding
